result.label: F04: CLV Unification
result.summary: Read-only audit of the six CLV-touching files confirms and sharpens tonight's finding: nfl-clv.js, nfl-execution-clv.js, nfl-execution-clv-downsize.js, nfl-prop-clv.js, forward-ledger.js and shadow-ledger.js each compute CLV differently — different tables, different sign conventions, points-space vs probability-space, and (newly found) nfl-execution-clv.js's DEFAULT_CLOSING_BOOKS=null never excludes the execution book from its own reference close, while shadow-ledger.js grades against the live, mutable game_lines.spread column instead of the frozen closing_spread that forward-ledger.js correctly prefers — a live instance of the "fixed grading period" defect. Four practitioner/academic sources read in full converge on the same canonical design: (1) Hubáček & Šír (arXiv:2010.12508) prove and empirically demonstrate (9,093 football games, 2006-2014) that a forecast's profitability depends on its *decorrelation* from the market, not its accuracy — directly explaining why Gridiron's nfl-ensemble.js market_residual blend (a market + shrunk-slope estimator, forecast≈0.68+0.632·market) is architecturally profit-suppressing regardless of skill; (2) Bailey et al.'s backtest-overfitting / deflated-Sharpe framework shows why the 21-model historical search needs multiplicity correction before promotion; (3) Buchdahl's CLV methodology piece and (4) Outlier.bet's devig-method comparison establish that CLV must be computed in de-vigged probability space against one declared, versioned reference book, with devig-method choice as part of the definition, not a bolt-on. nfl-devig.js's own history (five duplicated proportional-devig reimplementations consolidated into one shinNoVig function) is the existence proof that this consolidation pattern already works in this codebase. Recommends one canonical computeClv() module replacing all six current call sites, plus three new-capability candidates (decorrelation-aware ensemble loss, a real devig-method bake-off using the underused 12.4M-row Polymarket tape, and a PBO/deflated-Sharpe trial registry) that Gridiron has none of today.

sources.title: Beating the market with a bad predictive model
sources.authors: Ondřej Hubáček, Gustav Šír (Czech Technical University in Prague)
sources.sample: 9,093 real football (soccer) matches, seasons 2006-2014, expanding training window from 2000-2005; plus a 10,000-round x 30-bet simulated-data appendix
sources.key_result: A decorrelation-augmented loss (MSE minus γ times covariance with the bookmaker's own price) turns a model with WORSE prediction accuracy (67.6%→66.2% as γ rises) into one with statistically significant POSITIVE returns under both uniform-stake and Sharpe-optimal strategies (Table 3); feeding the market's own odds in as a model feature raises the model-market Pearson correlation from 0.87 to 0.95 and correspondingly destroys profitability at every γ. Theorem 4.1 proves essential profitability is maximized as partial correlation with the market approaches -1 and is exactly zero when the model equals the market. Authors' own limitation: the correlation-based loss is an admitted proxy, not derived from the actual investment utility, and demonstrated only on one sport/architecture.

sources.title: Statistical Overfitting and Backtest Performance
sources.authors: David H. Bailey, Stephanie Ger, Marcos López de Prado, Alexander Sim, Kesheng Wu
sources.venue: SSRN / Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory technical report (companion: Bailey & López de Prado, 'The Deflated Sharpe Ratio,' SSRN 2460551)
sources.sample: An online simulator applied to random-walk time series with exhaustive integer-parameter search, plus a worked null-skill example (10,240 = 10×2^10 recipients, halved each round, yielding 10 'correct' predictions in a row from pure selection)
sources.key_result: An 'optimal' strategy selected by exhaustively searching parameters on one random-walk series performs no better than chance on a second, independent random-walk series -- demonstrating that in-sample optimality from a large, uncounted number of trials is not evidence of skill. The companion Deflated Sharpe Ratio formalizes the correction using the number of independent trials N plus the return distribution's skewness/kurtosis. Limitation: the demonstration is a worst-case illustration (zero true skill), and applying PBO/DSR retroactively requires an honest, auditable count of trials actually run -- exactly the gap in Gridiron's un-preregistered 21-model search.

sources.title: Closing Line Value (CLV) demystified by expert Joseph Buchdahl
sources.sample: A cited real 20,000-bet betting record used as validation
sources.key_result: CLV should be computed as odds-taken/closing-odds in DE-VIGGED probability terms, using ONE declared reference book (Pinnacle, chosen for its sharp-accepting business model) rather than a tape-wide consensus; the equal-margin devig is explicitly called 'crude and frankly inaccurate' -- devig-method choice is part of the CLV definition itself. On the 20,000-bet record, CLV-implied EV (4.0%) matched realized profit (3.4%) closely, and because CLV's bet-to-bet variance (~0.1 SD) is far smaller than win/loss variance (~1.0 SD), significance needs as few as ~50 bets versus thousands for raw win rate.

sources.title: How to Devig Odds — Comparing the Methods
sources.sample: Qualitative comparison, no original dataset
sources.key_result: Lays out five real devig alternatives (multiplicative/proportional, additive, power, probit, Shin) with the specific bias each does or doesn't correct: multiplicative ignores favorite-longshot bias entirely; additive can push underdog probabilities negative; probit suits symmetric two-way markets but not skewed moneylines; Shin generalizes correctly to n-way markets where additive does not. The article's own stated limitation: even this reference has 'no definitive empirical ranking' -- it names methods and assumptions but never runs a real-market comparison, which is the exact gap candidate N2 proposes to close using Gridiron's own underused 12.4M-row Polymarket tape.

sources.title: Sports Betting Market Efficiency and the Role of the Closing Line
sources.venue: Blog synthesis of a 2024 Management Science sportsbook-efficiency study
sources.sample: Synthesis piece, not original data
sources.key_result: Defines the close as 'the last widely visible price before uncertainty turns into result,' notes closing-line sharpness varies by market liquidity (spreads/totals sharpen fastest, props/niche leagues stay softer longer -- consistent with props being Gridiron's one area of measured skill), and warns that short-run win/loss records are not evidence of process quality; notably does NOT itself specify book-exclusion or timing-window mechanics precisely, reinforcing why Gridiron must make and version its own explicit choice rather than rely on an implicit external convention.

candidates.candidate: Build one canonical computeClv() module (server/services/nfl-clv-core.js) and make nfl-clv.js, nfl-execution-clv.js, nfl-execution-clv-downsize.js, nfl-prop-clv.js, forward-ledger.js, and shadow-ledger.js thin adapters over it
candidates.fixes_finding: Five independent, disagreeing CLV (closing-line-value) implementations exist over four different tables with different math and sign conventions
candidates.mechanism: Extract one function taking {eventKey, market, side, line, price, kickoff, executionBook, referenceBooks, gradingPeriod, space} and returning {clv, clv_price_space, reference_close, books_used, reason, grading_version}. Probability-space CLV (using the already-centralized shinNoVig from nfl-devig.js) becomes the primary metric everywhere; price-space stays as a secondary diagnostic. This mirrors the exact consolidation nfl-devig.js already performed for de-vigging (its header names five prior duplicated implementations it replaced), so the pattern is proven in this codebase already.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Replace inline math at forward-ledger.js:159-176 and shadow-ledger.js:77-91 with calls to the shared function; nfl-execution-clv.js keeps its CLV_GRADING_VERSION pattern (line 48) but every consumer now stamps it; nfl-clv.js's closingConsensus() (lines 94-113) and nfl-execution-clv.js's closingQuoteForContract() (lines 98-150) collapse into one reference-close resolver.
candidates.expected_value: Every downstream reader (Model Room, promotion gates, the coverage report) gets one number that means the same thing everywhere, instead of five that silently disagree; eliminates a whole class of 'which CLV do you mean' bugs before any governance gate can trust CLV as a promotion signal.
candidates.exit_test: Run all six current call sites' existing test fixtures (test/forward-ledger.test.js, test/nfl-execution-clv.test.js, test/nfl-execution-clv-downsize.test.js, test/prop-clv-free-capture.test.js) against the new shared function and confirm every previously-graded bet in nfl_bet_log, nfl_execution_opportunities, forward_picks, and shadow_decisions reproduces the same Won/Lost/Push result (grading-INVARIANT check) while clv_points/clv fields now agree in sign and units across tables for the same underlying game.

candidates.candidate: Declare a real reference-book set that excludes the execution book, replacing DEFAULT_CLOSING_BOOKS = null
candidates.fixes_finding: Five independent, disagreeing CLV (closing-line-value) implementations exist over four different tables with different math and sign conventions
candidates.mechanism: nfl-execution-clv.js line 59 sets DEFAULT_CLOSING_BOOKS = null, meaning 'every book present in the tape' -- which necessarily includes whichever book the ticket was actually placed at. Grading a bet's CLV against a reference set that contains its own execution price biases CLV toward zero exactly when that book's line reacted to the bet itself, defeating the entire point of an independent benchmark (per Buchdahl and Saumarez: the close must be a benchmark external to your own action).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Change DEFAULT_CLOSING_BOOKS in server/services/nfl-execution-clv.js from null to a named, versioned array of sharp/consensus bookmaker_keys actually present in nfl_quote_tape, and filter out the position's own executionBook (already available on the nfl_execution_opportunities row) before computing latestPerBook (lines 147-150).
candidates.expected_value: Removes a specific, mechanical source of CLV bias that would otherwise systematically understate the market's true movement against (or in favor of) a position whenever the execution book itself was slow or fast to react.
candidates.exit_test: Re-grade a sample of already-graded execution positions with the execution book excluded from the reference set and confirm the resulting CLV distribution shifts (nonzero delta) versus the current null-books grading, proving the exclusion is not currently a no-op.

candidates.candidate: Freeze shadow-ledger.js's grading reference to the pre-kickoff closing_spread column instead of the live game_lines.spread column
candidates.fixes_finding: Five independent, disagreeing CLV (closing-line-value) implementations exist over four different tables with different math and sign conventions
candidates.mechanism: shadow-ledger.js's settlement query (around line 71) selects only spread,total,team_score,opp_score -- never closing_spread -- and its inline CLV (lines 77-91) grades against that live column. forward-ledger.js's own comment (lines 148-152) explains why this is wrong: syncCurrentLines can overwrite game_lines.spread with an in-game or post-game number after kickoff, so a column that is not explicitly frozen pre-kickoff cannot serve as a 'closing' reference -- exactly the 'fixed grading period' requirement this research topic names.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add closing_spread,closing_total to shadow-ledger.js's SELECT and mirror forward-ledger.js's fallback pattern (game.closing_spread ?? game.spread) before computing clv at lines 82 and 89-91.
candidates.expected_value: Removes a concrete, currently-live bug where shadow-ledger CLV can silently be computed against a post-kickoff number, which would corrupt exactly the observe/promote decisions the shadow ledger exists to make honest.
candidates.exit_test: For every settled shadow_decisions row where game_lines.spread and closing_spread differ, recompute clv_points with the fixed reference and confirm the two diverge -- proving the current code path is grading against a moving target on at least a subset of historical rows.

candidates.candidate: Add a decorrelation-aware objective to the ensemble's component selection/blend, alongside (not instead of) accuracy
candidates.mechanism: Per Hubáček & Šír's Theorem 4.1 and Table 3 result, a forecast's expected profitability is driven by its partial correlation with the market conditional on the true outcome, not by its raw accuracy; their real-data experiment shows accuracy and profitability can move in OPPOSITE directions as this correlation is deliberately reduced. Gridiron's nfl-ensemble.js has no metric anywhere that measures a component's or the blend's correlation with the market, let alone selects/reweights on it.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a computed diagnostic alongside the existing residual_slope/residual_weight fields in nfl-ensemble.js's perModel array (around lines 1260-1270): a rolling partial correlation of each component's margin residual (model.margin - marketMargin) against realized outcome residual, logged next to model_disagreement_margin. Do not wire it into promotion gates until backtested; start as an observability surface on the market_residual blend path (lines 1288-1299) that already computes marketMargin and model.margin - marketMargin per component.
candidates.expected_value: Turns an invisible property of the ensemble (how much it has quietly become a shrunk copy of the market) into a visible, trackable number -- a precondition for ever testing whether deliberately decorrelating any component would help, which cannot currently even be asked.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest the market_residual blend on 2021-25 held-out weeks with components re-weighted to minimize the decorrelation-augmented loss (MSE* = MSE - γ·Cov[model,market]) at several γ values, and check whether ANY γ improves mean CLV or Brier skill over the current blend on the same weeks -- a null result here is itself informative and should be reported, not hidden.

candidates.candidate: Build a real devig-method bake-off (proportional, Shin, power, additive) scored against actual realized outcomes
candidates.mechanism: nfl-devig.js already centralizes ONE method (Shin, exported as noVig at line 119) but Gridiron has never compared it against alternatives on its own data, and even the best practitioner reference (Outlier.bet) admits it has 'no definitive empirical ranking' either. Štrumbelj (2014, International Journal of Forecasting) established the right evaluation approach for this exact question (Shin vs. proportional normalization, scored by Ranked Probability Score against realized outcomes) but on different data than Gridiron has; the same evaluation design applies directly to Gridiron's own tape.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add proportionalNoVig (already present but unused as an alternative, nfl-devig.js line 114) plus power and additive methods as siblings to shinNoVig, then score each method's implied probabilities against realized game outcomes and the underused 12.4M-row Polymarket quote tape (currently used only for spread-ladder construction) using Brier/RPS, broken out by market skew (heavy favorite vs. pick'em) the way Štrumbelj's design does.
candidates.expected_value: Either confirms Shin is the right default (closing a real open question cheaply) or finds a market-segment (e.g. heavy favorites) where a different method calibrates better -- either outcome is new, decision-useful information Gridiron does not have today.
candidates.exit_test: On a held-out season of Polymarket + sportsbook quotes, the winning method's calibration (Brier/RPS) must beat the current Shin-only default by a margin larger than bootstrap noise across at least 2 of 3 skew buckets (heavy favorite, moderate, near-even) before any devig default changes in production code.

candidates.candidate: Stand up a PBO / deflated-Sharpe trial registry for the 21-component historical model search
candidates.mechanism: Bailey et al.'s combinatorially-symmetric cross-validation (PBO) and the companion Deflated Sharpe Ratio directly answer 'how many of these 21 already-run trials would look this good by chance alone' -- exactly the multiplicity problem the FOUND list names as unaddressed, and exactly the failure mode their own worked example (10 recipients, 0 real skill, from pure selection) demonstrates.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Preregister the 21 already-evaluated ensemble components (and any subsequent ones) in a trial log with fixed evaluation windows, then compute PBO over the existing 2021-25 backtest splits already used in docs/NFL_MODEL_STATUS.md, and require a deflated-Sharpe-adjusted significance threshold (not the raw one) before any future component is described as having cleared the materiality gate.
candidates.expected_value: Directly protects the one number Nick already treats as load-bearing (the 21-model, 0-clear-materiality-gate result) from being silently re-litigated by a 22nd model that only looks good because it was the 22nd trial, not because it has real skill.
candidates.exit_test: Recompute PBO on the 21 historical components using their original evaluation splits; report the resulting probability-of-overfitting figure and the deflated-Sharpe-adjusted bar a 22nd candidate would need to clear -- ship this as a number in NFL_MODEL_STATUS.md before evaluating any new spread/total model.

do_not_do: Do not let any candidate here touch the live fantasy-football-dashboard app, its database, or any running process -- this was a read-only research pass; F1-F3 are proposals for the next work session, not diffs applied tonight.

Do not treat Hubáček & Šír's decorrelation result as license to deliberately make the ensemble LESS accurate for its own sake -- the paper's own honest limitation is that the correlation-based loss is a proxy, not a derivation from the real utility function; N1 must be validated by backtested CLV/Brier improvement, not adopted on theory alone.

Do not pick a single 'best' devig method (N2) from practitioner blog claims alone -- Outlier.bet's own comparison admits it has no empirical ranking; the method must be chosen by scoring against Gridiron's own realized-outcome data, not by citation count.

Do not fold F1's canonical CLV module and N1's decorrelation metric into the same change -- one is a straight consolidation of existing, tested math (low risk), the other is a new, unvalidated signal; shipping them together would make it impossible to tell which one caused a regression if CLV numbers move after the change.

Do not set DEFAULT_CLOSING_BOOKS (F2) to an empty or overly narrow set just to 'fix' the null-books default -- an unreachable reference set (no quotes ever match) silently produces 'no_quote_tape_coverage' everywhere, which is a worse failure mode than the current bias because it looks like missing data rather than a biased number.

Do not apply the PBO/deflated-Sharpe correction (N3) only to future models while grandfathering the 21 already-run trials -- the whole point of the correction is to price in trials already spent; exempting past trials defeats it.

result.label: F03: Devig methods — Gridiron's Shin implementation is real but incompletely wired; power method untested
result.summary: Correction to tonight's FOUND item: nfl-devig.js already implements a real, tested Shin(1992/1993)-vs-multiplicative comparison and Shin is the correct default in 9 of the 11 files that compute a no-vig probability. But grep turned up two files — nfl-total-calibration.js and nfl-neural-replay.js — that still reimplement the pre-fix naive proportional split locally instead of importing shinNoVig, so two governance/audit surfaces (the totals-model staking gate and the neural-head prequential audit) are silently using a different market baseline than their sibling nfl-cover-calibration.js. Separately, literature confirms Gridiron's Shin implementation is mathematically identical to the "additive" method for every market Gridiron actually prices (all two-outcome), so the real missing comparison isn't Shin-vs-additive, it's Shin-vs-power — Clarke/Kovalchik/Ingram (2017) found the power method universally beats multiplicative and matches-or-beats Shin, and Gridiron has never implemented or tested it. No empirical validation of any devig method against Gridiron's own NFL outcomes exists anywhere (consistent with tonight's "no conformal/calibration" finding) — that harness is proposed as new capability.

sources.sample: n/a — source code, 110 lines

sources.title: mberk/shin — Python implementation of Shin's method
sources.sample: n/a — library README + usage examples
sources.key_result: Independently states and demonstrates: 'when there are only two outcomes, Shin's method is equivalent to the Additive Method' — confirms Gridiron's existing Shin implementation already covers the additive slot for every NFL market it prices (all two-outcome).

sources.title: neeljshah/shin-devig — multiplicative/additive/power/Shin devig library
sources.sample: worked 3-way example, decimal odds [1.40, 4.20, 9.00]
sources.key_result: Implements all four Clarke-et-al methods with a documented, tested two-outcome shin==additive identity ('verified in tests/test_methods.py::test_two_outcome_shin_equals_additive, stress-tested to ~1e-15 over random 2-way markets') and cites Štrumbelj (2014) finding Shin/power beat plain normalization on average.

sources.title: opisthokonta/implied — R package, 8 devig methods
sources.sample: n/a — R source (571 lines) + CRAN introduction vignette
sources.key_result: Uses the same Jullien & Salanié (1994) closed-form Shin algorithm Gridiron cites; vignette states the basic/multiplicative method 'tend[s] to be the least accurate of the methods in this package' — third independent source confirming multiplicative is the weak baseline.

sources.title: Clarke, Kovalchik & Ingram (2017), 'Adjusting Bookmaker's Odds to Allow for Overround'
sources.authors: Stephen Clarke, Stephanie Kovalchik, Martin Ingram
sources.venue: American Journal of Sports Science 5(6), 2017, pp. 45-49
sources.sample: 'three large bookmaker datasets, each in a different sport' — specific sports and n not confirmed by me; full-text PDF returned HTTP 403 from ResearchGate, 1Library, and Swinburne Figshare on every attempt
sources.key_result: Compares additive/multiplicative(normalization)/Shin/power; the power method (raise each implied prob to a fitted exponent so outputs sum to 1) 'universally outperforms the multiplicative method and outperforms or is comparable to the Shin method,' and is the only one of the four that can never push a probability outside (0,1) even applied in reverse. Corroborated identically across Semantic Scholar, ResearchGate, and two independent package docs, but I did not read the body — do not cite this as NFL-specific proof.

candidates.candidate: Route nfl-total-calibration.js's noVig() through shinNoVig from nfl-devig.js instead of its local naive proportional split, and re-run its walk-forward fit under a bumped calibration version.
candidates.fixes_finding: No real devig method comparison exists; probabilities are extracted with one ad hoc approach — grep-verified this literally still applies at server/services/nfl-total-calibration.js:37, which reimplements the pre-fix proportional-split noVig (pa/(pa+pb)) locally rather than importing shinNoVig from nfl-devig.js, unlike its sibling nfl-cover-calibration.js which correctly imports it.
candidates.mechanism: nfl-total-calibration.js defines its own `implied`/`noVig` pair and feeds `marketProbOver` (line 252) into `calibratedCoverProbability`'s totals counterpart — the exact staking gate the file's own docstring says was missing entirely before this module existed. That gate is now live but trained against a different market-probability baseline than the spread-side gate, meaning the two governance gates disagree about what 'the market' means for the same underlying devig problem.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Change `const noVig = (a,b)=>{...proportional...}` to `import { shinNoVig as noVig } from './nfl-devig.js'`; bump VERSION from 'total-logit-v1' to 'total-logit-v2-shin'; re-run buildTotalCalibration's fitLogisticOffset/selectLambda walk-forward fit since training labels shift slightly; do not reinterpret old stored rows under the new baseline without the version bump.
candidates.expected_value: Removes a live, silent double standard between the two model-vs-market governance gates (spread gate uses Shin, totals gate uses multiplicative) without changing the anchoring design (still sigmoid(logit(market)+b0+b1*x), still can only match-or-lose to market at b0=b1=0).
candidates.exit_test: Re-run the totals walk-forward fit; confirm b0/b1 stay within the same order of magnitude as before (no wild jump proving the old baseline was silently hiding a much larger discrepancy) and that nfl-total-calibration.test.js (if any) or a new equivalent test asserts marketProbOver now equals shinNoVig(total_over_odds, total_under_odds).

candidates.candidate: Same fix as F03-fix-1, applied to nfl-neural-replay.js's local noVig at line 26.
candidates.fixes_finding: No real devig method comparison exists; probabilities are extracted with one ad hoc approach — same defect, second grep-verified occurrence, this time feeding home_market_probability in the prequential audit for the online spread-residual neural head.
candidates.mechanism: nfl-neural-replay.js is explicitly documented as 'an opened research candidate and never changes production authority,' so the stakes are lower than F03-fix-1, but it exists specifically to judge a model's forecasts against the market and currently does so against the wrong market baseline relative to every other audit surface in the codebase.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Same import swap: replace local `implied`/`noVig` with `import { shinNoVig as noVig } from './nfl-devig.js'` at the top of nfl-neural-replay.js; bump NEURAL_REPLAY_VERSION since the calibrator (ridge-logit) is fit on these probabilities.
candidates.expected_value: Makes the neural-head audit consistent with every other model-vs-market comparison in the codebase; low risk since this module never gates live staking.
candidates.exit_test: NEURAL_REPLAY_VERSION bumped; a quick before/after diff on a sample week shows home_market_probability values shift by the same magnitude Shin-vs-proportional divergence tests already show for skewed lines.

candidates.candidate: Add a third method, power devig (Clarke/Kovalchik/Ingram 2017), to nfl-devig.js alongside proportional and Shin, ported from neeljshah/shin-devig's bisection-for-exponent approach.
candidates.fixes_finding: No real devig method comparison exists; probabilities are extracted with one ad hoc approach — even after tonight's Shin upgrade this remains true in a narrower sense: the comparison Gridiron ships (proportional vs Shin) omits the one method the peer-reviewed literature found actually outperforms both, and since every Gridiron NFL market is two-outcome, Shin is mathematically identical to the 'additive' alternative (independently confirmed by mberk/shin and neeljshah/shin-devig), so the real missing arm of the comparison is Shin-vs-power, not Shin-vs-additive.
candidates.mechanism: Solve by bisection for exponent k such that the two implied probabilities each raised to 1/k sum to 1, matching neeljshah/shin-devig's verified formulation; expose powerNoVig with the same export shape as shinNoVig/proportionalNoVig so every existing caller pattern ('kept for comparison') extends for free.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add powerDevig()/powerNoVig() to nfl-devig.js next to shinDevig/proportionalDevig; add divergence tests to test/nfl-devig.test.js mirroring the existing Shin-vs-proportional skewed-favorite test; do NOT flip the default noVig export until F03-new-1's backtest says to.
candidates.expected_value: Completes the actual comparison the module's own docstring implies exists ('this is the correct one' vs proportional) but doesn't yet test against the literature's stronger candidate; low cost since the bisection scaffolding (tol, maxIter, bracket-fallback pattern) already exists in shinDevig to copy.
candidates.exit_test: New tests pass showing power and Shin agree closely on mild skew and diverge in the direction Clarke et al. predict on extreme skew (-1400/900 case already in the test file); powerNoVig never returns a value outside (0,1) even on the most extreme price pairs already covered by 'Shin's output is always a valid probability distribution' test.

candidates.candidate: Build an NFL-specific empirical devig-method validation harness: replay Gridiron's own historical closing lines against actual final scores (spread cover, total over/under) and score multiplicative vs. Shin vs. power on log-loss/Brier/calibration curve.
candidates.mechanism: Clarke et al. (2017)'s 'power universally outperforms multiplicative' result is not confirmed to include NFL among its three sport datasets (I could not read the body to check), and no conformal/calibration validation of any kind exists anywhere in the pipeline per tonight's findings. This closes that gap with Gridiron's own data instead of importing an unverified-for-NFL result as the new default.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Attach to nfl-replay.js's existing walk-forward scoring infrastructure (replaySeason, already reused by nfl-cover-calibration.js) and the historical nfl_line_snapshots table; for each closed game, compute proportional/Shin/power fair probabilities from the closing two-way price, score each against the realized outcome, and report calibration curves + Brier score per method per season.
candidates.expected_value: Settles, with real NFL data rather than borrowed authority, whether switching any live governance gate's default devig method from Shin to power is actually justified — directly gates F03-fix-3's power method before it's allowed to become a default anywhere.
candidates.exit_test: A report showing per-method Brier score and calibration-curve deviation across at least 2 full historical seasons of closed NFL games; if power doesn't beat Shin by a real margin on Gridiron's own data, the do_not_do below applies and Shin stays the production default.

candidates.candidate: Per-book/per-market single-sided vig estimation: when only one side of a two-way price is captured (no opposite quote), estimate the fair probability from a learned historical overround profile for that book+market instead of returning the raw vig-included implied probability.
candidates.mechanism: Currently nfl-clv.js:198 and nfl-props.js fall back to raw americanToProb(ourPrice) — an honest 'best available' comment, but still a vig-included probability with no correction at all — whenever the opposite side's price is missing. No model of book-specific vig magnitude exists today anywhere in the pipeline.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Build a small lookup (book, market) -> median historical overround from nfl_line_snapshots' two-sided rows for that same book/market, then apply that median margin (via whichever devig method F03-new-1 validates) to the one-sided price rather than leaving it un-devigged; fall back to raw implied only when no historical overround estimate exists yet for that book+market pair.
candidates.expected_value: Small but real accuracy gain specifically on one-sided quotes (which the existing comment already flags as a known weak point), and directly reuses the 12.4M-row Polymarket tape / nfl_line_snapshots data tonight's findings call 'essentially unused.'
candidates.exit_test: For a held-out set of games where both sides were actually quoted, mask one side, apply the estimated-overround correction to the remaining side, and confirm the corrected probability is closer to the true two-sided-devigged probability than the raw implied probability is, on average.

candidates.candidate: Devig-method provenance tagging: record which devig method (and any fitted z or k parameter) produced each stored market_probability in nfl_bet_log, nfl_cover_calibrations, and nfl_total_calibration, so a later method upgrade can't silently reinterpret historical CLV grades under a different probability basis.
candidates.mechanism: Tonight's findings note five independent, disagreeing CLV implementations over four different tables with different math/sign conventions, and no trial registry exists for the historical model search already run. This is a narrower, cheaper adjacent gap: even a single consistent devig method (once F03-fix-1/2/3 land) still has no record of *which* method (and version) generated any given historical probability, so a future default-method change (e.g. adopting power after F03-new-1 validates it) has no way to distinguish old-basis rows from new-basis rows when computing longitudinal CLV.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a `devig_method` (+ optional `devig_param`) column to nfl_bet_log and the two calibration tables, populated at write time from nfl-devig.js's existing exported method name constants; migration only, no behavior change.
candidates.expected_value: Cheap insurance against exactly the kind of silent-baseline-change problem F03-fix-1 discovered by accident (grep, not by any existing safeguard); makes any future devig-method migration auditable instead of invisible.
candidates.exit_test: Every new row written to the three tables after this change carries a non-null devig_method matching one of nfl-devig.js's exported method names; a query joining bet_log to its devig_method can reproduce the exact market_probability stored, given the recorded odds and method.

do_not_do: Do not flip the default noVig export (or any live governance gate's devig baseline) to the power method without first running F03-new-1's Gridiron-specific backtest — Clarke et al. (2017)'s 'power beats multiplicative/Shin' result was not confirmed by me to include NFL among its three tested sports.

Do not implement a separate 'additive' devig method for any Gridiron market — every market Gridiron prices (spread, total, moneyline, anytime-TD) is two-outcome, where additive is mathematically identical to Shin (independently confirmed by mberk/shin and neeljshah/shin-devig); it would be redundant code and a fourth thing to keep in sync for zero behavioral difference.

Do not change nfl-total-calibration.js's or nfl-cover-calibration.js's devig baseline without re-running their walk-forward fits and bumping their version constants — both are logistic offsets anchored to 'reproduce the market exactly at b0=b1=0,' so changing what 'the market' means underneath them without refitting silently changes what they gate.

Do not touch, edit, run tests against, or otherwise disturb the fantasy-football-dashboard repo tonight beyond read/grep — it is live-capturing Week 1 NFL games through Sunday; everything above is a verified plan, not a change made.

Do not spend a paid API call or scrape new odds data to build the F03-new-1 backtest — the already-collected 12.4M-row Polymarket tape and nfl_line_snapshots table are sufficient and are explicitly flagged tonight as underused for exactly this kind of validation.
Do not port opisthokonta/implied's R source verbatim — it has no declared open-source license on GitHub; treat its documentation/vignette as citable literature, not as code to copy.

repos.what_it_does: Python (Rust core) implementation of Shin's method only, with a full_output mode exposing z, iteration count, and convergence delta; documents the exact two-outcome shin==additive identity.
repos.adoption_path: Not ported — Gridiron's own shinDevig already matches its behavior on two-outcome markets and already exposes z; its diagnostic-output pattern (iterations/convergence delta) is worth mirroring in nfl-devig.js's own bisection loop for debuggability, nothing more.

repos.what_it_does: Pure-Python, zero-dependency implementation of all four Clarke-et-al methods (multiplicative/additive/power/Shin) via bisection, with worked examples and an explicit tested two-outcome shin==additive identity.
repos.adoption_path: Port its power-method bisection formulation (solve for exponent k such that sum(p_i**(1/k))==1) into nfl-devig.js's existing bisection style, matching its verified sign/direction conventions rather than re-deriving from scratch.

repos.what_it_does: R package implementing 8 devig methods (basic, shin, bb, wpo, or, power, additive, jsd) using the same Jullien & Salanié (1994) closed-form Shin algorithm Gridiron already cites; CRAN vignette documents literature citations for each method.
repos.adoption_path: Used only as a corroborating literature summary (confirms Gridiron's Shin implementation matches the standard algorithm, confirms multiplicative is the documented weak baseline); do not copy R source given the unclear license.

result.label: F02: real forecast combination for nfl-ensemble.js
result.summary: nfl-ensemble.js's production blend ('market_residual', hardcoded by nfl-forecast-identity.js:41, nfl-unified-engine.js:40, nfl-auto-picks.js:83, nfl-cover-calibration.js:276) is a weighted average of 31 separate single-covariate no-intercept regressions of each model against the market (nfl-ensemble.js:1112-1143, 1291-1299) — mechanically why it collapses to forecast ≈ 0.68 + 0.632·market. The inclusion gate (lines 1185-1188) is a single-split paired t-stat, never benchmarked against the equal-weight option that already exists in code (line 1167) but is never used in production. Read in full: Yao/Vehtari/Simpson/Gelman 2018 (Bayesian stacking of predictive distributions via PSIS-LOO log-score optimization on the simplex), Claeskens/Magnus/Vasnev/Wang 2016 (proves estimated weights are biased and higher-variance than fixed/equal weights — 3-15% variance inflation in their 1M-replication Monte Carlo), Giacomini-White 2006 (the real conditional-predictive-ability test, generalizing Diebold-Mariano, with the exact χ² Wald statistic), and Diebold-Mariano 1995 (the base test, valid under any loss function and serial/contemporaneous correlation, needed because the current paired-t has no Harvey small-sample correction and no HAC variance). Proposes replacing the per-model regression-then-average with a real simplex-constrained stacking/CLS optimization, gating inclusion with a properly instrumented GW test with multiplicity correction, and benchmarking every promotion against the already-coded but never-used equal-weight baseline. New-capability half: full log-score stacking over predictive distributions (not just point margins), and a standing conditional-predictive-ability monitor (not a one-shot backtest stat) that can detect regime-dependent model decay using information-set instruments.

sources.title: Using Stacking to Average Bayesian Predictive Distributions (with Discussion)
sources.authors: Yuling Yao, Aki Vehtari, Daniel Simpson, Andrew Gelman
sources.sample: Simulations: n=3..300, 100 repeats x 100 test points, predictor correlation -0.3..0.9, 8-component Gaussian-mixture M-open example; real-data: US Senate proximity/directional voting (n=94) and Bangladesh party-switching.
sources.key_result: Stacking of predictive distributions solves max_w (1/n)Σ log Σ_k w_k p(y_i|y_-i,M_k) s.t. w on the simplex, using PSIS-LOO to avoid refitting; it and the cheaper Pseudo-BMA+ (Bayesian-bootstrap-regularized AIC weights) beat BMA, model selection, and full mixture models in every tested condition and are robust to high correlation among candidate models, unlike BMA which asymptotically collapses to one model.

sources.title: The forecast combination puzzle: A simple theoretical explanation
sources.authors: Gerda Claeskens, Jan R. Magnus, Andrey L. Vasnev, Wendun Wang
sources.sample: AR(2)-generated forecast pair, T=30 observations, 1,000,000 Monte Carlo replications, phi1/phi2 swept over [-0.9, 0.4]; closed-form moment results for general m-dimensional combinations.
sources.key_result: When weights are estimated rather than fixed the combined forecast becomes biased (E[y_c]=mu+cov(w,y1-y2)) purely from weight-estimation randomness; numerically the estimated-weight combination's variance is 3-4% higher than the fixed-equal-weight combination when forecasts are similar, and up to ~15% higher when forecast variances differ substantially -- the formal explanation for why simple averages beat 'optimal' estimated weights in practice.

sources.title: Tests of Conditional Predictive Ability
sources.sample: Theory + illustration: 146 monthly US macro series (Stock-Watson 2002 dataset), 1-/6-/12-month-ahead forecasts comparing sequential model selection, diffusion-index, and Bayesian-shrinkage forecasting methods.
sources.key_result: Reframes forecast comparison as testing E[delta-loss | F_t]=0 (conditional, not unconditional) for a full 'forecasting method' (model+estimator+window); test statistic T^h_{n,m}=n*Zbar'*Omega^-1*Zbar converges to chi-square_q (Theorem 1), unifying nested/non-nested comparisons and valid under heterogeneity and finite (non-vanishing) estimation windows -- in their own illustration the 'sophisticated' sequential-selection method is routinely beaten by a naive AR/random-walk benchmark once judged this way.

sources.title: Comparing Predictive Accuracy
sources.authors: Francis X. Diebold, Roberto S. Mariano
sources.sample: Theoretical derivation plus small-sample sign-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank alternatives; the base test the entire post-1995 forecast-comparison literature (including Giacomini-White) builds on.
sources.key_result: S1 = dbar / sqrt(2*pi*fhat_d(0)/T) is asymptotically N(0,1) under equal-accuracy H0, valid for ANY loss function (not just squared error) and for non-Gaussian, nonzero-mean, serially- and contemporaneously-correlated forecast errors -- the naive F-test on variance ratios requires four assumptions (incl. independent errors) that real forecasts essentially never satisfy.

sources.title: A Simple Explanation of the Forecast Combination Puzzle
sources.venue: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics 71(3)
sources.sample: Cited and directly quoted (3 numbered conclusions) within Claeskens et al. 2016 Section 5; not independently fetched.
sources.key_result: Three conclusions used to ground the do-not-do list: (1) simple average beats estimated-weight combination on MSFE in expectation; (2) if weights must be estimated, ignore forecast-error covariances and use inverse-MSE only; (3) with many forecasts, gains from unequal weighting are typically not statistically significant.

candidates.candidate: Replace the per-model no-intercept regression-then-average (nfl-ensemble.js:1112-1143, 1291-1299) with a single joint simplex-constrained stacking/CLS optimization over all surviving models.
candidates.fixes_finding: The naive forecast ≈ 0.68 + 0.632*market shrinkage: it is mechanically produced by averaging 31 separate single-covariate regressions of each model against the market instead of fitting the models jointly, which is exactly the 'stacking of means' problem Breiman/Yao et al. describe (Eq 1.1: minimize sum (y_i - sum w_k*fhat_k)^2 s.t. w on simplex).
candidates.mechanism: Compute each model's cutoff-safe, week-split leave-one-out (or leave-one-week-out) prediction fhat_k^(-i)(x_i) exactly as fitEnsemble already does per-model RMSE (lines 1112-1130), but instead of a per-model slope against the market, solve one QP: minimize sum_i (y_i - sum_k w_k*fhat_k^(-i))^2 s.t. w_k>=0, sum w_k=1 (Yao et al. Eq 1.1/2.2 with quadratic loss = 'stacking of means'). Include the market itself as one of the K inputs (it already is, id:'market_anchor') so shrinkage toward market emerges only if the data supports it, not by construction.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New function replacing blend('margin','margin_weight') and the market_residual path in nfl-ensemble.js (~1220-1300): fit weights via constrained least squares (small QP, <=31 unknowns) using the SAME weekly train/score split machinery already built (completeWeekSplit, fitWeeks/scoreWeeks, lines 1112-1119). Store as a new fit-artifact version bump (ENSEMBLE_FIT_VERSION in nfl-forecast-identity.js) so no stale artifact is silently reused across the methodology change, following the existing v9/v10 precedent in that file's own comments.
candidates.expected_value: Directly attacks the -2.28 CLV / 78%-adverse-move finding: a jointly-fit combination cannot degenerate to a fixed linear function of the market alone unless that is genuinely optimal, so if the ensemble truly has no edge this will show up as weights collapsing onto market_anchor (an honest result) rather than an opaque 0.68/0.632 shrinkage that looks like a model but isn't one.
candidates.exit_test: Refit both the current market_residual blend and the new CLS/stacking blend on the same 2022-2025 walk-forward weeks; compare mean CLV and RMSE against the close using a Giacomini-White test (candidate F02-fix-2). Ship the new blend only if it beats market_residual at p<0.05 after multiplicity correction; otherwise the honest conclusion is the market_anchor-only forecast and betting stays gated off regardless.

candidates.candidate: Replace the single-split paired-t inclusion gate (nfl-ensemble.js:1185-1188) with a real Giacomini-White conditional predictive ability test (with a Diebold-Mariano-with-Harvey-correction fallback for the unconditional case), plus Holm correction across the 31 models tested.
candidates.fixes_finding: Five independent, disagreeing CLV implementations and no real devig comparison both stem from the same root cause as this: ad hoc single-shot significance tests invented per-surface instead of one shared, textbook-correct predictive-ability test. Also directly fixes: 'residual_rmse_gain>=0.03 && residual_paired_t<=-1.645' (nfl-ensemble.js:1186) is an unconditional, uncorrected, single-split t-stat -- not the OOF-1 week-clustered standard the code's own comment (lines 1179-1184) says nfl-cover-calibration.js uses elsewhere.
candidates.mechanism: Giacomini-White (2006) Theorem 1: T^h_{n,m}=n*Zbar'*Omega_hat^-1*Zbar ~ chi-square_q, Z_{t+1}=h_t*deltaL_{t+1}, for a chosen information-set instrument vector h_t (e.g. h_t=[1, lagged model disagreement, market vig regime] rather than just h_t=1, which recovers the unconditional Diebold-Mariano special case). Port the ~40-line DM/Harvey-correction logic from johntwk/Diebold-Mariano-Test (MIT) directly into JS rather than adding an R/Python runtime dependency; extend the scalar case to the vector h_t/Omega_hat HAC form for the conditional version.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: See mechanism/module above.
candidates.expected_value: Removes false-positive component promotion: at alpha=0.05 across 31 simultaneous per-model tests, ~1.5 components pass the current gate by chance alone with zero correction; Holm-corrected GW/DM testing plus a shared implementation collapses five different CLV significance conventions into one auditable standard.
candidates.exit_test: Re-run the existing test/nfl-ensemble-authority.test.js and test/nfl-ensemble-opponent-adjustment.test.js suites against the new gate; confirm the set of models passing the Holm-corrected GW gate is a strict subset of what passes today's uncorrected single-split t-stat, and that at least one currently-passing model (candidate: a redundant efficiency-family model) is correctly demoted.

candidates.candidate: Add a standing equal-weight ('comb_SA') and inverse-MSE-only ('comb_BG') benchmark run alongside every production ensemble fit, and require any more complex weighting to beat both via the GW test before being served.
candidates.fixes_finding: weighting:'equal' already exists in code (nfl-ensemble.js:1167) and weighting:'inverse_mse' already exists (line 1168), but nfl-forecast-identity.js:44 defaults every caller to 'exponential' and no code path ever compares them -- so the exact naive-shrinkage defect (0.68+0.632*market) has never been checked against the literature's own null model.
candidates.mechanism: Smith & Wallis (2009) / Claeskens et al. (2016): with estimated weights the combination is biased (Eq 3, Claeskens) and has 3-15% higher variance than the fixed/equal-weight combination in their 1M-replication Monte Carlo; the equal average is 'hard to beat' and complex covariance-aware weighting rarely earns back its estimation cost.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: In fitEnsemble() (nfl-ensemble.js ~1094-1213), always additionally compute margin_weight/total_weight under weighting='equal' and weighting='inverse_mse' (the code paths already exist, lines 1167-1168) and store all three weighting results in the fit artifact. In nfl-forecast-identity.js, gate promotion of 'exponential' to production status on it beating 'equal' by a GW-test margin, not on developer default.
candidates.expected_value: Cheapest possible check: the weighting variants already exist in the code, this only wires up the comparison and a promotion gate that has never existed. If 'equal' wins (plausible given 31 collinear inputs), Gridiron immediately gets a lower-variance, harder-to-overfit production forecast for free.
candidates.exit_test: Run all three weighting schemes over the full 2022-2025 walk-forward replay (scripts/fit-weekly-ensemble.mjs) and report mean CLV + GW p-value of exponential vs equal. Ship whichever wins; if equal wins, flip the default in nfl-forecast-identity.js:44 and document the reversal.

candidates.candidate: Full log-score Bayesian stacking of each model's predictive DISTRIBUTION (mean + variance), not just its point margin, using PSIS-LOO-estimated leave-one-out predictive densities.
candidates.mechanism: Yao/Vehtari/Simpson/Gelman (2018) Eq 2.2: max_w (1/n) sum_i log(sum_k w_k * p(y_i | y_-i, M_k)) s.t. w on the simplex, using PSIS-LOO (Eq 2.4) to approximate p(y_i|y_-i,M_k) without refitting each model n times. This is the M-open-consistent generalization of BMA and is the only method in the simulation study that beats mixture models and BMA across every tested sample size and predictor-correlation level (Fig 6).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: predictiveDistribution() (nfl-ensemble.js:1301) currently builds ONE distribution AFTER the point margin/total are already blended -- it never stacks K separate predictive distributions. Give each surviving model a (margin_mean, margin_sd) pair (several already imply a natural residual SD from their own held-out errors, e.g. margin_rmse at line 1136), compute each model's LOO log predictive density at each historical game, and solve the log-score simplex optimization for w_k. Feed the resulting stacked distribution -- not just its mean -- into predictiveDistribution() and downstream into the drive simulator's margin/total inputs and the props module's projection distributions.
candidates.expected_value: This is the one place where the fix for the ensemble (point-forecast shrinkage) and the fix for 'no calibrated uncertainty interval anywhere' converge: a stacked predictive distribution gives an honestly-combined SD for free, instead of the current assumed-normal SD bolted on after a point blend. Directly usable by the props module (the one area of genuine measured skill) to move from point estimates toward real distributions.
candidates.exit_test: Compare the stacked distribution's PIT (probability integral transform) histogram / CRPS against the current predictiveDistribution() output on held-out 2022-2025 games; ship only if CRPS improves and the PIT histogram is flatter (better calibrated) than today's assumed-normal approach.

candidates.candidate: A standing, scheduled conditional-predictive-ability monitor (not a one-shot backtest stat) that runs the Giacomini-White test with time-varying instruments every week to detect regime-dependent decay in any ensemble component or in the ensemble itself.
candidates.mechanism: Giacomini-White's central methodological point is that H0 is conditional on F_t (Eq 3), not a fixed population average -- so a component can pass an unconditional/single-split significance test (like today's gate) while its predictive ability is entirely concentrated in one regime (e.g. only works pre-Week-6, or only when the market line is stale) and has decayed to zero or negative in the current regime. Today's gate has no mechanism to detect this because it only ever computes one static statistic per fit.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New weekly job (fits naturally alongside nfl-signal-reliability.js's existing shrink-only, cutoff-safe controller pattern) computing the GW statistic with h_t = [1, week-of-season bucket, market-disagreement magnitude, days-since-line-move] for every production model and for the ensemble as a whole, storing a rolling p-value trend rather than a single frozen number. Surface a decay alert (mirroring nfl-signal-reliability.js's shrink-only philosophy: it can flag decay and shrink weight but never increase authority based on a search).
candidates.expected_value: Converts model risk management from 'was this ever significant' to 'is this still working right now, in the regime we are currently in' -- the single most important gap for a model whose production authority currently rests on one fixed split fit weeks or months ago.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest the monitor against the known 2026 Week-1-diagnostic period (per memory: gridiron-week1-2026-diagnostic.md) and confirm it would have flagged the components later found to be broken before the unconditional single-split gate did.

candidates.candidate: Pre-optimization collinearity reduction: cluster the 31 models by held-out prediction correlation and collapse each cluster to its single best representative (or its own within-cluster equal-weight average) before any stacking/CLS weight optimization runs.
candidates.fixes_finding: none -- new capability (addresses the '20 components collapse to ~3 independent signals' framing, but as a genuinely new dimensionality-reduction step Gridiron has never had, not a repair of an existing broken step)
candidates.mechanism: Yao et al. note stacking is robust to correlated candidates but still degrades in small-n regimes (Fig 5, n < ~5x effective parameters) -- with 31 correlated inputs and roughly 4 NFL seasons x 17 weeks of history, the effective-parameter-to-n ratio is worse than it looks once true independence is accounted for. Reducing to ~3-6 effective clusters before optimizing directly improves the conditioning of the simplex QP in F02-fix-1.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New pre-processing step ahead of fitEnsemble()'s weighting loop: compute the pairwise correlation matrix of each model's held-out margin residuals (data already computed per-model in the `errs`/`residuals` maps around nfl-ensemble.js:1112), hierarchically cluster, and either drop near-duplicates or force cluster-level weight-sharing constraints into the F02-fix-1 QP.
candidates.expected_value: Makes the stacking optimization in F02-fix-1 more stable and interpretable (fewer, more distinct effective weights) and gives an honest answer to 'how many real signals does this ensemble actually have' instead of the current 31-model illusion of diversity.
candidates.exit_test: Report the effective number of clusters found (expect roughly 3-6 given the FOUND finding); confirm the F02-fix-1 stacking QP's out-of-sample CRPS/RMSE is no worse (ideally better) after clustering than fit on the raw 31 correlated inputs.

repos.what_it_does: dm_test.py (164 lines, ~40 of real logic): builds the loss-differential series under MSE/MAD/MAPE/power loss, computes an HAC-style variance V_d=(gamma_0 + 2*sum(gamma_1..h-1))/T via sample autocovariance of the loss differential, then DM = V_d^-0.5 * dbar * harvey_adj where harvey_adj = sqrt((T+1-2h+h(h-1)/T)/T) is exactly the Harvey/Leybourne/Newbold (1997) small-sample correction; p-value from a Student-t(T-1).
repos.adoption_path: Reimplement these ~40 lines natively in JS as server/services/nfl-predictive-ability-test.js's dmTest(), extended with a vector instrument h_t and HAC Omega for the Giacomini-White conditional form (F02-fix-2); do not add a Python dependency for something this small.

repos.what_it_does: R package cataloguing the textbook menu of forecast-combination weight schemes as separate files: comb_SA.R (simple average, w=1/N), comb_BG.R (Bates-Granger inverse-MSE with no covariance term), comb_CLS.R (simplex-constrained least squares), comb_OLS/comb_WA/comb_EIG1-4 (Hsiao-Wan eigenvector weighting)/comb_NG/comb_InvW/comb_MED/comb_LAD/comb_TA/comb_CSR. Confirmed by reading R/comb_SA.R and R/comb_BG.R directly.
repos.adoption_path: Not called from Node (R, and stale since 2018); used only as concrete confirmation that Gridiron's existing but unused weighting:'equal' (comb_SA equivalent, nfl-ensemble.js:1167) and weighting:'inverse_mse' (comb_BG equivalent, line 1168) are literature-standard baselines, not toy fallbacks, for F02-fix-3.

do_not_do: Do not add a Stan/R/Python runtime dependency to the Node betting service to get 'real' Bayesian stacking or the DM/GW test -- both are small enough (a <=31-dimension constrained QP; a HAC variance estimator) to implement natively in JS; port johntwk's ~40-line DM test rather than shelling out to R.

Do not add more models to chase a bigger 'ensemble' -- the finding is that 31 models already collapse to ~3 independent factors; more collinear inputs make the stacking QP more degenerate, not less. Reduce (cluster) before you optimize (F02-new-3), don't expand.

Do not let any new stacking or GW-gated weight bypass the existing walk-forward cutoff discipline (fitEnsemble's beforeSeason/beforeWeek) or the week-boundary split fix already made for finding M05/C07 (nfl-ensemble.js comment lines 1097-1152) -- a leave-one-game-out LOO for stacking must still respect 'no two games from the same week straddle the fit/score boundary'.

Do not treat a single significant DM/GW test on one model as production promotion. 31 models are being tested simultaneously; apply Holm (or another multiplicity correction) exactly as flagged for the separate 21-model historical-search trial-registry gap, or ~1.5 components will be falsely promoted by chance alone at alpha=0.05.

Do not compute stacking or GW-test weights once per season and freeze them for all 17+ weeks -- Claeskens et al.'s bias term (cov(w, y1-y2)) and Giacomini-White's whole conditional framing both say predictive ability is regime-dependent; refit/re-test on the same cadence the walk-forward cutoff already uses, and prefer the standing monitor (F02-new-2) over a single frozen backtest number.

Do not report the new stacking blend's in-sample fit quality as the exit criterion. Every comparison must be against genuinely held-out, week-clustered, out-of-fold games (the same OOF-1 standard nfl-cover-calibration.js already uses) -- an in-sample CRPS or RMSE improvement proves nothing about whether the new combination beats the naive shrinkage on real future games.

result.label: Bitemporal / point-in-time data engineering — receipt-clock bug
result.summary: Confirmed by reading the code: Codex correction C11 (migration 032) fixed the receipt-clock bug only at the nfl_quote_batches level, and only for callers that pass receivedAt. The two files this brief named still leak the bug. (1) book-feeds.js:390-419 — captureBookFeeds() computes `at` AFTER Promise.all resolves all 5 provider fetches (a genuine post-response receipt time) but passes it into ingestQuoteSnapshot only as `requestedAt`, never as `receivedAt` — so every batch from the free-book-feeds path (the feed actually running live right now, since paid Odds API credits are gone) is permanently mislabeled 'legacy_request_time_only' and every one of its quotes is thrown into availability_unknown by the T-60 packet's realClock filter, even though a good receipt time was computed and simply not passed through. (2) nfl-quote-tape.js's unwrap() (lines 35-41) always sets the per-quote `snapshot_at` — the only clock quoteSurface(), closingQuotes(), and bestExecutableQuote() ever filter on — from `requestedAt`, never `receivedAt`, regardless of what the batch table now correctly stores; nfl_quote_tape itself has no received_at/receipt_clock_source columns at all. Those three query functions currently have zero callers elsewhere in the repo, so this is a latent trap rather than an active corruption today, but it is exactly the surface any real point-in-time execution logic would reach for next. Grounded in 4 sources read in full (Akidau et al.'s Dataflow Model paper defining event-time vs processing-time and watermarks; Kulkarni & Michels' SQL:2011 temporal-features paper defining application-time vs system-versioned tables and the ADD-COLUMN-not-rewrite retrofit pattern; Snodgrass's canonical textbook chapter with the $25M Hudson Foods valid-time cautionary tale; Databricks' point-in-time feature-join docs, read specifically to find and flag that its AS-OF pattern makes the same single-clock mistake). Two real GitHub bitemporal implementations inspected directly (arkhipov/temporal_tables, 1,050 stars, actively maintained, BSD-2 — exact trigger+history-table retrofit recipe; scalegenius/pg_bitemporal, stale, correction-pattern reference only). Gridiron runs node:sqlite, so both are borrow-idea/reference-only, not portable dependencies — Gridiron's own migration 032 and its existing nfl_quote_tape_no_update/no_delete triggers already implement the append-only half of the pattern correctly; the gap is per-row receipt-clock completeness and a formal correction/supersession link, not the absence of the underlying technique.

sources.title: The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Balancing Correctness, Latency, and Cost in Massive-Scale, Unbounded, Out-of-Order Data Processing
sources.authors: Akidau, Bradshaw, Chambers, Chernyak, Fernández-Moctezuma, Lax, McVeety, Mills, Perry, Schmidt, Whittle (Google)
sources.venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, Vol. 8, No. 12
sources.key_result: Formally separates Event Time ('the time at which the event itself actually occurred') from Processing Time ('the time at which an event is observed... during processing, within the pipeline'), and introduces the watermark as a heuristically-established lower bound on event-time completeness. Maps exactly onto Gridiron's book_updated_at (event time) vs received_at (processing/receipt time) vs the bug's misused requestedAt (neither).
sources.sample: Figure 2 / §1.3: real production watermark skew lags and catches up in bursts against wall-clock time rather than tracking it smoothly — the same shape as book-feeds.js's own measured OddsTrader staleness (Unibet median 288h stale).

sources.title: Temporal features in SQL:2011
sources.key_result: SQL:2011 adds temporal semantics without a new period data type: PERIOD FOR <name> (<start_col>,<end_col>) metadata on ordinary datetime columns. Two independent mechanisms — application-time period tables (user-set valid time) and system-versioned tables (system-set transaction time, old rows preserved with closed periods on UPDATE/DELETE, never overwritten) — combinable into a true bitemporal table. This is the exact 'retrofit without a rewrite' recipe the brief asked for.
sources.sample: UPDATE Emp FOR PORTION OF EPeriod FROM DATE '2011-02-03' TO DATE '2011-09-10' SET EDept=4 WHERE ENo=22217 — the DBMS automatically splits the row into up to three contiguous rows so no historical period is destroyed.

sources.title: Developing Time-Oriented Database Applications in SQL
sources.venue: Morgan Kaufmann (book, freely hosted by University of Arizona)
sources.key_result: Canonical textbook definition of valid-time state tables (FROM_DATE/TO_DATE recording when a fact was true in modeled reality) and the current/sequenced/nonsequenced query taxonomy that any real 'as of' query needs. Cited by both SQL:2011's authors and every bitemporal repo found.
sources.sample: Opens chapter 2 with the 1997 Hudson Foods E. coli recall: 25 million pounds of beef recalled at a cost of $25 million because no time-varying database could track which lots of meat were coresident with which, at what interval.

sources.title: Point-in-time feature joins
sources.key_result: Production AS-OF join pattern (filter to latest row with timestamp <= label_timestamp) structurally identical to Gridiron's bestExecutableQuote/quoteSurface. Read specifically to check for an event-time/receipt-time distinction and confirm there is none — the doc treats a single 'timestamp' column as authoritative for both purposes, which is the exact collapse that caused tonight's bug, making this a do-not-copy-verbatim reference rather than a fix source.

candidates.candidate: Split requestedAt from receivedAt in book-feeds.js's captureBookFeeds() and pass receivedAt/receiptClockSource through to ingestQuoteSnapshot
candidates.fixes_finding: book-feeds.js:390-419 computes `at` AFTER Promise.all resolves all provider fetches (a genuine post-response receipt time) but passes it only as `requestedAt` to ingestQuoteSnapshot (line 417), never as `receivedAt` — so every batch from the free-book-feeds path (the feed actually running live right now) is permanently labeled 'legacy_request_time_only' and every one of its quotes is thrown into availability_unknown by the T-60 packet, even though a good receipt time was already computed.
candidates.mechanism: Capture `const requestedAt = new Date().toISOString()` immediately before the `await Promise.all(...)` call (line 380) instead of only after; keep the existing post-await `at` as `receivedAt`; pass both plus `receiptClockSource: 'response_completion'` into ingestQuoteSnapshot at line 417, mirroring exactly what captureCurrentQuoteTape already does correctly at nfl-quote-tape.js:129-137.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/book-feeds.js lines 380 (add requestedAt capture), 390 (keep as receivedAt), 417 (pass receivedAt + receiptClockSource) — a ~4-line diff, no schema change, no migration needed since migration 032 already added the columns this fix would finally populate correctly for this feed.
candidates.expected_value: Every free-book-feeds batch captured from this point forward becomes eligible for `received_by_cutoff` in the T-60 packet instead of being auto-quarantined as availability_unknown — restores real evidence to the only feed currently running (paid Odds API credits are gone), with zero new infrastructure.
candidates.exit_test: Run captureBookFeeds() against a test DB; assert the resulting nfl_quote_batches row has receipt_clock_source='response_completion' and received_at > requested_at; assert nfl-t60-packet's realClock filter (line 214) includes rows from provider='free-book-feeds'.

candidates.candidate: Thread a real per-row receipt clock through nfl-quote-tape.js's unwrap() and add received_at/receipt_clock_source columns to nfl_quote_tape itself
candidates.fixes_finding: nfl-quote-tape.js's unwrap() (lines 35-41) sets the per-quote `snapshot_at` field — the only clock quoteSurface(), closingQuotes(), and bestExecutableQuote() filter or order on — from `requestedAt` unconditionally for 'current' (array) payloads, even when a correct `receivedAt` was passed into ingestQuoteSnapshot and stored on the batch. Migration 032 fixed the batch table; the per-row/per-query surface in the same file was never updated, so it silently still operates on request time.
candidates.mechanism: Pass `receivedAt` into `unwrap(payload, requestedAt, receivedAt)` and use it (falling back to requestedAt only when receivedAt is genuinely absent, exactly mirroring the batch-level contract) to set snapshotAt for current-mode payloads; add `received_at TEXT` and `receipt_clock_source TEXT` columns to the nfl_quote_tape CREATE TABLE in nfl-n-to-z.js (an ADD COLUMN, not a rewrite, matching the SQL:2011/temporal_tables retrofit pattern read in source 2); update quoteSurface/closingQuotes/bestExecutableQuote's `at` filters to compare against received_at directly instead of requiring a join back to nfl_quote_batches.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-quote-tape.js lines 35-41 (unwrap signature), 72 (call site), 111-120 (INSERT column list); server/db/schema/nfl-n-to-z.js lines 390-413 (nfl_quote_tape CREATE TABLE) plus a new migration file (033_...) following the exact pattern of 032_quote_receipt_clock.js, including its explicit refusal to backfill received_at on existing rows from requested_at.
candidates.expected_value: Closes the last place in the two named files where request-time can masquerade as receipt-time; makes quoteSurface/closingQuotes/bestExecutableQuote safe to wire into execution or backtest code (currently they have zero callers) without silently reintroducing the C11 look-ahead the moment someone does wire them in.
candidates.exit_test: New migration adds the two columns and a NOT NULL check going forward; a unit test inserts a quote batch with requestedAt < receivedAt and asserts bestExecutableQuote(at: <a time between the two>) returns null (not the row), proving the function can no longer be tricked by request time.

candidates.candidate: Give each provider in captureBookFeeds its own receipt timestamp instead of one shared post-Promise.all instant
candidates.fixes_finding: Extends the same book-feeds.js:390 defect: `at` is stamped once after the entire Promise.all settles, so a provider that resolved in 200ms (Pinnacle's fast guest API) is stamped with the same receipt time as one that took the full 25s timeout (a slow scrape) — collapsing 5 genuinely different receipt instants into one, understating freshness for fast providers.
candidates.mechanism: Record `Date.now()` inside each provider's own async wrapper (PROVIDERS[name]() call site, line 386) immediately on resolution, carry it through mergeQuotes() as a per-quote field, and use it as that quote's individual receivedAt instead of the batch-shared `at` — or, cheaper, split the single ingestQuoteSnapshot call per provider into 5 calls each with its own receivedAt.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/book-feeds.js lines 380-388 (per-provider timestamp capture), 411-419 (either per-provider ingestQuoteSnapshot calls or a per-quote receivedAt field threaded through mergeQuotes at line 389)
candidates.expected_value: Modest — the current single-timestamp-per-batch understates freshness (safe direction) rather than creating a look-ahead, so this tightens precision without fixing a correctness bug on its own; worth doing alongside F05-F1 since it is the same code region.
candidates.exit_test: Capture a live batch; assert Pinnacle's stored received_at differs from Bovada's received_at within the same captureBookFeeds() call by a nonzero amount matching their observed fetch latencies in the logs.

candidates.candidate: Add a migration-032-style guardrail test that fails CI if any ingestQuoteSnapshot call site omits receivedAt
candidates.fixes_finding: The root cause of F05-F1 is structural, not a one-off typo: ingestQuoteSnapshot's `receivedAt = null` default (nfl-quote-tape.js:61) makes 'forgot to pass receivedAt' silently valid and downgrades to legacy_request_time_only rather than erroring, so the same mistake can reappear at any future call site (a new provider feed, a new backfill script) with no signal.
candidates.mechanism: Add a lint/test rule (grep-based or an actual unit test enumerating every ingestQuoteSnapshot call site in the repo) asserting each production call site passes an explicit receivedAt and receiptClockSource, or add a loud console.warn/metrics counter inside ingestQuoteSnapshot itself whenever it falls back to legacy_request_time_only in a non-backfill context (sourceRef != a known historical/backfill ref).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: test/nfl-quote-tape.test.js (new test) or a small addition inside nfl-quote-tape.js's ingestQuoteSnapshot (lines 61-72) — a counter/log line, not a schema change
candidates.expected_value: Prevents F05-F1-shaped regressions from recurring silently the next time a new quote-producing feed is added; cheap insurance given this exact bug already slipped through one migration (032) undetected.
candidates.exit_test: Temporarily remove receivedAt from a captureBookFeeds()-style call in a test fixture; assert the new guardrail fails the test suite or emits the warning, rather than silently succeeding.

candidates.candidate: Formal correction/supersession chain for quote batches, modeled on SQL:2011 system-versioning and the pg_bitemporal correction pattern
candidates.mechanism: When a quote is discovered to be wrong (a scrape parsed a stale cached page, a book corrects a fat-fingered line) SQL:2011 system-versioned tables and pg_bitemporal's ll_bitemporal_correction_hist.sql both insert a new row/period that formally supersedes the old one, closing its system-time period rather than deleting or silently re-fetching over it — so a later query can ask both 'what did we believe as of decision time D' and 'what do we now know was actually true.' Gridiron's nfl_quote_tape is already append-only (triggers at nfl-n-to-z.js:811-814) but has no `supersedes_quote_id`/`corrected_by_batch_id` column at all — a bad quote just sits there forever with no link to whatever later corrected it.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a nullable `supersedes_quote_id TEXT REFERENCES nfl_quote_tape(quote_id)` column to nfl_quote_tape (nfl-n-to-z.js:390-413) and a small `correctQuote(oldQuoteId, newQuoteData)` helper in nfl-quote-tape.js that inserts the new row with the link set, leaving the old row physically untouched (consistent with the existing immutability triggers).
candidates.expected_value: Turns 'a quote was wrong' from an invisible, untraceable event into an auditable one — directly useful for the audit-registry.js / decision-basis.js governance surfaces mentioned in tonight's findings, without which a wrong price and its correction look identical to two independent, unrelated market moves.
candidates.exit_test: Insert a quote, then insert a corrected one with supersedes_quote_id set; assert a query 'what was known as of T1' (before correction) returns the original and 'what is now known to have been true at T1' (after correction, via the chain) returns the corrected value — the exact sequenced-vs-nonsequenced distinction from Snodgrass ch.2.

candidates.candidate: A shared PIT (point-in-time) contract module + audit script enforcing the three-clock discipline across every timestamp column in the schema
candidates.mechanism: SQL:2011 and the Dataflow paper both name exactly three roles a timestamp column can play (event/valid time, transaction/receipt time, and — as this bug shows — an illegitimate fourth, 'request time,' that must never stand in for either). Gridiron's own T-60 packet code already juggles at least 6 differently-named columns doing these jobs ad hoc: modified_at, first_seen_time, fetched_at (nfl-t60-packet.js:253,267,285), snapshot_at, book_updated_at, captured_at (book-feeds.js/nfl-quote-tape.js) — with no shared module declaring which clock each one is, so the exact confusion tonight's bug exemplifies can and will recur table by table.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/pit-contract.js exporting a documented enum {EVENT, RECEIPT} and a small schema-audit script (`scripts/audit-pit-columns.mjs`) that walks server/db/schema/*.js, flags every TEXT column matching /_at$|_time$/ and requires it be registered with a declared clock role in a manifest file — CI fails if a new timestamp column is added without being classified.
candidates.expected_value: Systemic, not a one-table patch: makes the receipt-clock bug class visible and checkable everywhere at once (injuries, news, forecasts, quote tape) instead of relying on someone reading every file by hand the way this research pass had to.
candidates.exit_test: Run the audit script against the current schema; it should flag nfl_quote_tape's snapshot_at as unclassified/ambiguous today, and pass clean once F05-F2's new received_at column is registered with role RECEIPT and book_updated_at with role EVENT.

candidates.candidate: Per-provider coverage watermark on each quote batch, modeled on Dataflow's watermark concept
candidates.mechanism: The Dataflow paper's watermark is an explicit, queryable answer to 'how complete is our picture of event time X' rather than silently treating missing data as absent data. Gridiron's captureBookFeeds() already computes exactly the raw ingredients for this (errors{} and byProvider{} at book-feeds.js:379-388: which providers succeeded, which backed off, which threw) but discards them after logging — nothing downstream can tell 'Kambi had no line' apart from 'Kambi's poll failed and we don't actually know.'
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Persist `byProvider`/`errors` per batch as a new `nfl_quote_batch_coverage` table (batch_id, provider, status: succeeded|backed_off|failed, error_message) written alongside the existing nfl_quote_batches INSERT at book-feeds.js:417-419; expose a `coverageAsOf(batchId)` helper in nfl-quote-tape.js.
candidates.expected_value: Lets the T-60 packet (or a human) distinguish 'the market had no edge here' from 'we don't actually know what the market thought here' — directly relevant to the staking-guardrail work already flagged in the betting model findings, since an honest 'we don't know' should never be silently treated as 'no signal, skip.'
candidates.exit_test: Force a synthetic provider failure in a test run of captureBookFeeds(); assert nfl_quote_batch_coverage records status='failed' for that provider and that a downstream consumer calling coverageAsOf() can distinguish it from a provider that genuinely returned zero events.

candidates.candidate: Wire nfl-replay.js / backtest.js through a bitemporal-aware AS-OF quote join instead of joining off whatever the season manifest happens to store
candidates.mechanism: Feature-store point-in-time joins (Databricks/Feast pattern read in source 4) exist precisely so a backtest cannot leak a same-day corrected value into a historical evaluation. Gridiron's quoteSurface/closingQuotes/bestExecutableQuote (nfl-quote-tape.js:175-221) already implement almost this shape but — per the grep in this research pass — have zero callers anywhere, including nfl-replay.js and backtest.js, which is a real, confirmed capability gap: the backtest harness and the point-in-time quote surface exist in the same codebase today and have never been connected.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-replay.js and server/services/backtest.js — replace whatever direct table reads currently source historical closing/executable lines with calls to closingQuotes()/bestExecutableQuote(at: <backtest decision instant>) from nfl-quote-tape.js, once F05-F2's per-row receipt clock lands underneath them.
candidates.expected_value: Speculative until F05-F2 lands (these functions are not yet trustworthy for this purpose) but the connection itself is cheap once the clock is fixed, and closes a real, confirmed gap: two systems (backtest harness, PIT quote surface) built independently in the same repo that have never been wired together.
candidates.exit_test: Run one existing backtest season through the new join path and confirm ROI/CLV output is bit-identical to the current path for periods with no corrections, then confirm it differs (correctly, in the conservative direction) for any period containing a known bad-quote correction once F05-N1 exists.
