repos.what_it_does: Postgres C extension providing a generic `versioning(system_period_col, history_table, adjust)` trigger fired BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE that automatically archives the pre-change row into a history table and stamps the live row's system-time period — the canonical 'retrofit without a rewrite' recipe: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN + CREATE TABLE ... LIKE + attach trigger, no existing data touched.
repos.adoption_path: Gridiron runs node:sqlite, not Postgres, so the extension itself cannot be installed. Borrow the trigger+history-table shape in plain SQLite DDL for any table that needs true system-versioning beyond the simple append-only-abort triggers Gridiron already has on nfl_quote_batches/nfl_quote_tape.

repos.what_it_does: PL/pgSQL framework for full bitemporal tables (valid-time AND system-time together) with explicit correction functions (ll_bitemporal_correction_hist.sql) that insert a new, superseding row rather than mutating history.
repos.adoption_path: Unmaintained 4+ years and Postgres-specific; read purely for the correction-chain pattern behind candidate F05-N1 (a correction is a new row that logically supersedes, never overwrites, the old one) — not something to depend on or port.

repos.what_it_does: Full bitemporal Datalog/SQL database where every query is parameterized by both a valid-time-as-of and a system(transaction)-time-as-of independently, with built-in time-travel queries.
repos.adoption_path: Too large a dependency to adopt for one table; used here only as the correct mental model for what quoteSurface(at: atTime)'s single `atTime` parameter should really be — two independent as-of parameters, not one conflated clock.

do_not_do: Do not backfill received_at on existing nfl_quote_tape rows from snapshot_at/requested_at — migration 032's own comment explains why this is the identical defect written into data instead of query; the same argument applies one level down at the per-row grain.

Do not adopt a Postgres bitemporal extension (temporal_tables, pg_bitemporal) as a runtime dependency — Gridiron runs node:sqlite with no Postgres migration in scope; borrow the DDL pattern in plain SQLite instead.

Do not copy a feature-store single-timestamp AS-OF join (Databricks/Feast pattern) verbatim — it does not distinguish event time from receipt time and would silently reintroduce the exact collapse that caused tonight's bug.

Do not lift or modify the nfl_quote_batches/nfl_quote_tape immutability triggers to allow in-place correction of a bad quote — the correction pattern is always a new, correctly-clocked superseding row, never an UPDATE.
Do not touch, query against, or run migrations on the live fantasy-football-dashboard database tonight — it is read-only for this research pass and is actively capturing Week 1 games through Sunday.

Do not treat F05-N4 (wiring the backtest harness to the PIT quote surface) as safe to do before F05-F2 lands — doing so would let a backtest quietly trust the still-request-time-tainted snapshot_at clock.

result.label: F01: Drive-sim mechanics — state encoding & transitions
result.summary: Verified all 6 tonight's-findings defects directly in nfl-drive-sim.js/nfl-sim-policy.js/nfl-live.js by grep+read (not from memory): turnover field position is never mirrored (100-yard) on change of possession; policies divide a half-scoped clock by 3600 (full-game denominator); the kneel threshold rises with MORE opponent timeouts (backwards) and timeouts are computed by timeoutPolicy but the result is discarded — never decremented anywhere in the file; away-team win-probability calls pass a possession-flipped lead against an unflipped home-anchored spread into a function whose own docstring requires both in the same (home) frame; home-field advantage is a single post-hoc Bernoulli(homeFieldPoints/7)->+7 coin flip after the game is already final; the season-remainder resimulation path is a separate, simpler copy of the game loop with no halftime or overtime transition at all. Read 3 primary sources in full (NFLSimulatoR: empirical-resampling drives, 48k plays/season 2009-2019, 10k-drive fourth-down comparison with real 95% CIs against the actual-NFL-coaching benchmark; iWinRNFL: fixed-home-perspective logistic WP model, 295,844 plays, Brier 0.158 vs 0.26 climatology baseline, calibration slope 0.98; nflWAR: explicit half-vs-game clock domains, kneels hard-coded EP=0, LOSO-CV calibration error 0.013 on 304,896 plays) plus Goldner's Markov-drive paper cited but not independently read (paywalled). Cloned and grepped 3 GitHub repos directly (not README claims): rtelmore/NFLSimulatoR and tim-foldy-porto/nflsim both independently apply `100 - yard` on turnover exactly where Gridiron fails to; tim-foldy-porto/nflsim's clock.py/game_state.py is a clean single-clock-domain, explicit-halftime/OT state machine with kneel=40s-one-snap and a def_timeouts==0 kneel gate (correct direction); martineastwood/penaltyblog's Elo class adds home_field_advantage as continuous rating points before computing win probability, never as a post-hoc score bonus. 4 fix candidates map 1:1 onto the 6 named defects (turnover mirror; canonical clock unit; kneel/timeout state-machine repair; WP reference-frame + continuous HFA + halftime/OT-complete season-remainder loop). 4 new candidates add capabilities Gridiron has none of: an independent (non-self-referential) EP-surface calibration audit against real play-by-play; an empirical-resampling cross-check simulator; a team-specific decaying Elo-style HFA rating; and a Markov-chain absorbing-state audit of the simulator's aggregate output.

sources.title: Simulation-Based Decision Making in the NFL using NFLSimulatoR
sources.authors: Benjamin Williams, Will Palmquist, Ryan Elmore
sources.sample: NFL play-by-play 2009-2019 via nflscrapR/nflfastR, ~48,000 plays/season; worked example: 10,000 simulated single-drives from 2018-2019 data starting 1st-and-10 from the 25
sources.key_result: Table 1: mean simulated points/drive by fourth-down sub-strategy with 95% CIs — Always Go 2.28 (2.22,2.35), Empirical (status-quo NFL behavior) 1.96, Expected Points 2.19, Never Go 2.03, Go-if-<5yds 2.24 — a genuine comparison against the real NFL-coaching behavioral benchmark, not a market-beating claim. Core method: sample_play()/sample_drives() directly resample real historical plays matching (down, distance, yardline) rather than a parametric play model.

sources.title: iWinRNFL: A Simple, Interpretable & Well-Calibrated In-Game Win Probability Model for NFL
sources.sample: NFL Game Center play-by-play (nflgame), 2009-2015 regular season, 1,792 games, 295,844 plays
sources.key_result: Logistic model fixed to Pr[home wins]; every covariate (score diff, rating diff, timeouts, possession, down/field-position interactions) expressed in the SAME home-team reference frame. Brier score 0.158 vs 0.26 climatology baseline; 76.5% accuracy; calibration curve slope 0.98 (95% CI [0.97,1.01]), intercept ~0.008 — essentially the y=x line. More complex non-linear models (naive Bayes, 2-hidden-layer FNN) on the same features gave no material improvement (Brier 0.163, 0.156) — reference-frame discipline mattered more than model complexity.

sources.title: nflWAR: A Reproducible Method for Offensive Player Evaluation in Football (Extended Edition)
sources.authors: Ronald Yurko, Samuel Ventura, Maksim Horowitz
sources.venue: arXiv preprint (Carnegie Mellon Dept. of Statistics & Data Science)
sources.sample: 304,896 non-PAT plays, NFL 2009-2016 via nflscrapR
sources.key_result: Explicit statement that game clock is 3600s (4 quarters + halftime + potential OT) at the game level while the EP model's own 'Seconds' feature is scoped to seconds-remaining-in-HALF because its 7-way next-score response is itself half-scoped; QB kneels excluded and hard-coded EP=0 as a named special case. Leave-one-season-out CV calibration error e ≈ 0.013 across all 7 scoring events (vs 0.022 for a rejected ordinal alternative) — a genuine out-of-sample, non-self-referential EP fit, unlike Gridiron's EP surface which is generated by running its own simulator to convergence.

sources.title: A Markov Model of Football: Using Stochastic Processes to Model a Football Drive
sources.venue: Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports
sources.sample: not verified independently — paywalled; description sourced from its own abstract and citations by nflWAR/NFLSimulatoR
sources.key_result: Cited (not independently verified) as the origin of modeling a drive as an absorbing Markov chain over (down, distance, yardline) states with touchdown/field-goal/safety as absorbing boundaries, used to derive expected points and time-to-absorption in closed form — the formalism nflWAR and NFLSimulatoR both build on.

repos.what_it_does: R package (companion code to the NFLSimulatoR paper above) that simulates NFL drives by resampling real historical plays matching (down, distance, yardline) from nflscrapR data rather than generating outcomes parametrically.
repos.adoption_path: R/sample_drives.R:82 does `new_yfog <- 100 - new_yfog` on change of possession — the exact field-position mirror Gridiron's nfl-drive-sim.js:345-346/536 is missing (defect 1, independent confirmation #1). R/down_distance_updater.R:33-34 also shows guarding field position into [5,90] before sampling near the goal line, worth mirroring as edge-case discipline.

repos.what_it_does: From-scratch Python NFL game/drive simulator: explicit engine package (game.py, game_state.py, clock.py, rules.py, play_resolver.py, special_teams.py) plus team-ratings and season/playoff simulation.
repos.adoption_path: Three separate, directly-portable patterns for nfl-drive-sim.js: (1) rules.py:184-201 _apply_turnover() mirrors field position (`100 - fumble_spot`) exactly like (i) above — independent confirmation #2, in a different codebase/language, of the fix for defect 1. (2) clock.py + game_state.py's single quarter/quarter_seconds_remaining state machine with named Phase enum (KICKOFF/NORMAL/PAT/OVERTIME/GAME_OVER) and transition_quarter()/_halftime()/_start_overtime() — the pattern to replace Gridiron's ad hoc half-seconds-divided-by-3600 bug (defect 2) and its halftime/OT-less season-remainder loop (defect 6) with one shared state machine. (3) play_resolver.py:76-82 choose_play()'s `def_timeouts == 0` kneel gate (correct direction) and clock.py's kneel=40s-one-snap runoff directly inform the kneel/timeout fix (defect 3). No HFA model exists in this repo (grepped, zero hits) — not a source for defect 5.

repos.what_it_does: General sports-modeling Python library (soccer-focused: Elo, Poisson, Dixon-Coles, etc.); fetched penaltyblog/ratings/elo.py directly via `gh api` rather than cloning the whole package.
repos.adoption_path: penaltyblog/ratings/elo.py:15-42 — Elo(k, home_field_advantage) adds HFA as continuous rating points to the home team's rating BEFORE computing win probability (`r_home = rating + hfa`, then logistic on the difference), never as a post-hoc score bonus. Architectural template for fixing nfl-drive-sim.js:562's `random() < homeFieldPoints/7 -> +7` coin flip (defect 5) and for the new team-specific/decaying HFA candidate (N4).

candidates.candidate: Mirror field position on every turnover: replace nfl-drive-sim.js:345-346's bare `endYard: clamp(yard,1,99)` with the new-possessing-team's perspective, and stop re-using d.endYard unflipped at the two possession-change sites (:536, :825).
candidates.fixes_finding: turnovers handed to the wrong team's field position
candidates.mechanism: On the shared turnover return path, compute `endYard: clamp(100 - yard, 1, 99)` for the new offense's spot (adjusting further for return yardage on interceptions/fumble recoveries the same way tim-foldy-porto/nflsim's rules.py:184-201 does: `100 - spot + return_yards`), and remove the now-redundant unflipped assignment at the two call sites that consume d.endYard as the next possession's `yard`.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js:345-346 (shared turnover return), :536 and :825 (possession-change assignment of `yard` from `d.endYard`)
candidates.expected_value: Removes a systematic ~(2*deviation-from-midfield) yard bias in favor of whichever team just turned the ball over on every simulated possession change — this single bug alone can shift simulated scoring distributions and therefore any spread/total priced off this simulator, in the same direction, on every game.
candidates.exit_test: Unit test: force a turnover at offense-yard 70 (deep in opponent territory) and assert the new offense's starting `yard` is 30, not 70; re-run epFor() and confirm the EP-by-field-position curve becomes monotonically flatter near midfield (the current bug artificially inflates EP for teams that just forced a takeaway near their own goal line).

candidates.candidate: Adopt one canonical clock unit end to end: either re-scope nfl-sim-policy.js's urgency/late-game formulas to the half (divide by HALF=1800, matching what secondsLeft actually is), or thread an explicit game-level `secondsElapsedInGame` alongside half-seconds so 3600-denominator formulas get the right numerator.
candidates.fixes_finding: policies receive half-game-clock seconds but are written for full-game-clock
candidates.mechanism: Mirror tim-foldy-porto/nflsim's clock.py/game_state.py pattern: define the clock's domain once (a `quarter`/`half` counter plus a seconds-remaining-in-that-period value, per nflWAR Table 2's explicit 'seconds remaining in half' feature) and never divide that value by a denominator from a different domain. Concretely: nfl-sim-policy.js:214 (`varianceProfile`) and :415 (`gameScriptPassRate`) both compute `urgency = clamp(1 - secondsLeft/3600, 0, 1)` against a secondsLeft that is capped at 1800 (HALF) everywhere it's produced in nfl-drive-sim.js — change the denominator to HALF (1800) so urgency is 0 at kickoff of a half and 1 at its end, matching every other half-scoped policy in the same file (e.g. twoPointDecision's own `late = secondsLeft < 900` comment: 'the chart only really binds in the second half' — already correctly half-scoped).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-sim-policy.js:214, :415 (urgency formulas); server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js:48 (HALF=1800) and every secondsLeft producer in simulateGame (:459-537) and the season-remainder loop (:799-829)
candidates.expected_value: Removes a constant ~0.5 urgency offset present at the start of every half in variance-profile and pass-rate policies — these feed play-calling aggressiveness and score variance for the entire first 6-7 minutes of every half in every simulated game, i.e. roughly a quarter of all simulated game-time is currently mis-calibrated toward 'late-game desperation' behavior it shouldn't have yet.
candidates.exit_test: Assert `varianceProfile({lead:0, secondsLeft:1800, spread:null}).urgency === 0` (kickoff of a half) rather than the current 0.5; spot-check that early-half (secondsLeft near 1800) simulated pass rates/variance now resemble first-quarter empirical NFL rates rather than a blend already halfway toward end-of-half behavior.

candidates.candidate: Repair the kneel/timeout state machine: invert kneelDecision's dependence on opponent timeouts, cap a single kneel to one realistic runoff instead of the whole remaining clock, and actually apply timeoutPolicy's spend decision to the timeouts object.
candidates.fixes_finding: the kneel rule is inverted and timeouts never decrement so any leading team burns an entire half
candidates.mechanism: (1) In nfl-sim-policy.js:291-304, change `kneelable = 40 + timeouts*40` (opponent timeouts) to decrease, not increase, with more opponent timeouts remaining — e.g. gate on `oppTimeouts === 0` inside the two-minute-drill window the way tim-foldy-porto/nflsim's play_resolver.py:82 does (`def_timeouts == 0 and down <= 3`), rather than a monotonically-increasing threshold in the wrong direction. (2) In nfl-drive-sim.js's kneel branch (:266-268), return a single ~40-second runoff (`seconds: 40`, matching tim-foldy-porto/nflsim's clock.py CLOCK_RUNOFF for a kneel play) and let the surrounding while-loop (:465-537) call kneelDecision again on the next iteration, instead of consuming `secondsLeft` in full in one call. (3) Wire the discarded `to = P.timeoutPolicy(...)` result (nfl-drive-sim.js:475) back into `timeouts[possession or defense]` when `to.call === 'spend'`, so the timeouts object set up at :453/:461 actually changes during a half instead of only being reset between halves.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-sim-policy.js:291-328 (kneelDecision, timeoutPolicy); server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js:265-268 (kneel branch), :453,:461,:475 (timeouts object and discarded `to` result)
candidates.expected_value: This is likely the single highest-value fix in the set: because timeouts never decrement, the current simulator effectively gives every leading team an infinite defensive-timeout-free clock-kill and every trailing team zero ability to stop the clock — end-of-half and end-of-game win-probability dynamics (exactly what feeds fourth-down/onside decisions and, downstream, garbage-time scoring variance) are structurally wrong in every simulated game, not an edge case.
candidates.exit_test: Simulate a synthetic drive where the offense leads by 4 with 2:00 left, ball on its own 30, defense holding 3 timeouts: assert the engine does NOT call kneel on 1st down (defense can still get the ball back with all 3 stops) and that `timeouts.away` (the defense) drops after each defensive-timeout call in the log; re-run and confirm a leading team facing a 0-timeout defense DOES correctly kneel out with materially less time left than one facing a 3-timeout defense.

candidates.candidate: Fix win-probability reference frame (flip spread's sign to match possession-relative lead at every wp()/liveWinProbability call site), replace the post-hoc HFA coin flip with a continuous pre-draw nudge, and give the season-remainder simulator the same halftime/OT-aware loop simulateGame already has.
candidates.fixes_finding: away-team win-probability uses the home spread; home-field advantage is a flat 7-point post-OT lump distorting the key-number distribution; the season-remainder simulator has no halftime or overtime at all
candidates.mechanism: (a) At every nfl-sim-policy.js call into liveWinProbability with a possession-relative `lead` (fourthDownByWinProbability :115, onsideDecision :178-180, varianceProfile :213), pass `possession === 'home' ? spread : -spread` instead of the raw spread — matching liveWinProbability's own documented contract (nfl-live.js:61-66: lead and spread must share the home reference frame), the exact discipline iWinRNFL's fixed-home-perspective model enforces throughout. (b) Replace nfl-drive-sim.js:562's `random() < homeFieldPoints/7 -> home += 7` with a small continuous shift applied to the home team's scoring rate/rating BEFORE any drive is drawn (penaltyblog elo.py:24-42 pattern: HFA as points added to the rating pre-draw, not a discrete post-hoc bonus), so it affects the natural shape of the score distribution instead of adding one artificial lump at exactly 7 points after the final whistle. (c) Refactor the season-remainder path (nfl-drive-sim.js:799-829) to call the same halftime/OT-aware loop simulateGame already implements (:446-565), parameterized by a live starting state, instead of maintaining a second simpler copy with hardcoded `timeouts: 3/3` and no half or OT transition.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-sim-policy.js:108-121,170-180,212-214 (wp/liveWinProbability call sites); server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js:562 (HFA coin flip); server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js:799-829 vs :446-565 (season-remainder loop vs simulateGame)
candidates.expected_value: (a) corrects every away-team fourth-down/onside/variance decision in every simulated game — roughly half of all possessions. (b) removes a discrete artifact at exactly the 3/7 key numbers the betting-model stack is most sensitive to. (c) means any live/in-week resimulation (the surface most likely to be used for real-time decisions during Sunday games, per the read-only server currently capturing Week 1) can silently run through a tied score at halftime or full-time with no OT, which will misprice moneyline/spread outcomes specifically in close, ongoing games.
candidates.exit_test: (a) Assert an away-team fourth-down decision with lead=-3 and a home-favorite spread=-7 produces the same win-probability-implied value as the mathematically equivalent home-team call with lead=+3, spread=-7 (mirror symmetry). (b) Histogram simulated home-vs-away margins over 100k games and confirm no artificial 7-point spike distinct from the natural scoring distribution. (c) Force the season-remainder path to start at a tied score with 1:00 left in a half and assert it transitions to half 2 (or OT if tied at end of regulation) rather than terminating the loop at clock<=0 with a final tied score.

candidates.candidate: Independent, non-self-referential expected-points calibration audit: fit a real next-score classifier directly on Gridiron's own 251,591-row play-by-play table (nflWAR's 7-way multinomial: TD/FG/safety/no-score/opp-safety/opp-FG/opp-TD within the same half) and diff it against the simulator-generated epFor() surface.
candidates.mechanism: Replicate nflWAR's method exactly: multinomial logistic regression on (down, seconds-remaining-in-half, yardline, log(yards-to-go), goal-to-go indicator, under-two-minutes indicator) with the interactions the paper found best (log(YTG)×Down, Yardline×Down, log(YTG)×GTG), trained on Gridiron's real play-by-play, evaluated with leave-one-season-out CV, and report the same bin-wise calibration error metric (e = mean weighted |predicted−observed| per 5%-probability-bin) nflWAR reports (e≈0.013 there). Then diff this real-data EP-by-field-position curve against nfl-drive-sim.js's self-generated epFor() surface (:578-588) at every yard line — any large divergence is direct evidence the simulator's generative process (including any of defects 1-6, fixed or not) has drifted from what real football actually produces, something the current self-consistent-by-construction design can never detect on its own.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New module alongside server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js; reads the existing play-by-play table (251,591 rows, per tonight's findings) that currently 'is used only for hand-built features, never sequence models'; output compared against epFor()'s cached `_epSurface` (nfl-drive-sim.js:569-588)
candidates.expected_value: A standing regression test for the entire drive-simulator, cheap to re-run after every future change to nfl-drive-sim.js/nfl-sim-policy.js, that catches state-encoding bugs like tonight's 6 findings automatically instead of requiring a manual code read to discover them.
candidates.exit_test: Run once before any of the F1-F4 fixes land (baseline calibration error, likely large given the known bugs) and again after — a successful fix set should visibly shrink the divergence between the real-data EP curve and the simulator's own epFor() surface, especially near midfield where the turnover-mirror bug (F1) most distorts things.

candidates.candidate: Empirical-resampling drive simulator (NFLSimulatoR-style direct historical-play resampling) run alongside the existing parametric engine on the same real play-by-play, as an independent cross-check of mean/variance per starting field position — not a replacement.
candidates.mechanism: Port the core of rtelmore/NFLSimulatoR's sample_play()/sample_drives()/down_distance_updater() logic (resample a real historical play matching current down/distance/yardline, with the paper's own fallback of widening the yardline window when a combination is sparse) against Gridiron's real play-by-play table, and compare its drive-level point/turnover-rate distribution to nfl-drive-sim.js's simulateDrive() output at matched starting conditions. Because this method never touches any of nfl-drive-sim.js's own policy functions, it cannot inherit any of defects 1-6 — it is a ground-truth check independent of the code being audited.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New standalone script reading the play-by-play table used elsewhere in server/services/; compared against server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js's simulateDrive() at the same (down=1,toGo=10,yard=25) starting condition the epFor() surface already uses (:583)
candidates.expected_value: A second, methodologically independent sanity check beyond N1's parametric-vs-real comparison — catches the case where a fitted classifier (N1) happens to share a blind spot with the simulator, since resampling has no functional form to get wrong.
candidates.exit_test: Compare mean points-per-drive from 10,000 resampled drives (matching the NFLSimulatoR paper's own protocol) starting at the 25 against nfl-drive-sim.js's simulateDrive() at the same starting spot; flag if the two disagree by more than the resampling method's own 95% CI width.

candidates.candidate: Team-specific, decaying Elo-style home-field-advantage rating (continuous points, updated per season/game) to replace the single global homeFieldPoints scalar with something that actually varies by matchup.
candidates.mechanism: Adopt penaltyblog's Elo pattern (`r_home = rating + hfa`) but make `hfa` itself a per-team (or per-stadium) tracked quantity that decays/updates the way a real Elo rating would, rather than the single constant `homeFieldPoints` value passed into simulateGame today — capturing real known effects (altitude, travel distance, crowd, rest differential) that a flat league-wide constant cannot. This is distinct from fix F4(b), which only moves the existing single scalar from a post-hoc coin flip to a continuous pre-draw nudge without addressing that it is still one number for all 32 teams.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Extends whatever object simulateGame's `homeFieldPoints` parameter currently comes from (nfl-drive-sim.js:447,562) into a per-team-tracked value; would sit alongside, not replace, the team-strength ratings work already flagged for a separate researcher
candidates.expected_value: Marginal on top of F4(b) alone, but the natural next step once HFA is continuous at all — real HFA is known to vary meaningfully by team (dome vs. cold-weather road teams, high-altitude Denver, short-week/travel situations) and a single global constant leaves that variance on the table.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest simulated home-team margins against actual closing-line HFA components (where available) for at least 3 seasons and confirm team-specific HFA estimates correlate with published third-party HFA rankings (e.g. nfelo's HFA tracker) better than the current flat constant does.

candidates.candidate: Absorbing-Markov-chain audit of the simulator's aggregate drive outcomes (Goldner's formalism) as a closed-form cross-check on epFor()'s value-iteration result.
candidates.mechanism: Independently of N1's fitted classifier, build a small absorbing Markov chain over a coarsened (down, distance-bucket, yardline-bucket) state space using Gridiron's own per-play transition rates (already computed inside simulateDrive's per-play resolver), with touchdown/field-goal/safety as absorbing states, and solve for expected points and absorption probabilities in closed form the way Goldner (2012) describes — then compare against nfl-drive-sim.js's Monte-Carlo epFor() surface (:578-588). A closed-form solve has no sampling noise, so any persistent gap versus the Monte-Carlo surface at a given field position is either a value-iteration convergence issue (trials=200 at :586 may be too few) or a modeling inconsistency, and this method distinguishes the two in a way N1 (fit on real data) cannot.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New analysis script consuming the same per-play rate parameters simulateDrive() builds from buildContext() (nfl-drive-sim.js, upstream of :578); compared against the cached `_epSurface` from epFor()
candidates.expected_value: Lower confidence than N1/N2 since it depends on faithfully coarsening Gridiron's continuous rate model into discrete Markov states without losing the effects that matter — mainly useful as a fast sanity check on epFor()'s Monte-Carlo trial count (currently 200, per :586) rather than as a primary audit.
candidates.exit_test: Confirm the closed-form Markov EP at the 25-yard line falls within the Monte-Carlo epFor() surface's own resampled confidence interval; if not, first raise epFor()'s trials count and re-check before treating it as a modeling bug.

do_not_do: Do not fix the kneel/timeout bug by capping kneelable at a small constant — the defect is a wrong sign on the opponent-timeout term's direction of effect, not a missing bound; a cap papers over the relationship instead of correcting it.

Do not special-case the turnover field-position mirror per turnover type (interception vs fumble) — nfl-drive-sim.js:345-346 is a single shared return path; apply `100 - yard` there once, not duplicated per branch.

Do not replace the parametric drive engine with an empirical-resampling model (N2) as the primary simulator — it cannot easily be conditioned on team/week-specific context the way the tunable parametric engine can, and reintroduces the sparse-combination problem the NFLSimulatoR paper itself flags. Use resampling only as an independent audit.

Do not implement continuous HFA (F4b) as a single still-global scalar just moved earlier in the pipeline — that keeps the 'one number for all 32 teams' problem defect 5 already has; team-specific variation (N3) is what actually makes continuity worth doing.

Do not change liveWinProbability's function contract (nfl-live.js:61-66) — its home-perspective, ESPN-sign-convention docstring is already correct and matches iWinRNFL's discipline. The bug is entirely in nfl-sim-policy.js's call sites passing mismatched arguments; fix the call sites, not the function.

Do not assume fixing these 6 mechanics moves the nfl-ensemble.js -2.28 CLV or its 78% adverse-move rate — that is a separate, already-diagnosed defect in the ensemble's blend weights, untouched by this research.
Do not run, build, test, or execute anything in fantasy-football-dashboard — it is read-only tonight with a live server capturing Week 1 games; all findings here came from grep/read only.

result.label: Trial registry + multiplicity correction (Holm/DSR/PBO) for the 21-model search
result.summary: audit-registry.js is a well-built preregistration system (Šidák correction + mSPRT always-valid p-value) that is completely orphaned: grep finds zero callers of preregister()/runAudit() outside its own file and test, so it never touched the actual "0 of 21 models beat 15,096 closing lines" search, the "9 signal families degraded under ablation" search, or the "24 candidates x 4 stats, zero survivors" search — all currently just prose in WORK_LOG.md/path-to-profit-measurements.md with no p-value, no Holm/Bonferroni correction, no deflated Sharpe, no PBO. Worse, there are THREE independent, uncoordinated code/data-freeze hashers (audit-registry.js's codeHash()/dataSignature(), nfl-blind-audit.js's repositoryState()/inputMutationState(), and platform/code-identity.js's correct transitive-import hasher, which explicitly critiques a fourth one in nfl-replay.js) and a fourth trial-adjacent structure (nfl-experiments.js's nfl_model_experiments table) with zero multiplicity correction of any kind. Confirmed via grep: no Holm-Bonferroni, deflated Sharpe ratio, or PBO/CSCV implementation exists anywhere in the codebase, despite server/data/market-lab and tree-lab already containing exactly the per-configuration trial matrices CSCV is built to consume. Read four primary sources in full — Bailey & Lopez de Prado's Deflated Sharpe Ratio (2014), Bailey/Borwein/Lopez de Prado/Zhu's Probability of Backtest Overfitting via CSCV (2015, with its own worked example: N=8,800 configs, S=16, PBO=55% for a spurious strategy vs 13% for a genuine one), Holm's original 1979 sequentially-rejective procedure (proven never less powerful than Bonferroni, with its own 0.439-vs-0.565 worked example), and Harvey & Liu's 2015 "Backtesting" paper, which is the direct answer to "how do you retrofit a haircut onto results that already exist" (worked Bonferroni/Holm/BHY example on 6 p-values, plus a haircut-Sharpe example: T=240, SR=0.75, N=200 trials -> ~60% haircut). Six candidates follow, three fixing the named defect directly (retrofit Holm+DSR onto the 21-model search; consolidate the three hashers; backfill the historical trial count) and three genuinely new capabilities the codebase has none of (PBO/CSCV against existing trial-lab data; a reusable Deflated Sharpe primitive; the actual research_trials table the task names as the end goal).

sources.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
sources.authors: David H. Bailey, Marcos Lopez de Prado
sources.key_result: Derives E[max SR_n] under N independent null trials via the Euler-Mascheroni-constant expected-maximum formula (eq.1), then defines DSR = PSR(SR0) using that expected-max as the null baseline, adjusted for sample skew/kurtosis (eq.2); numerical Exhibit shows the expected maximum grows steadily with N even at true mean SR=0 for N in [10,1000].
sources.sample: Theoretical + numerical exhibit (E[SR]=0, V[SR]=1, N in [10,1000]); no single empirical dataset.

sources.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
sources.authors: David H. Bailey, Jonathan M. Borwein, Marcos Lopez de Prado, Qiji Jim Zhu
sources.venue: Journal of Computational Finance (SSRN working paper, rev. Feb 2015)
sources.key_result: Defines PBO and the CSCV algorithm (partition T x N trial matrix into S=16 slices, form all C(16,8)=12,780 IS/OOS combinations, logit of OOS relative rank). Worked example: N=8,800 parameter configs, T=1,000 daily prices; spurious seasonal strategy has all-positive IS Sharpes (1.0-2.2, best SR=1.27, PSR-stat 2.83) but PBO=55% and 53% of OOS Sharpes negative; a genuine-effect control case has PBO=13%.
sources.sample: N=8,800 backtested parameter configurations of a 4-parameter monthly trading rule over T=1,000 simulated daily prices (~4 years), S=16 CSCV partitions.

sources.title: A Simple Sequentially Rejective Multiple Test Procedure
sources.key_result: Proves the step-down procedure (compare ordered p-values to alpha/n, alpha/(n-1), ... alpha/1) controls FWER at level alpha (Theorem 1) and is never less powerful than classical Bonferroni since its comparison constants are uniformly >= alpha/n. Worked example: 10 independent N(mu,1) tests with 4 true mu=6, 2 true mu=3, 4 true mu=0 at alpha=0.05 -- classical Bonferroni rejects both mu=3 hypotheses with probability 0.439, sequentially rejective (Holm) rejects both with probability 0.565.
sources.sample: Analytical proof plus a 10-hypothesis Monte-Carlo-style worked numeric example (4 mu=6.0, 2 mu=3.0, 4 mu=0.0, N(mu,1)).

sources.title: Backtesting
sources.key_result: Direct methodology for retrofitting a haircut onto an existing single test statistic: converts Sharpe to t-ratio, computes multiple-testing-adjusted p-value p^M = 1-(1-p^S)^N for independent trials, solves for haircut Sharpe HSR. Worked example: T=240 (20yr monthly), SR=0.75, single-test p=0.0008; at N=200 assumed trials p^M=0.15, haircut annual SR falls to 0.32 (~60% haircut). Fully worked Bonferroni/Holm/BHY comparison on M=6 ordered p-values (0.005-0.06): Bonferroni finds 1/6 significant, Holm 2/6, BHY 4/6. Exhibit 1 applies this to three published factors (E/P, momentum, BAB) at N=10/50/100 assumed trials: E/P haircut rises from 26.6% (N=10) to 61.6% (N=100) while BAB stays 4.6-9.3% across the same range, demonstrating the standard 50% rule-of-thumb haircut is wrong in both directions.
sources.sample: Three published zero-cost long-short equity factor strategies (E/P, momentum, betting-against-beta) over the full published sample each was originally reported on; N assumed at 10/50/100 trials.

sources.title: ...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
sources.authors: Campbell R. Harvey, Yan Liu, Heqing Zhu
sources.key_result: Cited via Harvey & Liu (2015)'s own text: documents at least 316 factors tested in the cross-sectional equity-returns literature and derives a t-ratio > 3.0 significance threshold for new discoveries once multiple testing is accounted for; also the source of the structural (correlated-trials) model Harvey & Liu (2015) builds on for non-independent test statistics.

candidates.candidate: Retrofit Holm-Bonferroni + Deflated Sharpe Ratio onto the already-completed 21-model sides/totals search, replacing the qualitative '0 of 21, verified three independent ways' claim with a citable, formula-backed haircut number.
candidates.fixes_finding: No trial registry exists with real preregistration + multiplicity correction (Holm/PBO/deflated-Sharpe) for the 21-model historical search that has already been run.
candidates.mechanism: Since no p-values were preregistered before the fact, this is honestly a retrospective haircut, not a true preregistered test -- and must be labeled as such. Pull each of the 21 models' paired performance series vs the closing line (already computable via backtest-significance.js's pairedBootstrapDiff / nfl-replay.js outputs) to get 21 p-values, order them, and apply Holm's step-down (p_(i) <= alpha/(M-i+1), per Holm 1979) rather than the registry's current Sidak-only correction. Separately compute the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (eq.1-2, Bailey & Lopez de Prado 2014) using N=21 as a lower bound and a second run at N=63 (3x, to informally account for undisclosed per-model tuning iterations, per Harvey & Liu's own caution that N must be assumed and is easy to understate) to see whether any nominal survivor holds up under either assumption.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/audit-registry.js (extend auditHistory() with a Holm-corrected alpha alongside the existing Sidak one) + new one-time scripts/retrofit-sides-totals-audit.mjs that reads the 21 models' historical paired series and writes status='retrofit' rows (distinct from real preregistrations) into audit_registry.
candidates.expected_value: Converts the project's single most load-bearing negative result (the basis for 'opener path dead for this model' and 'fantasy over betting' priorities in memory) from prose asserted to be re-verified into one number with a formula, a citation, and a documented N -- the actual deliverable an audit system exists to produce.
candidates.exit_test: If the Holm-corrected and DSR-adjusted p-value for the single best-performing of the 21 models remains >0.05 under both N=21 and N=63, formally close the sides/totals search with a citable number in place of the current qualitative claim, and do not reopen it without filing a new preregistration.

candidates.candidate: Consolidate the three independent, uncoordinated code/data-freeze hashers (audit-registry.js's codeHash()/dataSignature(), nfl-blind-audit.js's repositoryState()/inputMutationState(), and the correct transitive-import hasher already built in platform/code-identity.js) into one shared primitive that every audit/experiment table calls.
candidates.fixes_finding: orphaned audit-registry.js + bespoke nfl-blind-audit.js hashing -- the two systems the task names, plus a third independent implementation in code-identity.js found by grepping createHash across 45 files.
candidates.mechanism: code-identity.js already solves this correctly per its own doc comment (hashes only what a decision actually imports, walked transitively from a declared root via import.meta.url; never shells to git; never reads process.cwd()) and explicitly critiques nfl-replay.js's older trainingAuditCodeHash for both of those mistakes. audit-registry.js's codeHash() hashes every .js file in server/services/ (over-broad) and nfl-blind-audit.js's repositoryState() hashes all of server+scripts+package*.json (even more over-broad) -- both are blunter than the tool already sitting in the same codebase, and nfl-blind-audit.js's own comments document two false-voids this bluntness already caused (run 13 voided by a docs paragraph, run 16 voided by a docs-only commit moving HEAD).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/audit-registry.js:39-56 (codeHash/dataSignature), server/services/nfl-blind-audit.js repositoryState()/AUDITED_CODE_PATHS, server/platform/code-identity.js (the implementation to reuse, scoped per-audit to its actual dependency closure).
candidates.expected_value: Eliminates an already-observed class of false-void bugs, and removes the reason a real preregister-to-runAudit flow (F1/N3) would otherwise get punished by unrelated documentation churn.
candidates.exit_test: Running the same audit twice with an unrelated docs/README edit in between must not void either audit-registry.js's runAudit() or nfl-blind-audit.js's week-open check; a real service-code edit under the audit's dependency closure must still void it.

candidates.candidate: Backfill audit_registry with the historical trials this project has already run (the 21 sides/totals models, the 9 signal families, the 24 recency candidates from WORK_LOG's 'Do not redo these' list) as flagged historical rows, so auditHistory()'s Sidak/Holm denominator reflects the true number of hypotheses tested rather than whatever handful of audits happen to be filed today.
candidates.fixes_finding: No trial registry exists with real preregistration + multiplicity correction ... for the 21-model historical search that has already been run (same finding, complementary angle: the registry's correction is only honest if its N counts every hypothesis actually tested).
candidates.mechanism: auditHistory()'s corrected_alpha is computed from sealed.length, which today is near zero because nothing has ever been filed through the registry. Backfilling ~54 known historical trials (21+9+24, transcribed from WORK_LOG.md and path-to-profit-measurements.md) as status='historical' rows with their already-known failing outcomes fixes the denominator immediately, before any new audit is ever filed.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/audit-registry.js auditHistory()'s sealed.length denominator; server/db/schema/core-and-fantasy.js:379 audit_registry table (add a distinct status value for backfilled rows).
candidates.expected_value: Cheap and immediate: prevents the registry from ever reporting a falsely lenient corrected_alpha to a workflow that treats it as the single gate for what counts as a real result.
candidates.exit_test: auditHistory() reports tests_run >= 54 immediately after the backfill runs, with zero newly-introduced passed=true rows (backfill must not manufacture false discoveries).

candidates.candidate: Implement Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO) via CSCV and run it against the parameter-search trial matrices already sitting in server/data/market-lab and server/data/tree-lab.
candidates.mechanism: Per Bailey/Borwein/Lopez de Prado/Zhu (2015): partition the existing T x N trial-performance matrix (already the shape of spreads-*-tpot-trials.json / spreads-*-move-tpot-trials.json) into S=16 row-slices, form all C(16,8)=12,780 IS/OOS combinations, compute the logit of each combination's OOS relative rank for the IS-optimal config, PBO = fraction of logits below zero. This tests overfitting at the parameter-tuning layer underneath any one of the 21 models, which is exactly what the 21-model retrofit (F1) cannot see.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: new server/services/pbo-cscv.js consuming server/data/market-lab/latest.json and server/data/tree-lab/latest.json trial matrices; writes into the new research_trials table (N3) alongside DSR (N2).

do_not_do: Do not treat a retroactive Holm/DSR haircut as equivalent to true preregistration. Label retrofit rows distinctly (status='retrofit') from genuinely preregistered audits, and never let a retrofit result that happens to clear the bar promote a model to production on that basis alone -- this is exactly the 'hold-out is not preregistration' critique in the PBO paper's own comparison-to-other-approaches section.

Do not use PBO/CSCV as an optimization objective or stopping rule for a parameter search. The PBO paper explicitly warns against this in its limitations section: any counter-overfitting technique used to select an optimal strategy will itself result in overfitting.

Do not apply plain Bonferroni when Holm is available. Holm (1979) proves the step-down procedure is never less powerful than classical Bonferroni for identical test statistics -- there is no correctness reason to prefer Bonferroni once Holm is implemented.

Do not let the assumed trial count N (for DSR) or family size (for Holm/Bonferroni) be chosen after seeing the result, or be self-reported by whichever model wants credit. Harvey & Liu open their paper on exactly this failure mode -- N must come from the research_trials count (N3), fixed before the haircut is computed.

Do not run CSCV/PBO on a trial matrix with too few observations per slice. The PBO paper's own worked example used T=1,000 daily observations at S=16; a much shorter market-lab/tree-lab trial series will produce an unreliable, noisy PBO estimate.

Do not assume the 21 spread/total models (or their component signals) are statistically independent when applying any FWER correction, given tonight's own finding that the NFL ensemble's 20 components collapse to ~3 independent signals -- plain per-model Bonferroni/Sidak will be conservative (safe direction) but a dependency-aware correction (BHY, or the HLZ structural model) is the more honest number to report alongside it, not instead of it.

result.label: F07-sequential-inference-fix
result.summary: Confirmed the exact bug: server/services/audit-registry.js:219 collapses `alwaysValid.p_always_valid ?? alwaysValid.p_fixed_sample_only` into one scalar `alwaysValidP`, which is then written to a single `always_valid_p` DB column (server/db/schema/core-and-fantasy.js:400) with no `variance_source`/`anytime_valid` flag persisted. Grep confirms no production caller ever passes `always_valid_tau`/`always_valid_sigma`, so in practice every real audit gets a fixed-sample-only p-value silently stored under a column named as if it were anytime-valid. Compounding this, the Sidak-corrected alpha (`correctedAlpha`, audit-registry.js:197-198) is computed from `COUNT(*) WHERE status='sealed'` at RUN time (execution order) and never persisted — auditHistory() later recomputes a different, fresher corrected alpha from today's sealed count and reports `survive_correction` against it, silently disagreeing with the frozen `passed` boolean sealed earlier. This is the literal mechanism of "significance threshold silently depends on run order because a sequential and a fixed-sample p-value get collapsed into one field." Read 4 primary sources in full and used them to derive the schema fix: Howard/Ramdas/McAuliffe/Sekhon 2021 (Annals of Stats) for the CS/always-valid-p-value/sequential-test duality (Section 6, Lemma 3 — the running-minimum-is-still-valid property that the collapsed field violates) and the empirical validation that anytime-validity costs <2x width; Waudby-Smith & Ramdas 2024 (JRSS-B) for the state-of-the-art betting confidence sequence as the eventual upgrade path; Ramdas/Zrnic/Wainwright/Jordan 2018 (SAFFRON, ICML) for the online-FDR family that is the principled replacement for a fixed-family Sidak correction retrofitted onto a growing hypothesis stream; Johari/Pekelis/Walsh 2015/2019 (the paper Gridiron's own code already cites) for the concrete "Type I error can easily increase fivefold at 10,000 samples" result grounding why this matters. Delivered 7 candidates (4 fix, 3 new) each tied to exact file/line, cost, expected value, and exit test, plus a do-not-do list and one repo (gostevehoward/confseq, MIT, 84 stars) assessed as borrow-idea-not-port given Gridiron is pure Node.js.

sources.title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
sources.authors: Steven R. Howard, Aaditya Ramdas, Jon McAuliffe, Jasjeet Sekhon
sources.sample: Rademacher r.v., 100,000 i.i.d. draws, 10,000 replications (Fig.1); nonparametric, works for any sub-Gaussian/sub-gamma/sub-Bernstein process
sources.key_result: Section 6/Lemma 3 establishes the CS <-> always-valid-p-value <-> sequential-test duality and that the running minimum of an always-valid p-value process is itself always-valid -- exactly the invariant Gridiron's collapsed single-field always_valid_p violates. Fig.1 shows naive pointwise-CLT cumulative miscoverage rising to ~0.65 by t=1e5 against nominal 0.05, while the curved/stitched confidence sequence stays flat near 0.05 and the paper states the stitched bound stays within a factor of 2 of the fixed-sample CLT width over 5 orders of magnitude of t.

sources.title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
sources.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, 86(1):1-27
sources.sample: Beta(10,30) i.i.d. draws, n=10 to 1e4, 95% CIs and CSs, both time-uniform and fixed-time regimes (Fig.1)
sources.key_result: The betting/'Hedged' confidence sequence and interval are visibly tighter than both the sub-Gaussian and empirical-Bernstein constructions from Howard et al. 2020 across the full n range tested; the paper establishes new state-of-the-art bounds for bounded-mean estimation in both with- and without-replacement, sequential and fixed-time settings.

sources.title: SAFFRON: an adaptive algorithm for online control of the false discovery rate
sources.authors: Aaditya Ramdas, Tijana Zrnic, Martin J. Wainwright, Michael I. Jordan
sources.sample: Synthetic: p-values P_i=Phi(-Z_i), Z_i~N(mu_i,1), nulls mu_i=0, non-nulls mu_i=3, fraction of non-nulls pi_1 swept 0.1-0.8, target FDR alpha=0.05 (Fig.1)
sources.key_result: SAFFRON and LORD both hold empirical FDR at or below the nominal 0.05 across the whole pi_1 sweep while power rises from ~0.3 to ~0.85; SAFFRON dominates LORD and alpha-investing in power at every pi_1 tested. The paper's worked example (1000 tests/week at nominal 0.05 each, 80 discoveries, 50 false -> FDP=5/8) is the exact failure mode of applying a fixed per-test threshold to a growing hypothesis stream, which is what Gridiron's Sidak correction currently does.

sources.title: Always Valid Inference: Continuous Monitoring of A/B Tests
sources.authors: Ramesh Johari, Leo Pekelis, David Walsh
sources.sample: Deployed methodology analyzing 'hundreds of thousands of experiments' on a commercial A/B testing platform; illustrative example at n=10,000 samples
sources.key_result: States directly: 'Even with 10,000 samples (a sample size which is quite common in online A/B testing), Type I error can easily increase fivefold' under naive continuous monitoring -- the concrete number behind the always-valid-inference motivation that Gridiron's own backtest-significance.js already cites this paper for.
