result.label: F09: Hierarchical Bayesian NB/ZI prop distributions
result.summary: Gridiron's prop pipeline is more sophisticated than FOUND's one-liner suggests — player-week-engine.js and projections.js already simulate from negative binomials with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (shrinkage-fit.js) — but every hyperparameter in that machinery (NB dispersion, shrinkage k) is a fixed method-of-moments point estimate, not a Bayesian posterior, so uncertainty from small samples (rookies, backups, Week 1) never propagates into prop intervals; and the TD-prop calibration heads (nfl-prop-player-heads.js, nfl-prop-player-weekly-heads.js, td-regression.js) output a single scalar probability via ridge-logistic regression or an ad hoc sqrt(expected) Wald heuristic mislabeled "Poisson standard error," never a count distribution. No table anywhere stores a posterior-predictive artifact — every percentile is recomputed by live Monte Carlo from point parameters — and no probabilistic-programming toolchain (pymc/stan/numpyro) exists in the repo's Python research env, confirmed by directly checking research/.venv. Four primary sources were read in full: Baio & Blangiardo (2010)'s original hierarchical Poisson team model (and its own admitted overshrinkage problem, fixed with a 3-group mixture); Whitaker et al. (2020)'s player-level extension of it, validated out-of-sample on a held-out EPL season with real market-return numbers (+£4486.73 vs -£378.54 for the baseline, AUC 0.47-0.68); Jensen, McShane & Wyner (2009)'s hierarchical baseball hitting model, validated against real external competitors PECOTA/MARCEL with an honest mixed result (loses on overall RMSE, wins on MAE and on young players); and the PyMC hierarchical partial-pooling (Efron-Morris) case study showing exactly why a posterior beats a point-estimate shrinkage constant for low-sample players. A practitioner fantasy-football PyMC case study (srome.github.io) is flagged as a cautionary secondary source: its hierarchical model lost to a naive 7-game rolling average on point MAE.

sources.title: Bayesian hierarchical model for the prediction of football results
sources.key_result: Hierarchical Poisson log-linear model (att/def team effects, home effect) on Italian Serie A goals; basic model overshrinks extremes (top team Inter's points underestimated 69 vs actual 85); a 3-component non-central-t mixture on att/def fixes this (76 vs 69). Validation is in-sample posterior-predictive checking against the same fitted season, not a held-out season — an admitted limitation.
sources.sample: Serie A 1991-92: T=18 teams, G=306 games; Serie A 2007-08: 20 teams, G=360 games

sources.title: A Bayesian approach for determining player abilities in football
sources.authors: Gavin A. Whitaker, Ricardo Silva, Daniel Edwards, Ioannis Kosmidis
sources.key_result: Extends Baio & Blangiardo to per-player Poisson abilities (VI-fit, 2182 params, 544 players) layered onto the team hierarchical model; validated out-of-sample on the held-out 2014/15 EPL season predicting over/under 2.5 goals: AUC improves from 0.47-0.61 (team-only baseline) to 0.54-0.68 (with player abilities) across all 5 prediction blocks, and a flat-stake betting backtest against the real over/under market returns +GBP4486.73 with player abilities vs -GBP378.54 for the baseline over the full season.
sources.sample: English Premier League touch-by-touch data, 2013/14 (train, 380 games) + 2014/15 (held out), ~1.2M events, 544 players

sources.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Modeling of Hitting Performance in Baseball
sources.authors: Shane T. Jensen, Blake McShane, Abraham J. Wyner
sources.key_result: Binomial hitting-rate model with position-specific B-spline age curves and an elite/non-elite HMM mixture, validated on a genuinely held-out 2006 MLB season against real external competitor models PECOTA and MARCEL on 118 top HR hitters: RMSE 7.33 (this model) vs 7.11 (PECOTA, model loses) vs 7.82 (MARCEL, model wins); model wins on MAE (4.40 vs 4.68/4.41) and especially on young players (age<=26: RMSE 2.62 vs PECOTA 4.62). A player-specific-transitions extension added parameters but did NOT improve accuracy (RMSE 5.45 vs 5.30 base full model) — reported honestly as a negative result.
sources.sample: Lahman MLB database 1990-2005 fit set (10,280 player-years, 9 positions), held out and tested on 2006 season (559 players; 118 for the PECOTA/MARCEL external comparison)

sources.title: Hierarchical Partial Pooling — PyMC Example Gallery
sources.key_result: Beta-Binomial hierarchical model (phi~Uniform(0,1), kappa_log~Exponential(1.5), theta_i~Beta(phi*kappa,(1-phi)*kappa)) on the classic small-sample baseball batting dataset; a synthetic 0-for-4 player is partially pooled to an estimated true rate near 0.20 rather than the raw 0.0 MLE, the canonical demonstration of why a posterior beats a point-estimate shrinkage constant for exactly the low-sample-size player case (rookie, backup, Week 1) Gridiron's props currently handle with a fixed method-of-moments k.
sources.sample: Efron & Morris (1975) 18-player baseball batting-average dataset plus one added 4-at-bat synthetic player

candidates.candidate: Replace the fixed method-of-moments NB dispersion constants (TEAM_PASS_ATTEMPT_DISPERSION=47, TEAM_RUSH_CARRY_DISPERSION=31 in player-week-engine.js, and the per-player dispersion formula in projections.js:478-480) with a hierarchical NB fit that puts a prior on dispersion and estimates it jointly with team/player effects (Baio & Blangiardo-style), so simulated prop percentiles reflect hyperparameter uncertainty, not one plug-in number.
candidates.fixes_finding: Player props are point-estimate projections, not distributions — no negative-binomial/hierarchical/calibrated model (verified more precisely: NB dispersion and shrinkage k in player-week-engine.js/projections.js/shrinkage-fit.js are fixed method-of-moments point estimates, not posteriors)
candidates.mechanism: A method-of-moments dispersion estimate (mean^2/(var-mean)) is a single number computed once from historical team-seasons and then treated as ground truth for every future simulation; it has no attached uncertainty, so a team-season with thin history (e.g. a new coordinator, a rookie starter) gets the same confidently-narrow NB spread as a 10-year-stable offense. A hierarchical fit (dispersion drawn from its own prior, updated jointly with the mean via MCMC/VI) yields a posterior over dispersion whose width naturally reflects how much data actually supports it.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Offline Python batch job (new file under research/, e.g. research/fit_hierarchical_dispersion.py using pymc) refits team pass-attempt/rush-carry dispersion (and per-player efficiency-rate priors) as a hierarchical NB/Beta model on player_week_usage, exporting posterior mean+SD (not just a point) into a new table nfl_prop_hierarchical_priors; player-week-engine.js reads dispersion as a random draw from N(posterior_mean, posterior_sd) each simulation run instead of a hardcoded constant, so the NB draw's own dispersion is itself uncertain when the season/coordinator has little history.
candidates.expected_value: Wider, more honest predictive intervals specifically for low-history teams/players (new coordinators, rookies, injury-replacement roles) — the exact case scripts/fit-team-volume-dispersion.mjs's own docstring says a point constant currently mishandles (it flags k=12 was already found to be 2.2x/1.7x too wide before being refit once; a static refit will drift stale again next season the same way).
candidates.exit_test: On a held-out season, 80% posterior-predictive interval coverage for team pass-attempt/rush-carry totals should land in [75%,85%] (Jensen et al.'s own coverage-check methodology, Table 1) for BOTH high-history and low-history team-seasons; today's fixed-dispersion model should be checked for the same split first — if low-history coverage is already fine, do not ship this.

candidates.candidate: Replace shrinkage-fit.js's per-metric point-estimate k (k* = sigma^2_within/sigma^2_between via one-way ANOVA) with a hierarchical model that puts a prior on the between-player variance itself, so shrinkSafe() effectively becomes a posterior mean instead of a plug-in constant, and can report a credible interval on the shrunk rate.
candidates.fixes_finding: Player props are point-estimate projections, not distributions — no negative-binomial/hierarchical/calibrated model (the empirical-Bayes shrinkage constants that drive every rate in projections.js are themselves un-uncertain point estimates)
candidates.mechanism: Method-of-moments variance-component estimation (Searle 1992, used in shrinkage-fit.js) can and does produce negative or unstable between-player variance estimates on noisy metrics (the codebase already special-cases k=Infinity via shrinkSafe for exactly this failure mode); a proper hierarchical model instead places a weakly-informative prior on sigma^2_between (e.g. half-Cauchy) and lets the posterior naturally handle near-zero true variance without a special-cased fallback, while also yielding a credible interval on each player's shrunk rate rather than one number.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Same offline Python job as F09-fix-1 extended to target_share/catch_rate/ypt/rec_td_rate/ypc/rush_td_rate (the exact metrics list in projections.js:437-471); posterior mean replaces the point k in the existing shrink() call, posterior SD is stored alongside and surfaced in nfl-props.js output as a per-prop confidence band.
candidates.expected_value: Removes the k=Infinity special-case as a symptom rather than papering over it, and gives every prop a real credible interval on the underlying rate that the current point-shrunk rate cannot provide.
candidates.exit_test: Re-run the exact walk-forward comparison shrinkage-fit.js's own test suite already performs (test/ dir has coverage for this) with hierarchical k vs point k; hierarchical version must not regress Brier/RMSE on any of the 3 held-out seasons already used, and must show narrower low-coverage-metric special-casing (fewer/no k=Infinity fallbacks needed).

candidates.candidate: Replace td-regression.js's sqrt(expected) 'Poisson standard error' heuristic and nfl-prop-player-heads.js/nfl-prop-player-weekly-heads.js's scalar ridge-logistic TD-probability heads with a genuine hierarchical NB/Poisson count model of touchdowns per player, partially pooled by position (Baio & Blangiardo/Whitaker structure), producing a full posterior-predictive count distribution instead of one calibrated probability number.
candidates.fixes_finding: Player props are point-estimate projections, not distributions — no negative-binomial/hierarchical/calibrated model (td-regression.js's se=sqrt(expected) is a Wald-normal approximation mislabeled 'Poisson standard error,' and nfl-prop-player-heads.js/nfl-prop-player-weekly-heads.js output a single sigmoid probability with zero count-distribution structure)
candidates.mechanism: sqrt(expected) is the correct SE only under a Poisson assumption with variance=mean; touchdown counts are known to be overdispersed relative to Poisson (goal-line role concentration), so this SE is a systematic understatement exactly when it matters most (high-volume goal-line backs). Separately, a ridge-logistic scalar probability cannot express 'this player is a lock for exactly 1 TD but never 2+' vs 'this player is boom/bust 0-or-2' — both can share the same anytime-TD probability but have very different multi-TD and DFS-relevant tails.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New model class registered in player-head-registry.js alongside the existing CHALLENGER_HEADS in nfl-prop-player-heads.js: a hierarchical NB(mean=opportunity-weighted rate, dispersion=position-pooled) fit offline in Python, exported as per-player-position posterior summaries, consumed by td-regression.js in place of the sqrt(expected) line and by a new applyHierarchicalTdModel() that outputs P(0),P(1),P(2+) directly instead of a single sigmoid.
candidates.expected_value: td-regression.js's own note already concedes 'touchdown rate is the least stable number in football' — a model that natively expresses overdispersion should out-calibrate a Wald-normal SE particularly in the tails (2+ TD games), which is exactly the market FOUND flags as Gridiron's one area of genuine measured skill (2+ TD Brier skill +27%) and therefore worth improving carefully rather than leaving untouched.
candidates.exit_test: Must pass the SAME walk-forward + paired-bootstrap gate nfl-prop-player-heads.js already implements (walkForwardChallengerTd, recordChallengerGateAudit) on identical held-out seasons (2023-2025) before touching calibrateAnytimeTd; per td-regression.js's own prior failure (declined 0/3, 0/3), do not promote on training-season Brier alone.

candidates.candidate: Build an offline hierarchical-Bayes fitting pipeline (PyMC or NumPyro, since research/.venv currently has neither) that jointly pools player rates AND week-to-week variation (a random-walk or AR(1) on player ability across weeks within a season), following the dynamic extension both Baio & Blangiardo and Whitaker et al. explicitly flag as unimplemented future work in their own papers.
candidates.mechanism: Every current pooling mechanism in Gridiron (shrinkage-fit.js's k, player-week-engine.js's dispersion) pools ACROSS players within one static season-level fit; none of it pools across WEEKS within a season the way a state-space/random-walk model would, so a mid-season role change (new starter, injury return, scheme change) is only picked up via role-changepoint.js's discrete changepoint detection, not via a smoothly-updating posterior belief.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New Python module fitting a per-player latent ability that follows a random walk across weeks (theta_i,w ~ theta_i,w-1 + N(0,sigma_walk^2)), hierarchically pooled across players by position at week 1; posterior mean/SD per player-week exported to a new table nfl_prop_dynamic_ability, read by player-week-engine.js as an additional multiplier alongside role-changepoint.js's existing discrete signal rather than replacing it.
candidates.expected_value: Directly targets the gap both primary sources call out as their own unfinished work; if it works, subsumes some of role-changepoint.js's discrete jumps with a smoother, better-calibrated signal — but Jensen et al.'s player-specific-transition result (added dynamics, no accuracy gain) is a real risk this exit test must rule out before shipping.
candidates.exit_test: On held-out weeks, compare Brier/RMSE of the random-walk model against role-changepoint.js's current discrete-changepoint signal alone; per the do-not-do list, do NOT ship unless the dynamic model beats the static-plus-changepoint baseline by a margin bigger than bootstrap noise — Jensen et al.'s own negative result on player-specific dynamics means null is the base-rate expectation.

candidates.candidate: Add a zero-inflation component (structural-zero mixture) to the player-week event simulator for receptions/carries/TDs, distinguishing 'drew from a low-but-positive NB rate' from 'did not meaningfully play this week' (benched, injured mid-game, blown-out garbage time, committee vulture).
candidates.mechanism: A pure NB distribution puts positive probability mass near zero but cannot represent a genuine point mass at exactly zero driven by a separate causal process (not playing) rather than bad racing luck; ZINB (zero-inflated NB) explicitly mixes a Bernoulli 'structural zero' gate with an NB count, and is the standard fix in the count-modeling literature (referenced directly in NCSS's and the arXiv spatiotemporal ZINB methodology papers found in this research, though neither is football-specific enough to count as a primary source here).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Extend playerWeekEventExpectation in player-week-engine.js: gate the existing NB draw behind a Bernoulli whose probability comes from nfl-player-context.js's opportunityContextMultiplier and nfl-news-signal.js's injury/role signal (both already exist and are already consulted elsewhere in this file) — when the gate fires 'zero,' skip the NB draw entirely rather than letting a low-mean NB occasionally produce an unrealistically-motivated zero.
candidates.expected_value: Most useful for the receptions/TD props market specifically flagged in FOUND as needing a distributional (not point-estimate) treatment — a committee-back vulture-TD scenario is exactly the kind of structural zero a plain NB misprices.
candidates.exit_test: On weeks where a player was inactive/limited for a real, identifiable reason (injury report, blowout garbage time via game-script data already in gamescript.js), ZINB-gated prop probabilities should show lower Brier than the plain-NB baseline on the same row set; if the improvement is not statistically distinguishable via the existing pairedBootstrapDiff harness, do not ship — added model complexity for no measured gain is exactly what Jensen et al.'s negative result warns against.

candidates.candidate: Stand up a real probabilistic-programming toolchain (pymc or numpyro added to research/.venv) plus a stored posterior-predictive artifact table, so props are served from a nightly-fitted posterior instead of re-simulated from point parameters on every request.
candidates.mechanism: Confirmed by direct inspection: research/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages has scipy/sklearn/pandas/seaborn but no pymc, no cmdstanpy/pystan, no numpyro, no arviz; there is no MCMC/VI capability anywhere in this codebase today, JS or Python. Every prop percentile nfl-props.js reports is a fresh Monte-Carlo draw from point parameters computed at request time, and no migration in server/migrations/ defines a table for storing a posterior or posterior-predictive summary (018_saved_prop_tickets.js is the user's own bet slip, not a model artifact).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: pip install pymc (or numpyro) into research/.venv; a new nightly script (research/fit_prop_posteriors.py) fits the hierarchical models from F09-fix-1/2/3 and exports posterior summaries (mean, SD, and a handful of quantiles per player-market-week) to a new migration-defined table, e.g. nfl_prop_posterior_summaries(player_id, market, week, season, mean, sd, q10, q25, q50, q75, q90, fitted_at); nfl-props.js reads from this table for the distributional shape instead of recomputing NB draws inline, falling back to the existing live-simulation path if no fitted row exists for a player-week.
candidates.expected_value: This is the concrete infrastructure every other candidate in this brief (F09-fix-1/2/3, F09-new-1/2) needs to actually ship — without it, 'hierarchical Bayesian' has nowhere to live in this JS-only codebase. Also removes the recompute cost of live Monte Carlo on every prop-board request.
candidates.exit_test: Before wiring into nfl-props.js's live path, verify offline that stored posterior summaries reproduce the same predictive means (within noise) as the current live Monte Carlo on a sample of player-weeks — a silent divergence between the stored artifact and the live simulator would be worse than not having the artifact at all.

do_not_do: Do not rip out player-week-engine.js/projections.js's existing NB-simulation + empirical-Bayes-shrinkage machinery wholesale — it already has the right shape (volume x efficiency, NB-distributed opportunity, walk-forward tested) and the fix is at the two specific point-estimate seams (dispersion, shrinkage k), not a full rewrite.

Do not promote any hierarchical prop model on training-season fit quality or in-sample posterior-predictive checks alone — Baio & Blangiardo's own original paper only validated in-sample and admitted it; every model here must clear the SAME walk-forward + paired-bootstrap + forward-CLV gate model-governance.js already enforces for every other prop head in this codebase.

Do not add player-specific dynamic parameters (per-player HMM transitions, per-player random walks) as a first move — Jensen et al. tried exactly this and measured no accuracy gain despite added complexity and parameters. Start with position/role-level pooling only and earn dynamics with evidence.

Do not assume 'more Bayesian' beats a naive baseline by default — the srome.github.io PyMC3 fantasy-football case study's hierarchical model lost to a plain 7-game rolling average on MAE (6.08 vs 5.99); gate on interval calibration and CLV, not point-forecast RMSE alone, and be willing to report a negative result the way Jensen et al. did (their model lost to PECOTA on overall RMSE and they said so).

Do not hand-roll MCMC/VI in JavaScript. No probabilistic-programming library exists anywhere in this repo (verified: research/.venv has no pymc/pystan/cmdstanpy/numpyro/arviz). Any hierarchical fit belongs in an offline Python batch job exporting posterior summaries for the Node server to read, mirroring the existing scripts/fit-team-volume-dispersion.mjs pattern of separating offline fitting from online consumption.

Do not touch the live fantasy-football-dashboard server, its database, or any in-progress process — this research is read-only against that codebase per the standing HARD RULES; all of the above is a design for future work, not a patch to apply tonight.

result.label: F11-conformal-calibration
result.summary: Tonight's audit's "assumed-normal SD on margins" is actually three distinct instances, all traced by file/line: nfl-market.js's single season-wide marginStd fed into normalCdf(predMargin/marginStd) with no per-game conditioning; nfl-expert-council.js's per-expert uncertainty (SD) combined into coordinator.uncertainty and audited only for its calibration gap (never corrected) by nfl-slice-diagnostic.js; and nfl-passing-specialists.js's flat 1.2816*residualSd interval for passing-yard props. A fourth spot, nfl-ensemble.js's predictiveDistribution(), is an empirical bootstrap already but is explicitly self-flagged production_eligible:false with an ad hoc disagreement-inflation cap. Read four primary sources in full (Angelopoulos & Bates 2021 gentle intro; Romano/Patterson/Candès 2019 CQR; Barber/Candès/Ramdas/Tibshirani 2023 nonexchangeable conformal; Angelopoulos/Candès/Tibshirani 2023 conformal PID control), each with exact theorem statements and real-data numbers. Three fix candidates wrap split-conformal/CQR calibration directly onto the three assumed-normal spots (replacing global SD with per-game/per-bucket guaranteed intervals, ~37% narrower at equal coverage per the CQR paper's own benchmark). Three new candidates bring capabilities the repo has zero of today: weighted/nonexchangeable conformal for in-season drift, an online conformal-PID quantile tracker for the weekly retraining loop, and discrete conformal prediction sets over TD-count outcomes for the props module (currently only point-estimated + Brier-graded, never given an actual coverage-guaranteed object).

sources.title: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification
sources.key_result: Split conformal: q̂ = ceil((n+1)(1-α))/n empirical quantile of calibration scores; C(x)={y: s(x,y)≤q̂}. Theorem 1: under exchangeability, P(Y_test∈C(X_test)) ≥ 1-α, distribution-free and model-agnostic, non-asymptotic. Validated on ImageNet/COCO/polyp segmentation/MEPS/weather. For drift/time-series proposes weighted calibration (e.g. w_i=0.99^(n-i+1)) with coverage bound 1-α-2Σw̃_i·ε_i.
sources.sample: Real-data examples across classification (ImageNet, MS-COCO, polyp segmentation) and quantile regression (MEPS); figures rather than one tabulated coverage number.

sources.title: Conformalized Quantile Regression
sources.authors: Yaniv Romano, Evan Patterson, Emmanuel Candès
sources.key_result: Score E_i=max(q_lo(X_i)-Y_i, Y_i-q_hi(X_i)); interval = [q_lo(X)-Q_{1-α}(E), q_hi(X)+Q_{1-α}(E)]. Theorem 1: exact two-sided finite-sample coverage, 1-α ≤ P(Y∈C(X)) ≤ 1-α+1/(|I2|+1) under exchangeability. Table 1 (α=0.1, 11 real datasets incl. bike-sharing, bio, community-crime, blog-feedback, MEPS, 20 splits): CQR+RF length 1.41 / coverage 90.33% vs plain split-conformal length 2.24 / coverage 89.99% — ~37% narrower at matched coverage because width is heteroscedasticity-adaptive instead of one global constant.
sources.sample: 11 real regression datasets, 20 random splits each, α=0.1; synthetic heteroscedastic experiment (CQR length 1.99 vs 2.91 for standard conformal at matched ~90% coverage).

sources.title: Conformal Prediction Beyond Exchangeability
sources.authors: Rina Foygel Barber, Emmanuel J. Candès, Aaditya Ramdas, Ryan J. Tibshirani
sources.key_result: Weighted conformal replaces uniform 1/(n+1) weights with normalized w̃_i (e.g. w_i=ρ^(n+1-i) for drift). Theorem 2: P(Y∈Ĉ(X)) ≥ 1-α-Σw̃_i·d_TV(R(Z),R(Z^i)) — coverage gap bounded by total-variation departure from exchangeability, the only one of the four papers with a formal non-exchangeability bound. Real data: ELEC2 electricity (3,444 half-hourly points) plain conformal 85.2% coverage vs weighted 89.3% at narrower width (0.527 vs 0.565); 2020 election county vote-shift (geographic train/test split) plain conformal 74.3% vs weighted 84.0%.
sources.sample: ELEC2 Australian electricity transfer time series (1996-99, 3,444 points, 9am-noon window); 2020 US presidential county-level vote-share shift, 1,119 train / 1,957 test counties split by time zone.

sources.title: Conformal PID Control for Time Series Prediction
sources.authors: Anastasios Angelopoulos, Emmanuel Candès, Ryan J. Tibshirani
sources.key_result: Online quantile tracker: q_{t+1}=q_t+η(err_t-α), err_t=1{y_t∉C_t}. Theorem 1: for ANY sequence (including adversarial), running miscoverage (1/T)Σerr_t → α, deterministic, no exchangeability needed. COVID CA death forecasts: base ensemble held only 20% coverage during 2020/21 winter wave (nominal 80%) vs conformal PID 70% in same window. NSW electricity: an earlier adaptive baseline (ACI) hit ~90% coverage but produced infinite-width sets at higher learning rates; conformal PID hit 90% coverage with median finite width ~19 — demonstrates that 'always valid' adaptive methods can be vacuous and PID control is the fix.
sources.sample: California COVID-19 weekly death forecasts (winter 2020/21 wave, ~10 weeks); Amazon daily stock price; New South Wales electricity demand time series.

candidates.candidate: Split-conformal wrapper around nfl-market.js's season-level margin/win-probability model
candidates.fixes_finding: nfl-market.js:412 fits one global marginStd = stdev(residuals) per season and line 435 does normalCdf(predMargin/marginStd) for every game with no per-game conditioning and no held-out coverage check — the literal assumed-normal-SD defect named in FOUND.
candidates.mechanism: Hold out the most recent N weeks of each season as a calibration fold (never a random split — NFL weeks are autocorrelated). Compute nonconformity scores s_i = |actualMargin_i - predMargin_i| on that fold, take q̂ = ceil((n+1)(1-α))/n empirical quantile (Angelopoulos & Bates Theorem 1), and report [predMargin-q̂, predMargin+q̂] as the interval instead of a Gaussian-CDF-derived one. For the win-probability number specifically, keep normalCdf only as a smoothing convenience but validate its 50/60/70/80% implied buckets against nfl-slice-diagnostic.js's existing calibration() bucketing — if buckets are already off (which nfl-slice-diagnostic exists to check), replace normalCdf's implied probability with the empirical CDF of the calibration-fold residuals directly (same trick nfl-ensemble.js already uses via quantile(marginSamples,...) — just conformalized so its coverage is provable, not just plausible).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New pure function conformalMarginInterval(predMargin, calibrationResiduals, alpha) added to stats-util.js (which already hosts normalCdf, quantile, stdev — natural home); called from nfl-market.js's scoreAccuracy() and wherever marginStd/normalCdf(predMargin/marginStd) currently appears; calibration fold pulled from the existing nested walk-forward split already computed in nfl-market.js (train/test/season loop ~line 380-410), just held out an extra week rather than folded into training.
candidates.expected_value: Replaces a plausible-looking but unvalidated Gaussian interval with one that has a finite-sample coverage proof; makes nfl-slice-diagnostic.js's existing calibration audit either close to empty (success) or gives it a concrete number to point at (still useful). Does not by itself create betting edge — a valid interval is not the same as +CLV given the ensemble's own -2.28 CLV finding.
candidates.exit_test: Run nfl-slice-diagnostic.js's calibration() bucketing against the new conformal intervals on a held-out season (e.g. train through 2023, calibrate/test on 2024): the 80% conformal interval must cover the actual margin in 78-82% of held-out games. If it doesn't hit that band, the fold size or conditioning is wrong — do not ship.

candidates.candidate: Group-conditional (Mondrian) conformal calibration replacing nfl-slice-diagnostic.js's diagnose-only gap
candidates.fixes_finding: nfl-expert-council.js combines per-expert SDs into one coordinator.uncertainty written to nfl_weekly_expert_examples, and nfl-slice-diagnostic.js:82-100 computes normalCdf(|forecast_residual|/uncertainty) and reports a calibration gap per slice (confidence bucket, matchup type, roof) but never corrects it — the audit finds the assumed-normal miscalibration and stops there.
candidates.mechanism: For each of nfl-slice-diagnostic.js's existing groupBy() strata (confidenceBucket, matchupType, roofType), run split-conformal separately within that stratum (Mondrian/group-conditional conformal, a direct extension of Angelopoulos & Bates Theorem 1 applied per group instead of globally) using the stratum's own held-out forecast_residual/actual_residual pairs already sitting in nfl_weekly_expert_examples. This turns 'here is the gap between implied and empirical' into 'here is a corrected width guaranteed to close that gap, per stratum.'
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New export in nfl-slice-diagnostic.js, e.g. conformalCalibration(list, groupKeyFn), sitting next to the existing calibration() function and reusing its same query against nfl_weekly_expert_examples; consumed wherever coordinator.uncertainty is currently read out of nfl-expert-council.js (lines ~545, 658, 680) to replace the flat SD with the stratum-specific conformal half-width.
candidates.expected_value: Turns an audit that only ever reports a problem into one that also ships the fix, using data the repo already collects (no new ingestion needed) — this is the cheapest of the three fix candidates because the calibration table already exists.
candidates.exit_test: For each stratum with readable sample size (>= MIN_SLICE_SAMPLE, the constant nfl-slice-diagnostic.js already defines), the corrected interval's empirical coverage must land within 3pp of nominal on a held-out slice of weeks; a stratum too small to test stays flagged unreadable exactly as the file already does today, rather than silently applying a global correction to it.

candidates.candidate: Conformalized quantile regression (CQR) replacing the flat 1.2816×SD interval in nfl-passing-specialists.js
candidates.fixes_finding: nfl-passing-specialists.js:163 sets intervalHalf = 1.2816 * residualSd, one fixed half-width for every quarterback in every game, graded by the file's own coverage_80 metric — a flat-width, assumed-normal player-prop interval, the exact 'point-estimate not distribution' defect FOUND names for props.
candidates.mechanism: Fit two quantile regressors (10th/90th percentile of passing yards) on the proper-training split using features already computed in the file's row.features[family] correction pipeline; on the calibration fold compute E_i = max(q_lo(X_i)-actualYards_i, actualYards_i-q_hi(X_i)) (Romano/Patterson/Candès score) and take its (1-α) empirical quantile; final interval = [q_lo(x)-Q, q_hi(x)+Q]. Their own benchmark (Table 1) shows this is ~37% narrower than a flat-width interval at the same coverage because width now varies with attempts/opponent/weather instead of being one global number.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Modify grade() in nfl-passing-specialists.js: replace the single intervalHalf line with a call to a new conformalQuantileInterval(row.features, calibrationSet) helper; reuse the file's existing groups clustering (by game, to keep same-game correlated QBs out of each other's calibration fold) as the conformal calibration split boundary.
candidates.expected_value: The passing-yards module is one of the props surfaces closest to production; a genuinely calibrated, heteroscedasticity-adaptive interval directly improves the interval half of its output without touching the point-estimate half that already tests well.
candidates.exit_test: coverage_80 (already computed in the same function) must land at 78-82% on a held-out season, and mean interval width must be strictly less than the current flat 1.2816×residualSd width for at least 60% of QB-games (Romano et al.'s narrower-at-equal-coverage result) — if width doesn't shrink, the quantile regressors aren't adding information and the change should be reverted.

candidates.candidate: Weighted / nonexchangeable conformal calibration for in-season drift
candidates.mechanism: Barber/Candès/Ramdas/Tibshirani's weighted conformal: replace uniform calibration weights with w_i = ρ^(week_gap), giving recent weeks more influence, and report the accompanying coverage-gap bound (Theorem 2) in terms of total-variation drift rather than silently assuming exchangeability across a 17-week season with accumulating injuries, weather shifts, and Week 15-18 seeding incentives.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New helper alongside stats-util.js's existing quantile()/stdev(), e.g. weightedQuantile(scores, weights, alpha); applied on top of the calibration folds built for F-A/F-B so both the correction and its formal non-exchangeability caveat ship together, rather than bolting weighting onto a system that has never validated coverage at all.
candidates.expected_value: Gridiron's existing team-strength blend (nfl-ensemble.js gain=0.075 Kalman-style update) already re-weights recent games for the point forecast, but nothing re-weights the calibration set behind an interval — this closes that gap with a citable, provable bound instead of an ad hoc decay constant.
candidates.exit_test: Compare weighted vs unweighted conformal coverage on the back half of a season (Weeks 10-18, where drift is largest): weighted must show measurably smaller coverage gap (|empirical-nominal|) than unweighted on that back half specifically, matching the qualitative ELEC2/election result (weighted recovers coverage lost to drift).

candidates.candidate: Online conformal-PID quantile tracker for the weekly retraining loop
candidates.mechanism: Angelopoulos/Candès/Tibshirani's q_{t+1}=q_t+η(err_t-α) recursion updates the interval half-width every week using only whether last week's actual margin fell inside or outside the previous interval — a deterministic, no-exchangeability-required guarantee (their Theorem 1) that self-corrects across a live season the way nfl-ensemble.js's point-forecast Kalman update already does, but for the interval instead of the point.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New stateful tracker persisted week-over-week (a small JSON/db row keyed by season+model, holding current q_t) that replaces nfl-ensemble.js predictiveDistribution()'s ad hoc disagreement-based inflation (capped at 0.25, no justification given for the cap or the 30-point divisor) with a mechanism that has an actual convergence guarantee; this is the direct route to flipping predictiveDistribution()'s own production_eligible:false flag.
candidates.expected_value: Moderate confidence because the paper's own results show this can work brilliantly (electricity) or only partially recover target coverage under true regime change (COVID: 70% vs 80% target) — it is not a silver bullet, but it is strictly more principled than an uninspected inflation cap, and it is cheap to bolt onto the weekly cadence Gridiron already runs.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest the tracker over 2-3 full historical seasons week-by-week (never touching live 2026 data); running miscoverage (1/T)Σerr_t must converge toward the target α within a few weeks each season and must not produce degenerate (near-infinite or near-zero) widths at any point — check median width alongside coverage, per the paper's own ACI-vs-PID caution.

candidates.candidate: Discrete conformal prediction sets for TD-count prop outcomes
candidates.mechanism: Extend split conformal to a discrete outcome space (TD counts 0/1/2/3+) by scoring s(x,y) = 1 - P̂(y|x) from the props module's existing per-bin probability estimates, then forming the prediction SET {y : s(x,y) ≤ q̂} from calibration-fold quantiles — a genuinely different object than a point estimate graded by Brier score, because it comes with the same marginal coverage guarantee as the continuous case (Angelopoulos & Bates's classification framing, e.g. their ImageNet/COCO set-valued examples) applied to a discrete sports outcome instead.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New module alongside the existing 2+ TD prop scoring logic (the file the task brief names as the project's one area of measured skill, +27% Brier skill) — add a conformalPredictionSet(probsByBin, calibrationSet, alpha) helper that turns the existing per-bin probabilities into a guaranteed-coverage set rather than changing the underlying probability model at all.
candidates.expected_value: Cheapest of the six candidates (reuses an already-good probability model, adds only the calibration/set-construction layer) but moderate value because a prediction SET over 4 discrete bins is a weaker deliverable than a genuinely sharp point/interval — mainly useful as a governance/abstention signal (e.g. 'the set includes both 1 and 2+ so this prop is not confidently gradable') rather than a pricing tool.
candidates.exit_test: On held-out weeks, the average prediction-set size must be < 3 of the 4 bins (otherwise it is vacuous) while still covering the true outcome in >= (1-α) of games; if set size collapses toward 4 (the whole outcome space) whenever the underlying model is uncertain, that is itself informative and should feed the existing abstention-audit machinery (nfl-abstention-audit.js) rather than be discarded.

do_not_do: Do not run vanilla (unweighted, unconditioned) split conformal across a full season and call it done — a 17-week NFL season is not exchangeable (injuries accumulate, weather turns, Weeks 15-18 carry seeding incentives); use the weighted/grouped variants (F-B, N-A) or explicitly report the Barber et al. TV-distance caveat next to any coverage number.

Do not conformalize on a calibration fold smaller than ~100-150 games — the (n+1)(1-α)/n empirical quantile is unstable/degenerate at small n, especially near the tails; nfl-ensemble.js already enforces this norm (cohort.length>=100, conditional cohort >=120) and any new conformal code should match or exceed that floor.

Do not apply a single symmetric split-conformal correction to nfl-passing-specialists.js as the 'fix' — that reproduces the exact flat-width bug in new packaging; use CQR (F-C) specifically, since the paper's own numbers show CQR beats flat-width conformal by ~37% at matched coverage precisely because it is heteroscedasticity-adaptive.

Do not treat 'valid 80% coverage' as 'found a betting edge.' A calibrated interval can be wide and still valid (see the PID paper's own point about ACI producing infinite sets); report width/sharpness next to coverage every time, and remember the ensemble's own measured -2.28 CLV means a well-calibrated interval around the closing line is not automatically +EV.

Do not build calibration folds via random/shuffled cross-validation — NFL weeks are autocorrelated; calibrate only on strictly-prior weeks/seasons (out-of-time), matching the walk-forward guards nfl-ensemble.js and nfl-market.js already use.

Do not execute, install, or import the cloned reference repos (yromano/cqr, aangelopoulos/conformal-time-series, aangelopoulos/conformal-prediction) — they are read-only algorithm references; port the (small, ~20-40 line) quantile logic to the existing JS stats-util.js by hand.

Do not touch the live database or any running process in fantasy-football-dashboard while Week 1 2026 is being captured — prototype and validate every candidate here against exported historical rows only.

result.label: F08 — Bayesian state-space / dynamic linear team-strength ratings
result.summary: Read Glickman & Stern (1998 JASA state-space model, and its 2016 practitioner chapter) and Koopman & Lit (2019 score-driven dynamic bivariate Poisson/Skellam) in full, plus Ley/Van de Wiele/Van Eetvelde (2018, weighted-MLE alternative), all with real out-of-sample numbers. Confirmed by reading the code that Nick's finding actually lives in server/services/nfl-preseason-blend.js (not nfl-team-strength.js, which is a preseason-only feature aggregate): blendedTeamRating() is a correctly-implemented (post Codex M01 fix) but single-shot normal-normal shrinkage that (a) is not opponent-adjusted (raw own-margin average, no paired-comparison design) and (b) is not a recursive state-space filter (no separate week-to-week vs season-to-season evolution variance, refit fresh each call from two global calibrated scalars). Found 4 repos; two are strong: mikemiller442/Bivariate_Poisson_Soccer has real runnable Stan code for the exact bivariate-Poisson model class, and renenunezg/momentumnfl is an actively-maintained (this week), MIT-licensed, NFL-specific closed-form Bayesian-ridge rating engine walk-forward-graded against the closing line — a live production analogue of the cheap fix proposed here. The single most load-bearing number found: Koopman & Lit's own head-to-head test shows their fast score-driven (GAS) filter beats a literal parameter-driven state-space/Kalman-MCMC fit on forecast precision AND does it in under 10 seconds vs ~1 hour per fit — directly determining which of the two "fix" implementation paths (cheap ridge-regression paired comparison vs full recursive filter) to build first.

sources.title: A State-Space Model for National Football League Scores
sources.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 93(441)
sources.sample: NFL regular seasons 1988-1993, 28 teams, held out weeks 11-18 of 1993 (n=110 games) for out-of-sample evaluation
sources.key_result: Paired-comparison state-space model with separate week-to-week (sigma_w ~ 0.88) and season-to-season (sigma_s ~ 2.35) evolution variances and team-specific home-field-advantage (ranged 1.6 to 7.7 points across 28 teams), fit by Gibbs sampling. Out-of-sample vs the Las Vegas point spread on 110 held-out games: MSE 165.0 vs 170.5, MAE 10.50 vs 10.84, correctly picked 64/110 (58.2%) winners vs Vegas's 63 (57.3%) -- a small, honestly-reported edge, explicitly stated by the authors as not large enough to generalize.

sources.title: Forecasting football match results in national league competitions using score-driven time series models
sources.venue: Tinbergen Institute Discussion Paper TI 2017-062/III (published, International Journal of Forecasting, 2019)
sources.sample: 6 European leagues (EPL, Bundesliga, La Liga, Ligue 1, Serie A, Eredivisie), 17 seasons 1999/2000-2015/16, ~15,000 out-of-sample toto forecasts 2009-2016
sources.key_result: Dynamic bivariate Poisson with score-driven (GAS) attack/defense updating is the best forecaster across all 6 leagues by Rank Probability Score, beating the Skellam and ordered-probit variants and beating a full parameter-driven (Kalman-filter/simulated-ML) state-space equivalent of the SAME model on forecast precision -- while costing under 10 seconds of estimation time per fit vs approximately 1 hour for the state-space fit.

sources.title: Ranking soccer teams on basis of their current strength: a comparison of maximum likelihood approaches
sources.authors: Ley, C., Van de Wiele, T. & Van Eetvelde, H.
sources.sample: English Premier League 2008-2017 and international national-team matches 2008-2017
sources.key_result: 10 weighted-maximum-likelihood models (Thurstone-Mosteller, Bradley-Terry, Bradley-Terry-Davidson, Independent and Bivariate Poisson) compared by out-of-sample Rank Probability Score using a smooth exponential half-life time-decay weight; Bivariate and Independent Poisson win. This is the cheapest alternative to a real dynamic model, and it is the specific 'weighting likelihood' benchmark Koopman & Lit (2019) test and find loses to their dynamic bivariate Poisson.

sources.title: Estimating team strength in the NFL
sources.sample: Methodological derivation, illustrated on NFL-style paired-comparison data (J=32 teams)
sources.key_result: Derives the closed-form ridge-regularized paired-comparison estimator theta_hat = (X'X + lambda*I)^-1 (X'y + lambda*gamma) that a state-space filter reduces to at a single time slice -- a single matrix solve, no MCMC or Kalman recursion required, with lambda chosen by K-fold cross-validation. This is the practical basis for a days-not-weeks fix to the opponent-blindness gap in Gridiron's current blend.

sources.title: A dynamic bivariate Poisson model for analysing and forecasting match results in the English Premier League
sources.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A 178(1)
sources.sample: English Premier League, 2010/11-2011/12 seasons for the betting evaluation
sources.key_result: Abstract/summary only (paywalled full text): reports a significant positive betting return over bookmaker odds using the same dynamic bivariate Poisson framework S2 extends to 6 leagues; cited as corroborating context, not independently verified in full here.

candidates.candidate: Replace nfl-preseason-blend.js's single-shot normal-normal blend with a real recursive state-space (Kalman) filter: paired-comparison design, separate week-to-week and season-to-season evolution variances, team-specific HFA -- the actual Glickman & Stern (1998) model, closed-form (linear-Gaussian, no MCMC needed for point/variance estimates).
candidates.fixes_finding: nfl-team-strength.js [actually nfl-preseason-blend.js] mixes stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update
candidates.mechanism: blendedTeamRating() recomputes weightOnPrior = per_game_variance/(per_game_variance + n*prior_variance) fresh at forecast time from two GLOBAL calibrated scalars, with no recursive state and no split between week-to-week vs season-to-season variance. A Kalman recursion carries a posterior mean+variance forward game-by-game with two distinct evolution-noise terms (sigma_w, sigma_s from S1), which is what 'state-space' actually means and what the current code does not do.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/nfl-state-space-ratings.js; new table nfl_team_strength_kalman(season, week, team, mean, variance, hfa_mean, hfa_variance) populated incrementally from game_lines(season,week,team,opponent,home,team_score,opp_score); expose the same {names, row} contract as teamStrengthGbmFeatures()/preseasonBlendGbmFeatures() in nfl-team-strength.js so it plugs into buildGbmDataset({extraFeatures}) with zero changes to the champion path.
candidates.expected_value: Uncertain but plausible: the current single-differential blend already tested non-significant on the existing harness (pooled MAE 9.86 vs 9.84, CI includes zero); a genuinely paired-comparison, opponent-adjusted, two-scale filter is a materially different (and per Glickman & Stern's own 110-game holdout, real if modest) signal, not a guaranteed win.
candidates.exit_test: Run teamStrengthWalkForward({challengerFeatures: kalmanFeatures()}); promote only under the file's own existing rule -- significant MAE reduction on >=2 of 3 walk-forward test seasons (2023-2025), block-resampled by week.

candidates.candidate: Cheaper, faster fix for the same defect: fix ONLY the opponent-blindness bug (not the missing recursion) by replacing blendedTeamRating's per-team raw-average inSeasonMean with a joint ridge-regularized paired-comparison regression across all 32 teams each week -- Glickman & Stern's own closed-form estimator theta_hat = (X'X + lambda*I)^-1 (X'y + lambda*gamma), refit weekly with gamma = the existing prior-season blend.
candidates.fixes_finding: nfl-team-strength.js [nfl-preseason-blend.js] mixes stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update
candidates.mechanism: Current in-season component averages a team's OWN margins with no adjustment for opponent strength -- two teams with identical average margins get identical in-season estimates even if one played the league's best defenses and the other its worst. A single 32x32 (well, 31-parameter after the identifiability constraint) matrix solve per week fixes this without touching the already-correct (post-M01) prior/posterior weighting math.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a function in nfl-preseason-blend.js (or a small new module) that builds the +1/-1 design matrix from game_lines rows played so far this season, solves the ridge system once (numeric.js or a hand-rolled Gauss-Jordan on <=32 dims -- no new dependency needed), and feeds the residual (this team's ridge rating minus its opponent-blind blended rating) as an additional differential column through the same GBM-feature seam as F1.
candidates.expected_value: Higher confidence, lower ceiling than F1: fixes a real, identifiable bug (opponent-blindness) cheaply; whether it moves held-out MAE enough to pass the promotion bar is untested but the mechanism itself is not in dispute the way F1's full recursive filter's incremental value is.
candidates.exit_test: Same teamStrengthWalkForward harness; also unit-test that two teams with equal raw average margin but different opponent strength now get different ridge ratings (a property the current code provably lacks).

candidates.candidate: Wire blendedTeamRating's already-computed posterior_se (or F1's posterior variance) into a real predictive interval for the drive simulator / GBM residual instead of an assumed-normal SD.
candidates.fixes_finding: No conformal or otherwise honestly-calibrated uncertainty interval exists anywhere in the pipeline -- margins/totals are point forecasts with an assumed-normal SD
candidates.mechanism: nfl-preseason-blend.js's own header states plainly that nothing consumes posterior_se today ('nothing has been wired to consume it that way yet') even though the module already computes a real posterior standard error every call. A state-space/ridge fit's posterior variance is a legitimate, cheap first ingredient for an honestly team-specific (not one-size-fits-all) predictive SD, ahead of and complementary to a full conformal wrapper.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Feed sqrt(posterior_variance_home + posterior_variance_away + residual_market_variance) into wherever nfl-drive-sim.js or the margin/total GBM currently assumes a fixed-normal SD, as a first step; this does not by itself constitute a conformal interval and should be labeled a diagnostic input, not a calibrated guarantee, until validated.
candidates.expected_value: Moderate -- cheap to wire, immediately testable against realized outcomes (does the team-varying SD improve calibration vs the current flat assumed-normal SD), but does not solve the larger conformal-calibration gap by itself.
candidates.exit_test: Compare empirical coverage of prediction intervals built from the new team-varying SD vs the current flat SD, on the same held-out seasons; only ship if coverage improves or stays neutral, since a mis-scaled posterior SD could make calibration worse.

candidates.candidate: Implement a score-driven (GAS) dynamic bivariate Poisson / Skellam joint scoring model (Koopman & Lit's actual method) as a new generative capability: one coherent model producing a correlated (home_score, away_score) distribution, updated by the scaled score of the predictive likelihood each week -- not a Kalman filter.
candidates.mechanism: Gridiron has no shared-latent-factor joint model of home/away scores anywhere: nfl-gbm.js predicts a margin residual and totals separately with no correlation structure between them, and no distributional (as opposed to point) forecast of either. Koopman & Lit's own head-to-head result (this model beats a literal state-space/Kalman fit on precision AND costs <10 sec vs ~1 hour per fit) makes this the correct FIRST dynamic model to build, ahead of F1's more expensive recursive filter.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/nfl-score-driven.js; new table nfl_score_driven_strength(season, week, team, attack, defense, updated_at) updated by a closed-form GAS recursion after each week's games; exposes a full joint P(home_score, away_score) via the bivariate Poisson pmf (lambda1, lambda2, shared covariance lambda3), from which margin AND total distributions are derived from ONE model instead of Gridiron's current separate point estimates -- and could eventually be graded against the props module (the project's one area of genuine measured skill) as a distributional upgrade path.
candidates.expected_value: High optionality: closed-form and cheap per Koopman & Lit's own timing result, produces calibrated joint distributions where only point estimates exist today, and is a natural feeder for both margin/total forecasts and eventually a real correlation term for teaser-leg/same-game correlation (currently assumed independent).
candidates.exit_test: Grade via the same teamStrengthWalkForward-style walk-forward harness (adapted for a distributional loss, e.g. log-score or CRPS on margin/total rather than point MAE), promotion only on >=2 of 3 significant seasons -- do not ship on backtest plausibility alone.

candidates.candidate: Port mikemiller442's working Stan bivariate-Poisson model (adapted for NFL, points-per-drive as the Poisson unit rather than soccer goals) as an OFFLINE research/validation tool run outside the live app with cmdstanpy, to independently cross-check N1/F1's point estimates against a full MCMC posterior and run Glickman & Stern's own posterior-predictive model-checking diagnostics (Section 5 of S1: simulate replicate data, compare discrepancy statistics, report tail probabilities).
candidates.mechanism: Gridiron has zero MCMC/Stan/PyMC tooling anywhere in the stack today (confirmed: no .stan files, no pymc/cmdstanpy dependency in the repo) and no posterior-predictive model-checking method distinct from backtest-significance.js's effect-size/CLV bootstrap testing.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: A standalone script (not touching the live DB or any running process) under a research/ directory: exports game_lines history to a flat file, fits the adapted Stan model with cmdstanpy, and reproduces S1's D1-D4 discrepancy diagnostics against Gridiron's own actual scoring history as a one-time or periodic audit, independent of and never gating the production pipeline.
candidates.expected_value: Moderate: primarily a validation/ground-truth tool rather than a production model, but directly answers 'is our closed-form ridge/GAS approximation actually close to the full Bayesian posterior' -- a real, previously-unavailable check.
candidates.exit_test: If the offline MCMC posterior and the production closed-form fit (F1/F2/N1) disagree materially (e.g. rank correlation of team ratings below some prespecified threshold), treat that as a flag to revisit the production approximation rather than trusting either uncritically.

candidates.candidate: Bring Glickman & Stern's posterior-predictive model-checking method itself (not just the rating model) into Gridiron as a standing diagnostic, run against the EXISTING champion GBM residual model, independent of whether any state-space rating ships.
candidates.mechanism: backtest-significance.js and audit-registry.js test whether an effect/edge is statistically real (paired bootstrap, Holm/Sidak correction); neither simulates replicate datasets from a fitted model and compares a discrepancy statistic the way S1 Section 5 does. This is a structurally different, complementary validation technique Gridiron has never had: it catches model MISSPECIFICATION (e.g., team-specific residual-variance heterogeneity the champion GBM implicitly assumes away) rather than just measuring whether an edge beats zero.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New diagnostic function, e.g. server/services/posterior-predictive-check.js: simulate replicate game outcomes from the champion GBM's fitted residual distribution, compute a discrepancy statistic (S1's D1/D2: range of per-team or per-season residual variance) on real vs simulated data, report the tail probability -- run once against the CURRENT champion before any new rating model ships, as an independent sanity check on an assumption (homoscedastic, team-agnostic residual variance) nothing currently tests.
candidates.expected_value: Moderate, mostly diagnostic: low cost relative to the two rating-model candidates, and useful regardless of whether F1/F2/N1 ever ship, since it audits an assumption baked into the ALREADY-DEPLOYED champion model.
candidates.exit_test: If the diagnostic finds the champion's assumed-homoscedastic residual variance is NOT supported by the data (tail probability far from 0.5 on the team-variance-range statistic), that is itself an actionable finding to route to the champion model's own maintainers, separate from this research thread.

do_not_do: Do not run a Gibbs-sampled MCMC state-space fit (Glickman & Stern's literal S1 method) in the live production pipeline -- their own paper needed 18,000 iterations across 7 parallel chains for one season's fit, and Koopman & Lit's own head-to-head test shows the cheaper score-driven alternative beats it on forecast precision anyway while costing under 10 seconds vs roughly an hour per fit. Use N1's score-driven update for anything that needs to run weekly in-app; reserve any MCMC/Stan fit (N2) for offline, periodic validation only.

Do not let a new state-space/ridge rating become a THIRD untested, disagreeing team-strength implementation sitting alongside nfl-team-strength.js and nfl-preseason-blend.js forever. If F1/F2/N1 fails its walk-forward promotion gate, document the negative result in the same honest, retained-not-reopened style nfl-preseason-blend.js already uses for its own WALK_FORWARD_VERDICT, rather than shipping it anyway or silently abandoning the file.

Do not import Glickman & Stern's (1988-1993 NFL) or Koopman & Lit's (European soccer) fitted variance/decay constants directly -- per-game and prior variance MUST be calibrated from Gridiron's own history the way calibratePreseasonBlend() already does, with the same asOfSeason cutoff-safety discipline (no globally-future-fitted substitute, per the Codex C10 correction already documented in nfl-preseason-blend.js).

Do not treat any of this as a new betting signal or wire it toward stake sizing directly -- per standing project rule, betting only moves through governance gates (model-governance.js registration, the walk-forward promotion bar, beat-the-close.js's live-CLV retirement rule). This research produces feature/diagnostic candidates for that gate, not an approved bet.

Do not copy mikemiller442/Bivariate_Poisson_Soccer's Stan files verbatim into any shipped artifact -- the repo carries no declared license (default all-rights-reserved); re-derive the (short, standard, textbook) bivariate-Poisson Stan model from the published equations in S1-S3 instead if any code needs to leave the research/validation stage.

Do not conflate the two separate defects: opponent-blindness (fixed cheaply by F2's ridge regression, hours of work) and missing recursive state (fixed expensively by F1's real filter, days of work). Building only F1 without F2 still ships an opponent-blind filter with impressive-sounding machinery; building only F2 is a legitimate, complete fix to the specific bug even without ever building F1.

repos.what_it_does: Real, runnable Stan models (bivariate_poisson_no_cov.stan / bivariate_poisson_model.stan / bivariate_poisson_int_cov.stan) implementing the Maher/Karlis-Ntzoufras bivariate Poisson exactly as specified in S1-S3: attack/defense/covariance random effects with inv_gamma priors, poisson(lambda1+lambda3)/poisson(lambda2+lambda3) likelihood, fit via RStan with 5-fold CV against Bradley-Terry/Davidson MLE baselines on 10 EPL seasons.
repos.adoption_path: Re-derive (do not copy, no license) the same ~40-line Stan model spec for N2's offline cmdstanpy validation tool, adapted to points-per-drive as the Poisson unit consistent with nfl-drive-sim.js's own per-drive framing.

repos.what_it_does: An actively-maintained (pushed the same week as this research), NFL-specific Bayesian power-rating and spread-projection engine. backend/model/joint_scoring.py::solve_ridge() is exactly S4's ridge-regularized paired-comparison estimator generalized to a joint weighted-GLS system across all 32 teams with exponential recency weighting (half-life weeks), refit from scratch each week rather than filtered forward. backend/model/preseason.py blends a win-total-market prior with mean-reverted last-season ratings. Walk-forward-calibrated against the closing line with a versioned, gated recommendation ledger (backend/recommendations.py, backend/grading.py) structurally analogous to Gridiron's own beat-the-close.js / model-governance.js.
repos.adoption_path: Use as a working confirmation that F2's ridge-regression fix is production-viable and as a design reference for how to structure the {names,row} extraFeatures contract's weekly refit and recency-weighting choices -- do not port code directly (different stack: Python/Poetry/Postgres vs Gridiron's JS/SQLite), reimplement the equations in JS.

repos.what_it_does: A clean, composable static Dixon-Coles Python library with exponential time-decay weighting (same idea as S3) and modular attack/defense/HFA 'blocks'. No dynamic/state-space extension.
repos.adoption_path: Reference for how to decompose attack/defense/HFA into composable, testable units in application code if F1/N1 grows complex enough to warrant it -- the model class itself (static, weighted-MLE Dixon-Coles) is the specific benchmark S2 found loses to the dynamic bivariate Poisson, so do not adopt the model, only the code shape.

repos.what_it_does: A from-scratch, honestly-labeled reproduction of S3 (Ley et al. 2018), independently recovering the paper's model ordering and optimal ~3-year half-life on a newer data vintage.
repos.adoption_path: Use only as independent confirmation that S3's numbers replicate; no code adoption planned (single notebook, soccer-specific, superseded by the stronger S2/N1 approach for Gridiron's purposes).

result.label: F12: Cold-start / transfer-learning fix for the fantasy weekly-learning loop
result.summary: Confirmed by code read (read-only) the exact chain that makes player_week_engine.heads null at Week 1: priorScores() in player-week-engine.js queries current-season-only rows (week < current), so priorWeeks is empty at week 1; weeklyEnsembleContext() in weekly-ensemble.js returns null on empty priorWeeks with no fallback; captureWeeklyPredictions() in weekly-learning.js then silently `continue`s past any player with null heads instead of capturing a degraded snapshot; and retrainWeeklyWeights()'s own SQL (`WHERE ... AND season_to_date IS NOT NULL`) would exclude such a row even if it were captured. Result: the weekly-learning promotion loop has never had one Week 1 example to grade against. Notably, the repo already contains the fix pattern elsewhere and unused for this path — player-head-registry.js's candidatePlayerHeads() falls every head back to the structural prediction when prior is empty, but the production weeklyEnsembleContext() does not. Sports-forecasting literature (empirical Bayes/hierarchical shrinkage toward a population prior at low sample size, meta-learned fast adaptation, and cross-season Elo carryover blended with external market priors when internal history is zero) gives three converging, well-precedented fixes, plus room for genuinely new capability (state-space player tracking, meta-learned adaptation replacing brute-force grid search, and a true rookie/never-played transfer module) that Gridiron has none of today.

sources.title: In-Season Prediction of Batting Averages: A Field Test of Empirical Bayes and Bayes Methodologies
sources.sample: 432 MLB players, 2005 season, predictions issued after ~45 at-bats, target = rest-of-season batting average
sources.key_result: Hierarchical Bayes has substantially lower total squared error than a naive current-season-only baseline; empirical Bayes lands between naive and full hierarchical Bayes — the direct quantitative precedent for shrinking hard toward a population prior when current-period evidence is near zero.

sources.title: Meta-Learning Framework with Applications to Zero-Shot Time-Series Forecasting
sources.authors: Boris N. Oreshkin, Dmitri Carpov, Nicolas Chapados, Yoshua Bengio
sources.sample: Meta-trained on M4 (100k series) + FRED (290k series); zero-shot evaluated with no target-domain retraining on M3 (3,003 series), Tourism (1,311 series), Electricity (370 meters), Traffic (963 lanes)
sources.key_result: Zero-shot M4→M3 sMAPE 12.44 vs Theta baseline 13.01; M4→Tourism MAPE 18.82 vs Theta 20.88; M4-Hourly→Electricity ND 0.09 matching DeepAR's 0.09; ablation shows meta-learning alone contributes 1.2%-7.8% of the gain over a non-meta single block.

sources.title: Bayesian Hierarchical Modeling Applied to Fantasy Football Projections for Increased Insight and Confidence
sources.sample: 2014 NFL weekly fantasy data, trained 2014 tested 2015, positions QB/RB/WR/TE with team/rank-quartile hierarchy
sources.key_result: MAE 6.08 vs 5.99 for a plain 7-game rolling average (essentially no point-accuracy gain); real value was calibration (low-SD predictions were in fact more accurate); sparse-history players caused convergence trouble handled only by inflated SD, not real transfer — an honest negative result showing partial pooling alone doesn't fix cold start without an external/cross-period prior to feed it.

sources.title: NFL Elo Model (documenting FiveThirtyEight's preseason carryover methodology)
sources.sample: All NFL teams/seasons 2003-present under FiveThirtyEight's published Elo methodology
sources.key_result: Preseason rating = 1/3 regression toward league mean (1505) of prior season's ending Elo, blended 2/3 with a market-derived prior (Vegas win total, ~34 Elo/win, floor ~1250); for zero-history entities (first season) the market prior gets 100% weight (w1=0, w2=1) — the practitioner template for cross-period decay plus external-market fallback at true cold start.

sources.title: Stein's Paradox in Statistics (James-Stein shrinkage on 1970 batting averages)
sources.authors: Bradley Efron, Carl Morris (1977); re-derivation cross-checked via secondary sources
sources.sample: 18 MLB players, 1970 season, first 45 at-bats shrunk toward grand average 0.265 to predict rest of season
sources.key_result: Total squared prediction error: naive per-player average 0.086 vs James-Stein shrinkage 0.027 — less than one-third the error; canonical smallest-scale demonstration of Gridiron's exact situation (near-zero new evidence, shrink hard toward group mean).

candidates.candidate: Cross-season transfer for the ensemble heads: extend priorScores() to fall back to the same player's prior-season weeks (with a season-decay weight matching projections.js's existing SEASON_WEIGHT = {0:1,1:0.55,2:0.28,else:0.12}) whenever the current season has zero rows, instead of returning an empty array.
candidates.fixes_finding: player_week_engine.heads is null at Week 1 because priorScores() (player-week-engine.js) only queries `season = ? AND week < ?`, never crossing the season boundary, so weeklyEnsembleContext() (weekly-ensemble.js:29) always sees priorWeeks=[] and returns null at cold start.
candidates.mechanism: Empirical-Bayes/hierarchical shrinkage toward a same-entity prior-period estimate when current-period n=0, exactly Brown (2008)'s and Efron-Morris's demonstrated approach, using season-decay weighting Gridiron already validated and shipped in the structural model.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Edit priorScores() in server/services/player-week-engine.js (~line 123) to union in player_week_usage rows from season-1/season-2 when the season=season query is empty, weighted via the same SEASON_WEIGHT function already imported/used in server/services/projections.js:75; weeklyEnsembleContext() (server/services/weekly-ensemble.js:28) needs no change once priorWeeks is non-empty.
candidates.expected_value: Populates season_to_date/last3/last1/median with a real, precedented number instead of null for every player's first game of a season (not just Week 1 — also mid-season debuts), unblocking capture at the source.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest: rebuild player_week_engine for Week 1 of 2023/2024/2025 with the fix; confirm heads is non-null for every player with >=1 prior-season game logged, and MAE/Spearman of the resulting week-1 ensemble prediction vs actual beats the current structural-only fallback on held-out actuals.

candidates.candidate: Mirror the existing fallback pattern from candidatePlayerHeads() (player-head-registry.js:55, which already sets every head to the structural value when prior is empty) into the production weeklyEnsembleContext(), and change captureWeeklyPredictions() to always capture a snapshot (tagged mode='cold_start_structural_only') instead of `continue`-skipping when heads is null.
candidates.fixes_finding: captureWeeklyPredictions() in weekly-learning.js:69 does `if (!engine?.heads) continue;`, silently discarding every Week-1 (and mid-season debut) player from ever entering weekly_prediction_snapshots, so the weekly-learning loop has zero forward snapshots to eventually grade at cold start — exactly the finding text ("never captured one forward snapshot in its life").
