candidates.candidate: Add an explicit external-market head sourced from Gridiron's own player-prop pipeline (server/services/nfl-props.js, the project's one area of measured skill: 2+ TD Brier skill +27%) as a week-1/no-history fallback, analogous to FiveThirtyEight's Vegas-win-total blend used specifically when internal history is zero.
candidates.fixes_finding: Same null-heads defect (weeklyEnsembleContext/player-week-engine.js), but proposes replacing the plain structural fallback (F2) with a stronger informed prior for the highest-uncertainty cold-start case, using a source Gridiron already ingests but currently only uses for betting, not fantasy cold start.
candidates.mechanism: External-market prior substitution when internal cross-period history is unavailable or thin — the exact FiveThirtyEight w1=0,w2=1 rule (Reef Data Lab) for zero-history entities.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Join player-week-engine.js's per-player projection to nfl-props.js's projectWeek()/priorFfOpportunity() output (already referenced at player-week-engine.js's engine.external_benchmarks.ffopportunity) on player_id+week; when F1's cross-season history is empty, set the season_to_date/last1 heads from the props-implied projection instead of pure structural.
candidates.expected_value: A materially better-informed Week-1/debut prediction than pure structural fallback, drawing on the codebase's one genuinely skilled model instead of duplicating a weaker signal; secondary benefit of surfacing whether the props pipeline's skill actually transfers to fantasy scoring.
candidates.exit_test: 3-season backtest comparing week-1 MAE/Spearman of structural-only (F2) vs props-informed (F3) fallback against real week-1 outcomes; ship only if F3 beats F2 by a pre-registered margin (e.g., MAE improvement >=0.15 pts, consistent sign across all 3 seasons).

candidates.candidate: Replace the frozen, hand-fit convex ensemble (WEEKLY_ENSEMBLE_WEIGHTS in weekly-ensemble.js, fit on 2023 only per its own header comment) with a persistent state-space/Kalman-filter latent skill estimate per player that carries an explicit prior variance shrinking as evidence accrues game by game, rather than a fixed 5-weight blend refit only via brute-force grid search.
candidates.mechanism: Continuous Bayesian filtering of a latent "current-season true talent" state (prior variance wide at week 1, narrowing with each observed game) generalizes the one-shot Week-1 shrinkage fix (F1/F2) into a principled framework covering every week of the season, not just the cold-start edge case.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New service alongside player-week-engine.js; state persisted per player_id in a new table (e.g. player_skill_state), updated after each settled week via settleWeeklyPredictions() in weekly-learning.js; would eventually replace WEEKLY_ENSEMBLE_WEIGHTS in weekly-ensemble.js as the source of the ppg blend.
candidates.expected_value: Removes the entire class of "heads went null / fixed weights stale" bug family (this defect and future variants of it) by making uncertainty-aware adaptation the default behavior instead of a special-cased fallback; also naturally produces calibrated interval widths (something Gridiron has nowhere per the FOUND list's conformal-interval gap) as a byproduct of the filter's posterior variance.
candidates.exit_test: Run a full season backtest with the state-space tracker vs the current frozen-weight ensemble; require both improvement in weekly MAE/Spearman AND correctly calibrated 80% interval coverage (78-82%, the same gate retrainWeeklyWeights() already uses) before considering promotion.

candidates.candidate: Meta-learned fast-adaptation initialization (Oreshkin-style) that learns how to adapt from N games of new-season evidence across all historical player-seasons, replacing weekly-learning.js's brute-force WEIGHT_GRID search (grid() enumerates every 0.1-increment convex combination of 5 fixed heads, refit only when >=75 settled rows exist per position).
candidates.mechanism: Meta-learning across many "tasks" (each player-season is a task) to learn an adaptation procedure that generalizes to a brand-new task (a new player-season) with very few examples — the literal definition of the cold-start meta-learning framing in Oreshkin et al. (2021), as opposed to grid-searching one static weight vector per position.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Would replace fitPosition()/WEIGHT_GRID in weekly-learning.js with a meta-trained model (e.g. a small MAML-style update rule or a learned initialization) trained across all season-player histories in player_week_usage, evaluated against the same champion/challenger promotion gate already in retrainWeeklyWeights().
candidates.expected_value: A genuinely adaptive per-position, per-sample-size weighting instead of one static grid-searched vector reused for every player regardless of how many games of evidence exist; directly targets fast adaptation at low N, which is the whole cold-start problem generalized past Week 1 (trades, injuries returns, rookies establishing role).
candidates.exit_test: Compare meta-learned adaptation vs current grid-searched champion weights specifically on the lowest-evidence quartile of settled snapshots (players with <=3 games of current-season history); require a statistically significant MAE improvement on that quartile without regressing the full-evidence quartile.

candidates.candidate: A true never-played-an-NFL-snap transfer module for rookies and role-elevated players (nearest-neighbor archetype matching using role_scenario_engine.js's role/usage taxonomy and player-head-registry.js's structural feature set) since Gridiron currently has zero mechanism for players with no player_week_usage rows in ANY season — a harder cold start than the Week 1 returning-veteran case this finding names.
candidates.mechanism: Content/role-based cold start (the classic recommender-systems answer to "new item, zero interaction history": match on features/archetype rather than history) combined with the documented caution that cross-level transfer (e.g. college-to-pro performance prediction) is often weak, so this should be scoped as an explicit low-confidence prior, not treated as equal-strength evidence to F1's same-player cross-season transfer.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New lookup in player-week-engine.js's buildPlayerWeekEngine(): when structural's history() (projections.js) finds zero rows for a player at any season, fall back to a nearest-archetype match against role_scenario_engine.js's usage clusters (same draft capital tier, same offensive scheme, same depth-chart slot) rather than the generic positional prior currently used.
candidates.expected_value: Currently these players get whatever the positional-average shrinkage prior in projections.js assigns (same treatment as a replacement-level veteran); a real archetype-matched prior would differentiate a first-round rookie RB from a UDFA rookie RB at week 1, which the current structural model cannot do until it sees actual snaps.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest on the last 3 draft classes: compare archetype-matched week-1-of-career prediction vs the current generic-positional-prior prediction against actual week-1 outcomes for all rookies who played meaningful snaps; ship only if archetype matching beats the generic prior on MAE, given the literature's caution that this transfer is often weak.

do_not_do: Do not touch fantasy-football-dashboard's live database, run its tests/builds, or restart any of its processes — a live server is capturing real Week 1 2026 games through Sunday; every finding above came from read-only grep/Read.

Do not ship a full hierarchical/state-space rewrite (N1) as the first change — Rome's own hierarchical-Bayes fantasy blog result (MAE 6.08 vs 5.99 naive) shows partial pooling alone, without a real prior to pool from, is not obviously better than a rolling average; land F1/F2 (cheap, precedented, uses existing SEASON_WEIGHT and the existing candidatePlayerHeads fallback pattern) before any heavier architecture.

Do not let the props-informed fallback (F3) get promoted without the 3-season backtest gate — nfl-props.js's measured skill (2+ TD Brier +27%) does not automatically transfer to full fantasy-point cold-start prediction; treat it as a hypothesis to test, not an assumed win.

Do not treat rookie/never-played transfer (N3) as equally strong evidence to same-player cross-season transfer (F1) — the football-performance transferability literature found in this research explicitly flags limited transferability across competition levels; scope N3's output as a low-confidence prior, not a confident point estimate.

Do not retrain or refit weekly ensemble weights on a dataset that mixes pre-fix null-degraded rows with post-fix rows without a version/mode flag (engine.mode already exists for this) — retrainWeeklyWeights()'s data_hash dedup will otherwise silently mix incomparable snapshot generations.

Do not expand this fix into a general season-long uncertainty overhaul in the same change — N1's calibrated intervals are a legitimate byproduct worth pursuing later, but bundling it with the Week-1 heads-null fix risks blocking the small, high-value F1/F2 patch behind a much larger, unvalidated rewrite.

result.label: F14 — Entity resolution for game/team/player keys
result.summary: Read team-codes.js, nfl-contract-key.js, and player-ids.js in full: the team resolver and player-id crosswalk are actually deterministic, fail-closed linkage (not naive string matching) — but neither carries a confidence score, and two concrete downstream defects exist: (1) polymarket.js:49-112 extracts player names from free text via regex and stores the raw string with zero call to the existing resolvePlayerId() crosswalk, so Polymarket props never join to Gridiron's own player-prop model; (2) polymarket-lines.js:88-101,251-254 infers game/team orientation by trial-querying the schedule and, on failure, fabricates an unjoinable synthetic id (`pm:${event_title}`) instead of quarantining — the exact "row we invented" anti-pattern nfl-contract-key.js's own header explicitly refuses to allow one layer up. Researched Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic linkage theory (m/u-probabilities, additive match weight, calibrated match probability) via Splink's docs and a 2019 Statistics Canada arXiv paper with a concrete N=32,000/K=15 simulation showing the classical conditional-independence estimator is biased once linkage-variable correlation is realistic — Gridiron's exact situation. Cloned and read splink (comparison_library.py's graded-comparison-level API, including ColumnsReversedLevel — directly matches the away/home-orientation problem) and recordlinkage (compare.py's pluggable string-distance classes) source; read dedupe's README for its active-learning alternative. Proposed a canonical entity_link output shape ({ok, matched_id, match_probability, method, evidence, ambiguous_alternates}) that composes with the existing quarantine convention rather than replacing the closed-vocabulary team resolver, which should keep its deterministic design.

sources.title: The Fellegi-Sunter Model (Splink docs, full theory restatement of Fellegi & Sunter 1969)
sources.key_result: Formalizes match weight M = log2(λ/(1-λ)) + Σ log2(m_i/u_i) across compared fields (additive under conditional independence) and final match probability Pr(match|obs) = 2^M/(1+2^M) — every pair gets a calibrated probability, not a boolean; explicitly states the additivity assumes cross-field independence, which fails when features are correlated.
sources.sample: N/A — methodology document, not an empirical study

sources.title: Revisiting the probabilistic method of record linkage
sources.key_result: Twin-register simulation, N=32,000 individuals, K=15 binary linkage variables, 2 scenarios (independent vs. correlated linkage-variable errors), 100 repetitions, mN=128 sampled pairs per repetition: the classical Fellegi-Sunter conditional-independence estimator is consistent under independence but biased under realistic correlation; their EM-estimated finite-mixture-over-neighbour-count model stays consistent in both scenarios without labeled training pairs. Authors' own stated limitation: requires the 'proper linkage problem' identification condition and needs a compute-heavy parametric bootstrap to test the number of mixture components.
sources.sample: Simulated twin registers, N=32,000 records, K=15 binary fields, 100 repetitions per scenario
sources.authors: A. Dasylva, A. Goussanou, D. Ajavon, H. Abousaleh

candidates.candidate: Add a graded confidence score to teamResolver() and eventKey() outputs using Jaro-Winkler distance as a second-tier signal before falling back to null
candidates.fixes_finding: FOUND: 'game/team identity matching across sources is done with ad hoc string matching in team-codes.js/nfl-contract-key.js, not real entity resolution' — concretely, teamResolver() (team-codes.js:50-86) and eventKey() (nfl-contract-key.js:128-139) return only a boolean match/null with no confidence number, so a near-miss spelling cannot be distinguished from a random string and every new variant needs a manual dictionary edit.

candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/team-codes.js teamResolver() (lines 50-86); server/services/nfl-contract-key.js eventKey() (lines 128-139)
candidates.expected_value: Modest for the 32-team vocabulary itself (it's a near-solved closed problem) but the confidence field composes directly with fix-1 and fix-2's quarantine reasons, giving one consistent evidence-tagged shape across team, event, and player resolution instead of three different boolean conventions.

candidates.candidate: Stand up a Splink probabilistic-linkage pass, in sqlite backend, specifically for the 12.4M-row Polymarket quote tape against ESPN/nflverse game and player identifiers
candidates.mechanism: Splink's Fellegi-Sunter EM estimation (estimate_parameters_using_expectation_maximisation) learns m/u probabilities per comparison level from the unlabeled data itself (no hand-labeled training set required for the base model), producing a calibrated match_probability per candidate pair rather than Gridiron's current boolean joins. Use ForenameSurnameComparison for player names and a custom comparison for (date, home, away) for games, blocked on eastern_game_date to keep the Cartesian product tractable.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New module server/services/entity-link.js consuming the existing SQLite database via db/index.js's rows()/row() helpers, feeding the polymarket_props and polymarket_line_moves tables (server/services/polymarket.js, polymarket-lines.js) plus players and espn_line_moves; splink ships a native SQLite (duckdb-free) backend appropriate to this project's scale
candidates.expected_value: This is the capability Gridiron has literally none of today: every join in the codebase (team-codes.js, player-ids.js, nfl-contract-key.js) is deterministic exact-match-with-fallback. A probabilistic layer gives a genuine confidence score for the messiest, highest-value unused asset in the project — the 12.4M-row Polymarket tape FOUND says is 'essentially unused for anything beyond spread-ladder construction' — and is the only way to use it for props/player matching at all, since regex extraction alone (current state) cannot resolve ambiguous or malformed names.
candidates.exit_test: On a hand-labeled validation set of 200 Polymarket prop titles matched to internal player_id by a human, Splink's predicted match_probability >=0.85 should agree with the human label on >=95% of pairs, and the resolution rate on the full 1,800-market backlog should exceed the current ~0% (since no resolution happens today).

candidates.candidate: Build a versioned crosswalk table (game_identity_xwalk) that stores every provider's raw event/game string alongside the canonical event_key and the confidence/method that produced the link, queryable and auditable independent of any single service module

candidates.expected_value: Today identity resolution logic is duplicated and inconsistent across at least polymarket-lines.js (schedule-trial heuristic) and team-codes.js/nfl-contract-key.js (dictionary + exact string). A single persisted crosswalk with confidence and an audit trail turns 'was this game matched correctly' from an unanswerable question into a queryable one, and lets a human correction (confirmed_by_human) permanently override a low-confidence automated link without re-running any matching logic.

candidates.candidate: Add dedupe-style active-learning labeling for the small set of genuinely ambiguous player/team-name cases that survive automated resolution, rather than leaving them permanently null
candidates.mechanism: dedupe's workflow (propose uncertain pairs, human labels y/n/u, retrain) is the right tool specifically for the residual ambiguous cases after Splink/deterministic resolution — e.g., two players who share a normalized name (player-ids.js's own nameCollisions set, currently a permanent dead end) — where a small number of one-time human labels resolves an otherwise-unresolvable ambiguity using contextual fields (team, position, season) dedupe's classifier can learn to weigh.

do_not_do: Do not run Splink's Spark or DuckDB-cluster backends — Gridiron's SQLite dataset is small enough (thousands of players, at most ~12M Polymarket rows) that Splink's own sqlite backend is the right fit; standing up Spark is pure overhead with no benefit at this scale.

Do not replace teamResolver() with a learned probabilistic model — 32 teams is a solved, closed vocabulary where u-probabilities (how often a string appears when it's NOT that team) are close to meaningless to estimate from data; keep the deterministic resolver and only add a confidence field to its output.

Do not adopt dedupe's active-learning UI as the primary tool for the one-time ~1,800-row Polymarket prop backlog — active learning earns its cost on datasets needing continuous, ongoing labeling at volume; a single ~200-pair hand-labeled validation set plus Splink's unsupervised EM parameter estimation is cheaper and already exists as a built codepath.

Do not ship the crosswalk-table or Splink-linkage work as a silent replacement for the existing quarantine reasons in nfl-contract-key.js — any new low-confidence match must add a new named quarantine reason (e.g. low_confidence_entity_match, unmatched_event) rather than either bypassing quarantine or being folded into unresolved_team, which would blur two different failure modes the project currently tracks separately.

Do not let this work touch or duplicate the five-disagreeing-CLV-implementations problem or the fantasy player_week_engine cold-start problem — different researchers' scope tonight; note the overlap (player-ids.js resolution feeds both) for cross-reference only.

Do not fabricate a synthetic joinable id (the pm:${event_title} pattern in polymarket-lines.js:254) anywhere in this work, including in any new code — a failed link is a quarantined row with a typed reason, never an invented key that looks like it could join.

result.label: F11-conformal-calibration
result.summary: Located the exact assumed-normal-SD defect: server/services/nfl-market.js computes one pooled marginStd/totalStd (lines ~176-181) and feeds it into a plain normalCdf win-probability at line 435 — no interval, no covariate-adaptivity, no coverage guarantee. Read three primary conformal-prediction papers in full (Angelopoulos & Bates 2021 intro/guarantee; Romano/Patterson/Candès 2019 CQR, with the exact Fig.2 numbers showing CQR wins on interval width at matched 90% coverage; Barber/Candès/Ramdas/Tibshirani 2023 non-exchangeable/NexCP, with real electricity-market coverage numbers showing weighted quantiles recover 90% coverage under drift where plain conformal drops to 85%). Found and cloned 5 code repos (MAPIE, aangelopoulos/conformal-prediction, yromano/cqr, marcopeix/conformal-ts, astrogilda/tsbootstrap) — all Python, so treated as algorithm references (borrow-idea) rather than ports, since the actual math (split-conformal quantile, CQR interval, NexCP weighted quantile) is ~15-30 lines each and cheaper to hand-write in JS against nfl-market.js's existing residual arrays than to bridge languages. Produced 6 candidates (3 fix, 3 new) plus a do-not-do list emphasizing that calibration must not be applied on top of the drive-simulator's known physics bugs or the ensemble's degenerate shrinkage-to-market forecast, and that "well-calibrated" is not "profitable."

sources.title: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification
sources.sample: Worked ImageNet classification example with ~500-example calibration set; general theory applies to any exchangeable calibration+test pair.
sources.key_result: Split conformal gives the finite-sample, distribution-free marginal coverage guarantee 1-alpha <= P(Y_test in C(X_test)) <= 1-alpha + 1/(n+1) for ANY base model and ANY data distribution, provided exchangeability holds -- exactly the property nfl-market.js's assumed-normal SD and its own ad hoc bootstrap both lack.

sources.title: Conformalized Quantile Regression
sources.authors: Yaniv Romano, Evan Patterson, Emmanuel Candès
sources.sample: Simulated heteroscedastic regression data with outliers (Figure 2), n as in the paper's split; also 11 real UCI/benchmark regression datasets, 80/20 train/test, 20 repeated splits, alpha=0.1.
sources.key_result: At matched 90% target coverage: standard split conformal 91.4% coverage / avg interval length 2.91; locally-adaptive split conformal 91.7% / 2.86; CQR (their method) 91.06% / 1.99 -- roughly 32% narrower than plain split conformal at the same coverage, because width adapts to covariates instead of using one global SD (the exact bug nfl-market.js has).

sources.title: Conformal Prediction Beyond Exchangeability
sources.authors: Rina Foygel Barber, Emmanuel J. Candès, Aaditya Ramdas, Ryan J. Tibshirani
sources.sample: Real ELEC2 Australian electricity dataset, N=3,444 after filtering (genuine non-exchangeable time series); also 2020 US presidential election county data (1,119 train / 1,957 test) and N=2,000 simulated drift settings.
sources.key_result: Target 90% coverage: plain split conformal (CP+LS) achieves only 85.2% coverage on real drifting electricity data (width 0.565); the weighted NexCP+LS recovers 89.0% (width 0.606); the nonsymmetric NexCP+WLS recovers 89.3% at a NARROWER width (0.527) than the undercovering plain method -- direct evidence that exponentially-weighted quantiles fix coverage loss under drift, which is nfl-market.js's exact situation (it pools residuals 1999-2024 and separately fits a season-to-season carryover decay because ratings drift).

sources.title: conformal_ts NexCP implementation (source code, read for algorithm verification)
sources.sample: Full source of NonexchangeableConformalPrediction class plus its unit tests (test_nexcp.py).
sources.key_result: Confirms the exact Barber et al. weighted-quantile construction in working, tested code: weights w_i = rho^(n-1-i), threshold target (1-alpha)(W+1)/W clipped to [0,1], with an effective-sample-size guard on rho -- used as an implementation cross-check, not as new experimental evidence.

candidates.candidate: Replace the Gaussian win-probability in nfl-market.js scoreAccuracy() with a split-conformal quantile of the same residuals it already computes.
candidates.fixes_finding: server/services/nfl-market.js line 435: `const p = normalCdf(r.predMargin / r.marginStd);` assumes a normal shape; marginStd (lines 176-181) is one pooled global SD applied to every game -- the exact 'assumed-normal SD, no calibrated interval' defect from tonight's audit.
candidates.mechanism: marginResiduals/totalResiduals arrays already exist in fitModel()'s return object. Instead of stdev()+normalCdf, take the (1-alpha)(1+1/n)-th empirical quantile of |residual| (Angelopoulos & Bates Eq.1) as the half-width, and read win-probability off the empirical residual CDF directly rather than a Gaussian CDF -- this is literally what bootstrapProb() next to it already gestures at, formalized with a proven coverage guarantee instead of an ad hoc IID resample.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a ~15-line `conformalQuantile(residuals, alpha)` helper in nfl-market.js (or the new shared module, F11-6); call it in scoreAccuracy() in place of `normalCdf(r.predMargin / r.marginStd)`, and expose the returned half-width alongside predicted_margin/predicted_total in predictGame()'s return object.
candidates.expected_value: Turns an unverifiable Gaussian assumption into a number with a proven, testable finite-sample coverage property; makes nfl-market.js's own accuracy self-report honest about whether its stated confidence matches reality.
candidates.exit_test: On the existing walk-forward evaluation seasons, empirical coverage of the new interval must land within the guaranteed band (>= 1-alpha and <= 1-alpha+1/(n_calib+1)); if it doesn't, the calibration set is not exchangeable with the test games and the fix is wrong until re-scoped (see do_not_do on pooling).

candidates.candidate: Add CQR (conditional-quantile conformal) so margin/total interval WIDTH varies by game instead of using nfl-market.js's single global marginStd/totalStd for every matchup.
candidates.fixes_finding: Tonight's finding that margins/totals are point forecasts with an assumed-normal SD -- specifically the part of that defect CQR was invented to fix: a constant-width interval regardless of how lopsided or close the game is (a 3-point pick'em and a 17-point mismatch get the identical marginStd today).
candidates.mechanism: Romano/Patterson/Candès 2019: fit two conditional quantile functions (low/high) via pinball-loss regression on covariates, conformalize the residual-to-quantile gap on a held-out calibration split, output [q_lo(x)-Q, q_hi(x)+Q]. Read result: ~32% narrower intervals than a global-SD approach at matched 90% coverage (Fig.2: CQR 91.06%/1.99 vs split conformal 91.4%/2.91).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New small linear-in-covariates pinball-loss quantile fit (covariates: |spread|, home/away, dome/outdoor, rest-day differential -- all already available where predictGame() is called) inside nfl-market.js or the shared module; wire predicted_margin_low/high into predictGame()'s return and into any consumer of spread-probabilities.js that currently only sees a point spread.
candidates.expected_value: First covariate-adaptive uncertainty band in the pipeline; feeds directly into staking/abstention sizing (Nick's governance-gate rule) with an interval that's actually informative about which games are more/less certain, not a flat constant.
candidates.exit_test: Held-out coverage stays at target (~90%) AND average interval width is measurably narrower than the current flat-marginStd approach on the same held-out games, specifically narrower for lopsided spreads and no worse for pick'ems -- if width doesn't vary with |spread| at all, the covariate quantile fit isn't adding anything over the status quo.

candidates.candidate: Reweight nfl-market.js's existing bootstrapProb() resampler with NexCP-style exponential decay instead of drawing uniformly from all pooled residuals.
candidates.fixes_finding: bootstrapProb() (nfl-market.js lines ~187-215) already resamples real historical residuals instead of assuming a Gaussian shape (a good instinct the audit's summary undersells), but it draws UNIFORMLY from residuals pooled across 1999-2024 with no weighting for recency, despite the same file's fitModel() explicitly fitting a season-to-season carryover decay because team strength drifts -- i.e. the resampler ignores the non-stationarity the point-forecast half of the same module already takes seriously.
candidates.mechanism: Barber et al. 2023: weight calibration/resample scores by rho^(age in games) instead of uniformly, recovering the exchangeable case exactly at rho=1 and giving a provable, graceful-degradation coverage guarantee under drift instead of an unweighted resample with none.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: In bootstrapProb(), change `residuals[(next() * residuals.length) | 0]` (uniform pick) to a weighted pick using precomputed cumulative weights rho^(n-1-i) over the residuals array sorted by game recency; add an effective-sample-size guard (ESS = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2) so an over-aggressive rho doesn't collapse the resample pool, mirroring the check in the marcopeix/conformal-ts reference implementation.
candidates.expected_value: Cheap, surgical fix to code that already exists and already has the right instinct; makes the resample coherent with the point-forecast model's own drift assumption instead of contradicting it.
candidates.exit_test: Compare walk-forward coverage/width before and after on the most recent 2-3 seasons specifically (where drift from older pooled data matters most) -- weighted version should show equal-or-better coverage with equal-or-narrower width than the current uniform bootstrap on recent seasons, with no regression on older, more stable seasons.

candidates.candidate: Stand up NexCP as the standing calibration layer for the nested walk-forward evaluation in nfl-market.js's evalSeasons loop (and any future weekly re-fit), rather than the current one-shot pooled-residual fit.
candidates.mechanism: Barber et al. 2023's weighted-quantile method gives a coverage guarantee that degrades gracefully (bounded by total-variation distance between consecutive seasons/weeks) instead of silently failing when the exchangeability assumption every current method in the file relies on is violated by real within/across-season drift.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Extend the per-season loop already in nfl-market.js's nested-CV evaluation function (the one computing marginStd per training window at line ~412) to carry forward a rolling, exponentially-weighted residual pool across seasons instead of refitting marginStd fresh each season from scratch or pooling everything equally; expose the chosen rho and resulting effective sample size in fitWindow's returned diagnostics object (which already documents alpha/carryover choices) so the calibration choice is as visible as the point-forecast hyperparameter choice already is.
candidates.expected_value: First place in the codebase where forecast UNCERTAINTY (not just the point forecast) gets a walk-forward-validated, drift-aware treatment -- directly generalizable later to the ensemble and to totals.
candidates.exit_test: On a held-out recent season, NexCP-calibrated coverage must be closer to the 90% target than the current pooled-residual approach's coverage, with the gap explainable by the measured effective sample size (small ESS -> honest warning, not silent undercoverage).

candidates.candidate: Conformalize player-prop point estimates (Mondrian/group-conditional conformal, grouped by position and prop type) instead of leaving them as bare point projections.
candidates.mechanism: Split conformal prediction (Angelopoulos & Bates Sec. on group-balanced/Mondrian conformal) computes conformity scores within each group separately, giving each group (e.g. RB rushing yards vs WR receptions) its own calibrated interval instead of one marginal guarantee averaged across all props -- appropriate because prop error distributions plainly differ by position/stat.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Grep-confirmed target: `server/services/nfl-prop-player-weekly-heads.js` and whatever prop point-estimate module feeds it (props are named in tonight's audit as the project's one area of genuine measured skill, 2+ TD Brier skill +27%, currently exposed only as point estimates). Add a per-(position, prop-type) conformal wrapper computing group-specific conformity-score quantiles from historical prop-vs-actual residuals, then emit low/high alongside each point projection.
candidates.expected_value: Turns the project's single strongest module into the first place with an honestly calibrated, per-group interval -- lets downstream consumers distinguish a confident prop call from a wide-uncertainty one, which a bare point estimate cannot do today.
candidates.exit_test: Per-group (not just overall) empirical coverage must hit target within the guaranteed band for at least the largest 3-4 position/prop-type groups by sample size; a group failing this needs either more data or coarser grouping before shipping.

candidates.candidate: Build one shared `conformal-calibration.js` module (split-conformal quantile, CQR interval, NexCP weighted quantile) as pure functions on residual arrays, for every module in the pipeline to converge on.
candidates.mechanism: All three algorithms (Angelopoulos & Bates Eq.1; Romano et al. Eq.9-11; Barber et al.'s weighted quantile) are each under ~30 lines of array arithmetic with no external dependency -- cheap enough to implement once, correctly, and reuse everywhere uncertainty needs quantifying.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New file server/services/conformal-calibration.js exporting splitConformalQuantile(residuals, alpha), cqrInterval(qLo, qHi, calibResiduals, alpha), and nexcpWeightedQuantile(scores, rho, alpha) with unit tests replicating the exact CQR Figure-2 (91.06%/1.99) and NexCP ELEC2 (89.3%/0.527) numbers on synthetic data as regression tests, verified against the papers read above. This directly also serves tonight's separate finding of 'five independent, disagreeing CLV implementations over four different tables with different math and sign conventions' by giving every module one tested, correct quantile/coverage primitive instead of five reinventions -- though unifying the CLV call sites themselves is a separate, larger migration not scoped here.
candidates.expected_value: Removes the temptation for every future module (props, ensemble, teasers, CLV) to hand-roll its own ad hoc uncertainty math, the same failure pattern that produced five disagreeing CLV implementations; one well-tested module is cheaper than five bespoke ones and is the natural target once F11-1/F11-2/F11-4/F11-5 exist.
candidates.exit_test: All three exported functions reproduce the published paper numbers (CQR 91.06% coverage / 1.99 width; NexCP 89.3% coverage / 0.527 width on the electricity replication) to within simulation noise before any production module is migrated to call them.

do_not_do: Do not wrap the drive-simulator's point forecasts (server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js) in a calibrated interval before its 6 known physics bugs are fixed (inverted kneel rule, wrong-team turnover field position, half-vs-full-game-clock mismatch, home-side win-prob using the home spread, flat 7-point HFA lump, no halftime/OT in the season-remainder sim). A calibrated interval around a biased simulator just produces a well-calibrated WRONG number -- coverage guarantees say nothing about bias, only about how honestly the spread of the (possibly biased) forecast is reported.

Do not apply plain (unweighted, exchangeability-assuming) split conformal across the full 1999-2024 pooled residual set in nfl-market.js and call it calibrated. fitModel() already fits a carryover decay parameter BECAUSE team strength is non-stationary; feeding that same non-stationary residual stream into an exchangeability-assuming method silently voids the coverage guarantee exactly as Barber et al. describe. Use NexCP (or block/re-fit by season) instead of naive pooling.

Do not conformalize the NFL ensemble's blended forecast (forecast ~= 0.68 + 0.632*market, the naive-shrinkage-to-market finding) and present the resulting interval as evidence the model is good. Calibration guarantees the ADVERTISED coverage rate, not that the point forecast carries information beyond the market -- a calibrated interval around a degenerate, market-shrunk forecast is still a degenerate forecast with an honest error bar bolted on.

Do not read 'well-calibrated' as 'profitable' or as new betting edge on its own. Per Nick's standing governance-gate rule, conformal intervals are a sizing/abstention INPUT (e.g. only bet when the interval excludes the market line), not a source of edge to market or chase in themselves.

Do not stand up a heavy ML stack (gradient-boosted quantile regressors, quantile neural nets) for the margin/total CQR fit. The relevant covariate set is tiny (|spread|, home/away, dome/outdoor, rest-day differential); a linear-in-covariates pinball-loss quantile regression is enough to capture CQR's adaptive-width benefit, and keeps the work in the hours/days tier -- Romano et al. themselves note overly complex quantile regressors are often MORE conservative (wider), not better.

Do not treat any conformal calibration set as permanent/fit-once. The coverage guarantee is conditional on the calibration data being exchangeable with the next point being predicted; a rule change, a new season, or a real roster shift is exactly the drift NexCP exists for -- recalibrate on a rolling/weighted window, mirroring the care nfl-market.js already takes with its own lastCompletedSeason/carryover boundary logic for point forecasts, rather than fitting a calibration set once and reusing it indefinitely.

result.label: F13-causal-news-impact
result.summary: Gridiron's own code admits the gap in three places verbatim: nfl-news-market-latency.js:81 returns authority:'latency measurement only; a reaction is not proof the claim caused the move', and the same disclaimer repeats in nfl-tweet-line-correlation.js:12 and signal-latency.js:22/186. All three pair a verified fact (nfl_verified_events/nfl_news_signals) with the nearest sportsbook quote (nfl_line_snapshots) and threshold the raw delta (|line_move|>=0.5, nfl-news-market-latency.js:49) with no market-wide baseline, no confounder control, and no placebo-calibrated false-positive rate — a co-occurrence test, not a causal estimate. Read in full: (1) Chernozhukov et al. 2018 DML (arXiv:1608.00060) — partially linear model, cross-fitting, Neyman-orthogonal score, its own simulation shows naive vs orthogonal estimator bias on identical data, 401(k) real-data example ~9,915 households, effect ≈$9,000 (SE≈$2,000); (2) Lopez & Bliss 2024 NFL bye-week paper (arXiv:2408.10867) — 5,679 games 2002-2023, Bayesian state-space + 2011 CBA natural experiment, on-field effect fell +2.21→+0.31 pts/game while the betting-market's priced valuation rose +0.39→+0.97 pts, proof a real vs. market-believed effect can diverge for a decade without a causal check catching it; (3) Angelini & De Angelis 2026 prediction-markets paper (arXiv:2606.07811) — Kalshi NBA one-minute quotes vs a play-by-play benchmark probability, finds only 0.64-for-one contemporaneous adjustment (36% underreaction) concentrated in thin markets, predicting further drift — the completeness-of-adjustment template Gridiron's 12.4M-row unused Polymarket tape (polymarket_quotes) could run; (4) MacKinlay 1997 event-study methodology, read via Ødegaard's full lecture-note distillation — market-model baseline E[R]=α+βR_m, abnormal/cumulative-abnormal-return construction, and the event-clustering over-rejection failure mode that Gridiron's flat, un-baselined threshold is directly exposed to. Six candidates (3 fix, 3 new), each tied to a named file/table with cost/EV/exit test, plus a do-not-do list anchored on never letting an unvalidated causal estimate touch staking.

sources.title: Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Treatment and Structural Parameters
sources.authors: Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Demirer, Duflo, Hansen, Newey, Robins
sources.sample: Simulation: n=500, p=20, g0 smooth in few variables, nuisance fit by random forest. Real-data example: ~9,915 households, 401(k) eligibility on net financial assets.
sources.key_result: Naive plug-in ML estimator is badly biased/non-normal (Fig 1 left); the orthogonalized, cross-fit DML estimator on identical data concentrates on the true value and matches N(0,Sigma) (Fig 1 right). 401(k) example: effect ~$9,000, SE~$2,000. Requires nuisance-estimator convergence faster than n^-1/4.

sources.title: Bye-Bye, Bye Advantage: Estimating the competitive impact of rest differential in the National Football League
sources.venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
sources.sample: 5,679 NFL regular-season games, 2002-2023, point differential and closing point spread
sources.key_result: Bayesian state-space model exploiting 2011 CBA bye-week practice-time rule change as a natural experiment: on-field bye advantage fell from +2.21 pts/game pre-2011 (95% CrI 0.61-3.80) to +0.31 (CrI -1.01 to 1.64, ns), while the betting market's priced valuation of the same bye advantage rose from +0.39 (CrI 0.00-0.78) to +0.97 pts (CrI 0.65-1.28) over the same period -- market belief and ground truth diverged for over a decade.

sources.title: When Do Markets Fully Process Public Information? Evidence from Real-Time Prediction Markets
sources.sample: One-minute Kalshi NBA winner-contract quotes (bid/ask, volume, open interest) merged with second-by-second NBA play-by-play across many games
sources.key_result: A one-minute change in an out-of-sample benchmark win probability produces only a 0.64-for-one contemporaneous change in the traded price (~36% underreaction); the shortfall predicts further price drift over subsequent minutes. Underreaction is concentrated in thin/illiquid markets even for salient signals; predictable drift is smaller than the bid-ask spread net of trading costs, so not a simple arbitrage.

sources.title: Event Studies in Economics and Finance (survey), read via Ødegaard's 'Empirical Methods in Corporate Finance: Event Studies' lecture notes
sources.authors: A. Craig MacKinlay (1997 survey); distilled by Bernt Arne Ødegaard
sources.venue: Journal of Economic Literature 35:13-39 (1997); teaching notes
sources.sample: Methodology survey/teaching notes, no single dataset -- covers the general market-model event-study framework applied across the corporate-finance literature
sources.key_result: Establishes the market-model baseline E[R_it]=alpha_i+beta_i*R_mt (expected outcome as a function of the market's concurrent move, not a flat threshold), abnormal/cumulative-abnormal-return construction, and documents that naive cross-sectional aggregation over-rejects under event clustering -- the exact failure mode Gridiron's flat, no-baseline 0.5pt/5-cent threshold is exposed to when many injury designations land on the same practice-report day.

sources.title: Event Study Testing with Cross-Sectional Correlation of Abnormal Returns
sources.sample: Not accessed in full (SSRN/RFS paywalled, 403 on fetch)
sources.key_result: Proposes a modified BMP cross-sectional test statistic that corrects for cross-correlation of abnormal returns under event-date clustering; cited as the formal fix for the over-rejection problem MacKinlay's survey flags, and as the pointer for N1's exit-test design, not counted toward the 4 full reads.

candidates.candidate: Replace the raw-threshold 'reacted' boolean with a market-model abnormal move (event-study CAR) in nfl-news-market-latency.js
candidates.fixes_finding: authority:'latency measurement only; a reaction is not proof the claim caused the move' (nfl-news-market-latency.js:81) and the flat no-baseline threshold reacted=|line_move|>=0.5 or |price_move|>=5 (nfl-news-market-latency.js:49)
candidates.mechanism: For every claim/event, build a MacKinlay market-model baseline from other games captured in the same window (median move of games not involving either team) and compute abnormal_move = observed_move - market_baseline_move, replacing the flat boolean threshold with a signed, sized estimate.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add marketBaseline(snapshots, captureWindow, excludeTeams) beside quoteReaction() in server/services/nfl-news-market-latency.js; subtract it before computing line_move/price_move; tighten the existing research_eligible gate to require N abnormal-move estimates with SE below a threshold instead of raw counts.
candidates.expected_value: Turns three modules' honest-but-useless 'it reacted y/n' output into a signed, sized estimate that can actually feed a forecast or staking decision.
candidates.exit_test: On games with no verified event for a team, the false-positive 'reacted' rate should match the placebo rate established by N1 -- fails today since the flat threshold's false-positive rate has never been measured.

candidates.candidate: DML-adjusted causal point estimate for a verified Out/Doubtful/IR designation's effect on the closing spread, feeding the ensemble's market-blend diagnosis
candidates.fixes_finding: nfl-ensemble.js's blend forecast ~= 0.68 + 0.632*market is naive shrinkage toward the close, not real forecast combination, with 20 components collapsing to ~3 independent signals and mean CLV -2.28 pts; nfl-online-neural.js:149-154 feeds verified-news features (home/away_verified_news_burden, coverage) into that same collapsing blend with no check on whether they carry residual causal signal beyond what the market has already priced.
candidates.mechanism: Fit Chernozhukov et al.'s partially linear DML model: Y=closing-spread move after available_at, D=verified-event treatment indicator/probability, X=day-of-week, time-to-kickoff, primetime flag, nfl-team-strength.js gap, polymarket_quotes liquidity/volume. Cross-fit nuisance functions with boosted trees/lasso; report theta-hat with SE.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New module server/services/nfl-news-causal-effect.js reading nfl_verified_events + nfl_line_snapshots + nfl-team-strength.js; feed output into nfl-ensemble.js's existing candidate_shrink_only diagnostic mode (nfl-ensemble.js:1311), which was already built to consume exactly this kind of external component-reliability check.
candidates.expected_value: If theta-hat is near zero and tight, it explains why the blend collapses to shrinkage (the news features are redundant with market); if nonzero and the market undershoots it, it is the model's first sized, causally-defensible edge candidate since the current -2.28 CLV history.
candidates.exit_test: theta-hat's sign/magnitude must replicate on an independent split of the season's verified events (e.g. first half vs second half); failure to replicate means shelve it, do not wire into staking.

candidates.candidate: Use the causal event-anchored abnormal move (F1/F2) as the single reference definition to reconcile the five disagreeing CLV implementations
candidates.fixes_finding: Five independent, disagreeing CLV implementations over four different tables with different math and sign conventions -- confirmed present: nfl-clv.js (321 lines), nfl-execution-clv.js (354), forward-ledger.js (335, own CLV math), nfl-quote-tape.js (234), plus CLV logic embedded in nfl-execution-edge.js and the betting-hub.js/nfl-market.js routes.
candidates.mechanism: Define one canonical convention: causal CLV for a fact = the abnormal_move (F1) from available_at until it returns to the placebo noise floor (N1), signed consistently. Publish as a spec and add one fixture test asserting each of the five existing implementations, converted to this convention on a shared fixture, lands within a documented tolerance -- surfacing disagreements as failing assertions rather than five silent numbers.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New test/clv-convention-reconciliation.test.js plus docs/reference/clv-convention.md naming the canonical formula and where each of the five files diverges.
candidates.expected_value: Stops 'what was our edge on this bet' from having five silently different answers -- a precondition for trusting any number F1/F2 would produce.
candidates.exit_test: Run the fixture test; count how many of the five implementations pass within tolerance today (expected: most fail -- the point is to make the disagreement visible and countable, not to average over it).

candidates.candidate: Placebo/permutation null distribution for 'did the market react,' replacing the fixed 0.5pt/5-cent threshold with an empirically-calibrated false-positive rate
candidates.mechanism: Run the same quoteReaction/abnormal-move pipeline against quiet windows with no verified event (bye weeks, or randomly-shifted fake available_at timestamps) to build the honest null distribution of 'reacted' rates and abnormal-move sizes under no real news; compare the real verified-event rate against it via a permutation p-value instead of a fixed threshold.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/nfl-news-causal-placebo.js built directly on nfl-news-market-latency.js's existing exported quoteReaction (line 29, already exported via __test) -- feed it placebo claims instead of real ones, don't reimplement the pairing logic.
candidates.expected_value: Converts 'reacted: true/false' from an arbitrary guess into a calibrated statistical claim -- the missing noise-floor ingredient F1, F2, and F3 all depend on.
candidates.exit_test: Estimated false-positive rate on placebo windows should sit near the chosen nominal significance level (e.g. 5-10%); if far higher, F1's abnormal-move construction needs a stronger market-baseline before anything downstream trusts it.

candidates.candidate: Heterogeneous treatment effects (causal forest / DML-based CATE) for how a verified-event effect varies by position, injury type, and team scheme-dependency
candidates.mechanism: Once F2's baseline DML estimator exists, swap its final stage for an honest causal forest to estimate a conditional average treatment effect surface -- e.g. whether a WR2 Out designation moves the total more for pass-heavy offenses, or a starting-LT Out moves a QB-sack prop more than the spread.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Extends F2's DML module with a causal-forest final stage; attaches to the props module's projection distributions (exact file to be confirmed with the props research track) -- prioritized there because props is the area with tonight's confirmed genuine measured skill (2+ TD Brier skill +27%).
candidates.expected_value: Could give Gridiron its first stratified, standard-error-bearing causal effect per fact-type rather than a single average -- but only pays off once verified-event volume accumulates across the season.
candidates.exit_test: Does not proceed until F2's own exit test (season-half replication) passes; stratifying a noisy unvalidated average effect just multiplies the noise into confident-looking nonsense.

candidates.candidate: Cross-market triangulation: use the 12.4M-row Polymarket quote tape and the sportsbook line-snapshot tape as two independent assets reacting to the same verified-event treatment
candidates.mechanism: Run the F1 abnormal-move pipeline twice -- once against nfl_line_snapshots (sportsbook), once against polymarket_quotes/polymarket_price_history (exchange) -- for the same verified-event treatments. Agreement in sign/magnitude across markets strengthens the causal claim; lead-lag timing shows which market discovers a given news class first, using the same benchmark-vs-actual completeness measure Angelini & De Angelis build for Kalshi/NBA.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/nfl-cross-market-causal.js, parameterizing F1's quoteReaction-style pairing over either table; polymarket-lines.js currently only builds the isotonic spread/total ladder (lines 1-55) and reads nothing else from the 12.4M-row polymarket_quotes tape.
candidates.expected_value: Turns Gridiron's largest, most neglected table into the independent second measurement that makes every other causal claim in this research more credible, for less cost than F2 or N2 individually.
candidates.exit_test: On a sample of verified QB-Out events, do sportsbook and Polymarket abnormal-move estimates agree in sign meaningfully above chance? Routine disagreement means F1's construction still has an unresolved confounding problem.

do_not_do: Do not wire F1/F2/N1/N2/N3 output directly into staking or bet sizing this week -- every candidate produces a diagnostic estimate, none validated out-of-sample yet, and the model's -2.28 CLV / 78% adverse-move history is exactly the track record that should require a clean replication (at minimum F2's exit test) before any causal estimate touches a real dollar.

Do not build the causal-forest/CATE layer (N2) before F2's flat-average DML estimate is validated -- stratifying a noisy or non-replicating average effect produces confident-looking numbers on strata too small to mean anything, worse than the current honest disclaimers.

Do not treat a single significant abnormal-move estimate from F1 as evidence of a real reaction before N1's placebo calibration exists -- this is the exact over-rejection risk MacKinlay's survey and the Kolari & Pynnonen cross-sectional-correlation literature warn about for clustered event data (multiple injury designations landing the same practice-report day across many games).

Do not rewrite all five existing CLV implementations (F3) as a single refactor tonight -- reconcile the definition first via a spec and failing fixture test; a blind mass refactor risks breaking whichever implementation is currently load-bearing during a live Week 1 capture.

Do not present any DML or event-study point estimate without its standard error or credible interval -- a bare point estimate is actively misleading per Chernozhukov et al.'s own motivation, and Lopez & Bliss's headline numbers are never reported without a credible interval either.

Do not assume Polymarket NFL liquidity matches the Kalshi NBA liquidity in the Angelini & De Angelis study -- that paper's central finding is that thinner markets underreact more, so early Polymarket-vs-sportsbook disagreement in N3 should be read as the expected liquidity effect first, not as evidence the causal design itself is broken.

result.label: F10-copula-correlation
result.summary: Read Sklar/Joe/Czado-level copula theory (Haugh's IEOR notes; Aas-Czado-Frigessi-Bakken's foundational vine-copula paper) plus a sports-specific copula application (van der Wurp et al.'s football goals paper, GJRM) and a practitioner SGP explainer, then grepped fantasy-football-dashboard read-only to find that the assigned defect's literal wording is half-wrong and half-real: teaser legs in teaser-leg-rates.js structurally NEVER share a game (same_game_pairs: 0, proven in code) and the module's own audit already found the cross-game same-week correlation is a week-size composition artifact (~0 after correction), not true dependence — so a naive "correlation bonus" there would repeat a documented past mistake. What IS real: nfl-prop-correlation.js already runs a genuine Gaussian copula (Cholesky/correlatedNormals in stats-util.js) for player-prop SGP pricing, but (a) it has zero coverage for team-leg (spread/total) x player-prop pairs — the actual "legs sharing a game with no dependence model" case — (b) it forces every pair through one symmetric, zero-tail-dependence Gaussian family despite Aas et al.'s own result that a single global copula can understate tail dependence by 29x, and (c) it fits one static correlation number per archetype forever, never conditioned on game script. Also found pyvinecopulib (MIT, 126 stars, actively maintained, real Vinecop.from_data/simulate API) as the working vine-copula library, and confirmed via GitHub code search that several 0-1-star hobby repos independently reinvent the exact same Gaussian-copula SGP construction Gridiron already has in production — useful negative evidence that Gridiron's existing approach is already at parity with the hobbyist state of the art, and the real uplift is moving past Gaussian.

sources.title: An Introduction to Copulas (IEOR E4602 Quantitative Risk Management lecture notes)
sources.key_result: States/proves Sklar's theorem and the Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds; defines the Gaussian, Student-t and Archimedean (Gumbel/Clayton) copula families and their simulation algorithms (Cholesky-based, matching what Gridiron's stats-util.js already implements); shows a bivariate normal and a meta-Gumbel distribution sharing identical linear correlation (rho=0.70) produce visibly different tail co-movement (Fig. 1), and documents named fallacies of Pearson correlation directly relevant to any single-number 'correlation bonus.'
sources.sample: Worked derivations of Sklar's theorem, Gaussian/t-copula simulation, Gumbel/Clayton density formulas, Spearman's rho and Kendall's tau, and a rho=0.5, n=60, t(3 d.f.) simulation comparing Pearson vs Kendall-tau-based correlation estimators.

sources.title: Pair-copula constructions of multiple dependence
sources.authors: Kjersti Aas, Claudia Czado, Arnoldo Frigessi, Henrik Bakken
sources.venue: Insurance: Mathematics and Economics 44(2) [SFB 386 Paper 487 working version]
sources.key_result: Introduces the D-vine/C-vine pair-copula decomposition (build an n-dim density as a cascade of bivariate copulas, each free to be a different family) and applies a 4-variable Student-t D-vine to international stock/bond return data: AIC -665.08 vs -632.18 for a single 4-D Student-t copula, LR test p=0.0007 rejecting the single-copula model, and the pair-copula model's tail-dependence coefficient for one margin is 29x higher (0.029 vs 0.001) than the single-copula fit's — i.e. one global correlation assumption can erase almost all real tail co-movement. Authors themselves flag goodness-of-fit testing for pair-copula models as still unsolved.
sources.sample: Full derivation of the pair-copula factorization (eq. 1-9), D-vine/canonical-vine figures for 5 variables, Table 1-5 with fitted degrees-of-freedom, AIC, likelihood-ratio test statistic, and tail-dependence coefficients for the S/M/T/B financial data set.

sources.title: Generalised Joint Regression for Count Data with a Focus on Modelling Football Matches
sources.authors: Hendrik van der Wurp, Andreas Groll, Thomas Kneib, Giampiero Marra, Rosalba Radice
sources.key_result: Copula-based joint regression (GJRM package; Frank/FGM/Gaussian/Joe/Clayton/Plackett/AMH/Gumbel families, copula parameter itself a function of covariates) fit to goals scored by both teams across 5 FIFA World Cups (2002-2018): best copulas show only weak dependence (Kendall's tau ~0.07-0.10) and improve predictive measures 'by a small margin or not at all' vs a plain independence/Skellam baseline, consistent with prior literature. A fictional Kelly-vs-constant-stake betting backtest on World Cup 2018 shows positive but small-sample, high-variance returns the authors themselves caution against over-reading.
sources.sample: Methodology section (bivariate copula joint regression, eq. 1-2), Table 4 copula-family rankings, and the Results/Betting subsection with the constant-stake vs Kelly return comparison and the South-Korea-vs-Germany extreme-odds caveat.

sources.title: Same-Game Parlays: The Mathematics of Correlation
sources.key_result: Walks the exact 3-step Gaussian-copula SGP construction Gridiron's nfl-prop-correlation.js already implements (probit transform -> correlated multivariate normal -> integrate) with a worked numeric example: three legs at 58.3%/52.4%/52.4% give independent joint 16.0% vs ~21.2% correlated (33% relative increase), explaining why a book prices that combo near +350 rather than the independence-implied +600. States sophisticated books use a hybrid copula + empirical-frequency approach when historical data for a combination is thin.
sources.sample: Full 3-step methodology description and the 58.3%/52.4%/52.4% -> 16.0% vs 21.2% worked example with the +350 vs +600 pricing implication.

candidates.candidate: Extend nfl-prop-correlation.js's existing Gaussian-copula machinery (propPairCorrelation / sgpAnalysis) to cover team-level legs (spread, total) paired with player props, not just player-prop-to-player-prop pairs

Grep confirms zero existing vine-copula code anywhere in the repo.

candidates.candidate: Make same-game correlation conditional on game script (spread magnitude, total, live win probability) instead of one static number per stat-pair archetype forever

candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-prop-correlation.js: add a spread_bucket/total_bucket dimension to prop_correlation_estimates (or a new table) and refit fitPropCorrelations() within buckets; propPairCorrelation() looks up by (stat pair, bucket) instead of one global value.

do_not_do: Do not add a "correlation bonus" to ticketProbabilities/familyPairCorrelation in teaser-leg-rates.js using the raw -0.044 same-week rho — the module's own bootstrap already showed this is a week-size composition artifact (CI includes zero; corrected rho ~ -0.0015). Doing so anyway repeats the exact 'factor of four' EV mistake the file's own header documents having made and retracted once already.

Do not describe teaser legs as 'sharing a game' when proposing fixes — the code proves the opposite (familyPairCorrelation reports same_game_pairs: 0, structurally guaranteed by the cross-both candidate-line construction). A 'same-game teaser copula' is not a real object; the real gaps are cross-game correlation within a week (already measured, ~0 after correction) and team-leg-to-player-prop same-game correlation (genuinely unmodeled).

Do not touch fantasy-football-dashboard — it is read-only for this research, a live server is capturing Week 1 games through Sunday, and every exit test above can be run offline or in a sidecar without write access to the live repo or database.

Do not adopt any of the 0-1-star hobby 'copula parlay' GitHub repos found (Rithvik09/NBA-Player-Props-Analyzer, shryesth/nba-betting-engine, imnotaCTO/chachingAI, JesunAhmadUshno/BigFish) as a dependency or reference implementation — unmaintained, license-unclear in places, and none exceed what nfl-prop-correlation.js already does in production.

Do not treat any fitted copula (play-by-play vine, tail-dependent family, context-conditional model) as tradeable without the same forward-CLV promotion gate sgpQuoteEvidence() already enforces (>=50 paired candidate/close quotes, positive mean CLV) — a better in-sample fit is not evidence of profitability against real prices, and both primary sources #2 and #3 show real AIC/likelihood improvements from copula modeling that say nothing directly about betting edge.

result.label: F15: Empirical Bayes / James-Stein shrinkage for team strength
result.summary: Read Efron-Morris/James-Stein foundations and 3 modern applications (all 4 sources fetched and read in full, with real sample sizes and out-of-sample numbers) and verified them against Gridiron's actual shrinkage code. Finding: shrinkage-fit.js's method-of-moments ANOVA estimator is methodologically sound (Brown 2008 ranks this class 2nd-best of six tested). nfl-preseason-blend.js's normal-normal Bayes update is algebraically correct (matches Efron's formula exactly) but belongs to the WORST-performing shrinkage class Brown found (EB-MLE/harmonic-prior) because it only pools a team toward its own prior season, never cross-sectionally across the other 31 teams the way the classical James-Stein theorem (N>=4 units, jointly-estimated grand mean) actually requires. The literal FOUND target, nfl-team-strength.js, turns out to be a feature aggregator, not the blend itself — the actual hand-tuned-by-feel blend (fixed weights 0.5/0.23/0.17/0.10/0.28/0.78/0.22/0.88/0.12, unfit decay exponents) lives in nfl-roster-strength.js's rankPlayer(). Also found (by grep, not a verbatim FOUND bullet) at least 6 more independently hand-rolled shrink-toward-prior formulas with hardcoded, unfit k constants scattered outside shrinkage-fit.js's fitted-k infrastructure — the same duplication pattern FOUND already confirmed for CLV, generalized to shrinkage. New-capability gap: Gridiron has no locally-fit, cross-sectional Bradley-Terry/Elo team-strength model with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (nfelo.js only imports a third party's pre-computed Elo); Ragain/Peysakhovich/Ugander (2018) show exactly this kind of shrinkage cuts NFL out-of-sample MSE 16.8% on real 2016 NFL data, with the gain concentrated precisely where the schedule graph is sparse (NFL's division structure) — a mechanism that maps directly onto Gridiron's own schedule.

sources.title: The Future of Indirect Evidence
sources.sample: Efron-Morris/Morris 1970 MLB data: N=18 players, 45 at-bats each
sources.key_result: James-Stein estimator's total squared prediction error over the rest of the 1970 season was less than one-third of the naive (direct) estimator's error; derives and states the exact normal-normal Bayes shrinkage factor B=A/(A+sigma0^2), which matches Gridiron's own nfl-preseason-blend.js formula algebraically; also documents the N>=4-units requirement (Stein 1956) and the caveat that JS conceals poor point-estimate performance on legitimate outliers (Clemente).

sources.title: In-season prediction of batting averages: a field test of empirical Bayes and Bayes methodologies
sources.sample: 2005 MLB season, all players with >=11 first-half at-bats: P=567 estimation / 499 validation players
sources.key_result: Total-squared-error ratio to naive predictor (naive=1.0): Group mean 0.852, EB-MLE 0.902, harmonic-prior Bayes 0.884, method-of-moments EB 0.593, James-Stein 0.525, nonparametric EB 0.508 (best). The MLE-plug-in normal-normal class (the family nfl-preseason-blend.js's single-team update belongs to) was the worst-performing shrinkage method tested, barely beating a crude group mean.

sources.title: Improving pairwise comparison models using Empirical Bayes shrinkage
sources.authors: Stephen Ragain, Alexander Peysakhovich, Johan Ugander
sources.sample: NFL2016: N=256 games, n=32 teams (16 games/team); NBA2016 comparison: N=1260 games, n=30 teams (82 games/team)
sources.key_result: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of a Bradley-Terry-style team-strength model cut held-out win% MSE on real NFL 2016 data from .0591 (MLE) to .0491 (parametric block-bootstrap shrinkage), a 16.8% reduction (11.1%-15.5% for Fisher-information variants); individual-matchup MSE improved 5.4%-9.2%. Gains were far larger than the identically-built NBA test (5-9%) because the NFL's sparse, division-structured schedule graph is exactly the regime where shrinkage helps most; the non-parametric bootstrap variance estimator specifically failed on the NFL data because many team-pairs shared only one game ever played.

sources.title: Data Analysis Using Stein's Estimator and its Generalizations / Stein's Paradox in Statistics
sources.sample: N=18 MLB players, 45 at-bats each, 1970 season
sources.key_result: Foundational James-Stein/empirical-Bayes result for sports rate estimation; not independently fetched as a standalone document (paywalled off arXiv), but its full derivation, complete 18-row data table, and >3x total-squared-error improvement are reproduced verbatim and in full mathematical detail by the same author in source #1 above, which was read in full.

candidates.candidate: Fit nfl-roster-strength.js's hand-picked composite weights (0.5/0.23/0.17/0.10 evidence blend, 0.28 rookie slot, 0.78/0.22 roster score, 0.88/0.12 traded-veteran shrink, 0.84^n/0.82^n recency decay) via the same method-of-moments variance-decomposition machinery shrinkage-fit.js already built and validated for the fantasy side, instead of leaving all eight constants chosen by feel.
candidates.fixes_finding: Team-strength ratings (nfl-team-strength.js) mix stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update — code reading shows the literal hand-tuned blend actually lives in nfl-roster-strength.js's rankPlayer(), which nfl-team-strength.js aggregates without ever re-fitting.
candidates.mechanism: Reuse fitK()'s one-way random-effects ANOVA (Searle 1992 method of moments) treating each evidence component (depth prior, participation, performance, PFF grade) as a group-level observation of true player rating, estimating sigma2_within/sigma2_between per component the same way shrinkage-fit.js already does per (metric, position) for fantasy shares/rates.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a fitRosterStrengthWeights(through) function alongside buildFitSpecs in shrinkage-fit.js (or a sibling file), producing a versioned weight vector the same way saveFit/activateFit/activeKVector already do; wire teamRosterStrength() to read it via an override argument, falling back to today's hardcoded weights until a fit clears backtest.
candidates.expected_value: Brown (2008) shows method-of-moments EB beats a naive/hand-fixed blend by roughly 40% in total squared error (0.593 vs ~1.0) in an analogous setting; even a partial fraction of that gain on roster-strength ratings would meaningfully sharpen the offense/defense/special-teams scores several fantasy and betting surfaces read.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest fitted weights vs current hardcoded weights on held-out weeks using the existing weekly projection CRPS/MAE harness (fit-shrinkage-weekly.mjs's own comparison pattern); ship only if fitted weights beat hardcoded on >=2 of 3 held-out seasons, exactly the bar teamStrengthWalkForward already sets elsewhere in the codebase.

candidates.candidate: Extend nfl-preseason-blend.js's blendedTeamRating() to ALSO shrink each team's in-season mean toward the CURRENT-SEASON cross-sectional league mean (estimated jointly across all 32 teams, à la classical James-Stein), not just toward the team's own single prior season — turning a correct-but-partial single-unit Bayes update into the full multi-unit empirical-Bayes estimator the literature actually recommends.
candidates.fixes_finding: Team-strength ratings... mix stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update — nfl-preseason-blend.js IS principled (verified algebraically against Efron's own formula) but is incomplete: it only ever pools a team's own two seasons, foregoing the cross-sectional pooling across the other 31 teams that both Efron-Morris and Brown (2008) identify as the actual source of the James-Stein gain, and Brown found this single-unit normal-normal (EB-MLE/harmonic) class to be the WORST of six tested shrinkage methods (TSE ratio .88-.90 vs James-Stein's .525).
candidates.mechanism: Two-stage empirical Bayes: stage 1 (already built) shrinks a team's own in-season games toward its own prior season; stage 2 (new) additionally shrinks the stage-1 posterior toward the current-season league-wide mean margin, with the pooling weight set by the SAME sigma2/(sigma2+n*tau2) form but with tau2 now the CROSS-SECTIONAL variance of the 32 teams' stage-1 posteriors, estimated via calibratePreseasonBlend-style method of moments across the current season's teams rather than only across a team's own two seasons.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a second calibration function (calibrateCrossSectionalBlend) alongside calibratePreseasonBlend in nfl-preseason-blend.js, and a stage-2 shrink call inside blendedTeamRating gated behind an explicit opt-in flag so the existing (already-tested-null) single-stage feature is not silently changed underneath teamStrengthGbmFeatures.
candidates.expected_value: The file's own honest prior test (WALK_FORWARD_VERDICT) found the single-stage version non-significant (90% CI [-0.017, 0.056], includes zero); this candidate is a real methodological upgrade (not a re-run of the same feature) so it merits one clean re-test rather than assuming the null result stands for a materially different estimator.
candidates.exit_test: Re-run teamStrengthWalkForward({ challengerFeatures: preseasonBlendGbmFeatures() }) with the two-stage estimator swapped in; only wire it into the live challenger dataset if it clears the file's own existing gate (>=2 of 3 walk-forward seasons significant, pooled bootstrap CI excludes zero) — otherwise record the negative result exactly as the current null was recorded, don't silently drop the finding.

candidates.candidate: Consolidate the >=6 independently hand-rolled shrink-toward-prior formulas with hardcoded, unfit k constants (nfl-context-heads.js:39, nfl-opponent.js:31, nfl-expert-council.js:117 k=30, nfl-rookies.js:364 k=80, nfl-props-replay.js:127 k=4, draft-assist.js:995) onto stats-util.js's canonical shrink()/shrinkRate() and shrinkage-fit.js's fitted-k infrastructure.

candidates.candidate: Build a locally-fit Bradley-Terry/Elo-style team-strength rating with empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward a jointly-estimated league mean, variance estimated via Fisher information and a parametric (not non-parametric) bootstrap — ported from Ragain/Peysakhovich/Ugander (2018)'s method, cross-validated with the existing teamStrengthWalkForward harness as a new challenger feature.

candidates.candidate: Implement the classical positive-part James-Stein estimator (exact (k-3) degrees-of-freedom shrinkage factor with non-negativity truncation) as a second engine alongside shrinkage-fit.js's method-of-moments estimator, A/B'd against it on the same real player-week panel.
