Only mattymitch499-sketch/nfl-sgp-model has a sports/parlay example, and it targets exactly Gridiron's problem: pricing a joint probability for two legs from the same game instead of assuming independence. Its stats.rs supplies the exact, small, dependency-free functions to reimplement in JS — uniform_scores (rank/distributional-transform), empirical_joint (nonparametric empirical copula evaluated at market-devigged marginals), and bvn_upper (from-scratch bivariate-normal orthant probability, Genz/Drezner-Wesolowsky quadrature) — plus a difference-bootstrap transport-validation gate that matches the discipline teaser-leg-rates.js's own familyPairCorrelation() already practices (report rho=-0.044, CI includes zero, take no action). sdv-dev/Copulas (BSL-1.1, 652 stars) and vinecopulib/pyvinecopulib (MIT, 126 stars) are real, actively-maintained, correct libraries but are Python/C++ with no JS binding — right as an offline-fit-to-JSON escalation path if same-game correlation ever clears significance or Gridiron adds 3+-leg parlays, not as a runtime dependency today. DanielBok/copulae (MIT, 163 stars, stale since Feb 2025) adds only a goodness-of-fit exchangeability test worth borrowing conceptually. No repo had verifiable performance numbers against a real book beyond the nfl-sgp-model's own in-repo, unaudited figures.

repos.license: none (no LICENSE file — all rights reserved)
repos.what_it_does: Personal Rust research repo, not a library: pre-registered study of whether NFL same-game-parlay prices under-charge for the true joint probability of two same-game legs. crates/nfl-sgp/src/stats.rs implements loo_standardize (leave-one-out z-score per subject-season), uniform_scores (rank + seeded-jitter distributional transform), empirical_joint(u,v,marginalA,marginalB) (nonparametric empirical copula evaluated at market-devigged Over/Under corners), gaussian_rho/gaussian_joint/bvn_upper (dependency-free bivariate-normal orthant probability via adaptive Gauss-Legendre quadrature, Genz/Drezner-Wesolowsky), and cluster_bootstrap_joint_difference (train<=2017/test>=2018 difference-bootstrap transport validation gating which families may be scored at all). 162 tests, verified by reading the source, not the README.
repos.adoption_path: No license to port verbatim; reimplement uniform_scores, empirical_joint, and bvn_upper as three small dependency-free JS functions in server/betting/nfl/strategy/teaser-leg-rates.js, following this repo's exact Marginal{p,direction}.wins() sign convention (doc-commented at stats.rs:621-634) and gated by the same train/test difference-bootstrap transport check before any correction is ever applied.

repos.license: Business Source License 1.1 (converts to MIT after 4 years; free for internal/non-SaaS use)
repos.what_it_does: General-purpose Python copula library (SDV ecosystem), no sports/bet/parlay example anywhere in the repo (verified by grep). GaussianMultivariate (multivariate/gaussian.py) fits per-column marginals + a Pearson correlation matrix on normal scores for Monte-Carlo sampling. copulas/bivariate/{clayton,frank,gumbel}.py fit real Archimedean copulas via Kendall's-tau-to-theta inversion under a common Bivariate base with CopulaTypes dispatch — Clayton/Gumbel carry asymmetric tail dependence a Gaussian copula cannot represent. multivariate/vine.py is a pure-Python vine-copula implementation independent of vinecopulib's C++ engine.
repos.adoption_path: Offline Python fitting script (not a runtime dependency) that fits Archimedean theta/Gaussian rho on historical same-game leg pairs and dumps parameters to a JSON file teaser-leg-rates.js reads at startup — only worth doing once a same-game correlation signal clears the significance bar familyPairCorrelation() currently fails.

repos.what_it_does: pybind11 Python bindings over the C++ vinecopulib library, the reference vine-copula implementation in the academic literature. bicop_base.py's BicopBase supplies fit/select/from_data given only pdf+hfunc1+hfunc2; select() auto-picks among Gaussian/Student-t/Clayton/Gumbel/Frank/Joe/BB1/BB2/BB6/BB7/BB8 (with rotations) per edge by AIC/BIC and assembles a full R-vine/D-vine/C-vine. No sports/parlay example in examples/ (checked all 10 notebooks: bivariate, vine, discrete, PyTorch-backend, sklearn-estimator topics only).
repos.adoption_path: No JS binding and no WASM build; would need the same offline-Python-fit-to-JSON pattern as sdv-dev/Copulas but with higher setup cost (native C++ build). Only warranted if Gridiron adds 3+-leg same-game parlays needing a genuine vine — its current teaser product is a fixed two-leg 6-point teaser (TEASER_POINTS in teaser-leg-rates.js).

repos.what_it_does: Archimedean copulas (Clayton/Gumbel/Frank) parallel to sdv-dev's, plus an empirical/ module implementing the empirical copula distribution as a queryable fitted object, and a gof/exchangeability.py goodness-of-fit test for whether C(u,v)=C(v,u) — i.e. whether leg-order symmetry is even justified. No sports/parlay example in the repo.
repos.adoption_path: The gof.exchangeability test is a cheap, borrowable idea (check whether teaser-leg-rates.js's implicit symmetric leg treatment is statistically justified) but the library is stale (no 2026 commits) and otherwise redundant with sdv-dev/Copulas for Gridiron's needs.

candidates.candidate: Reimplement empirical_joint + uniform_scores (rank/distributional-transform empirical copula) as dependency-free JS functions in teaser-leg-rates.js
candidates.fixes_finding: Teaser-leg and same-game correlation is assumed independent (server/betting/nfl/strategy/teaser-leg-rates.js) with no copula/dependence model, despite legs sharing a game.
candidates.mechanism: Standardize each leg's subject via leave-one-out z-score (factors out the market-priced level, isolates within-game co-movement), rank-transform pooled residuals to uniform scores with seeded-jitter tie-breaking (correct for count stats like TDs with few distinct values), then read the joint as the fraction of historical paired observations landing in both of tonight's market-devigged Over/Under corners. This is a nonparametric empirical copula, not a correlation-transport assumption.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New functions uniformScores(values, seed) and empiricalJoint(u, v, marginalA, marginalB) in teaser-leg-rates.js, fed by the same historical spread/total leg data familyPairCorrelation() already reads; ticketProbabilities() calls empiricalJoint() instead of multiplying independent leg probabilities whenever both legs come from the same game.
candidates.expected_value: Only replaces the independence assumption where it is currently wrong (same-game legs); familyPairCorrelation()'s own measured same-week rho CI [-0.095,+0.008] includes zero, so on today's data this may change nothing — the value is having a correct mechanism ready and gated for when/if more same-game leg data clears significance, rather than a silent, unfixable independence assumption.
candidates.exit_test: Fit uniform_scores + empirical_joint on same-game leg pairs (not same-week — Gridiron's current data only supports the weaker same-week measurement); if the resulting joint deviates from the independence product by less than one bootstrap standard error, do not apply any correction and say so in a comment, exactly as familyPairCorrelation() already does for its own statistic.

candidates.candidate: Port bvn_upper (dependency-free bivariate-normal orthant probability via Genz/Drezner-Wesolowsky quadrature) as the Gaussian-copula fallback for thin cells
candidates.fixes_finding: Teaser-leg and same-game correlation is assumed independent (server/betting/nfl/strategy/teaser-leg-rates.js) with no copula/dependence model, despite legs sharing a game.
candidates.mechanism: Closed-form bivariate normal CDF (adaptive 6/12/20-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature with a separate near-unity asymptotic branch) computes P(both legs win) under a fitted Gaussian copula parameter rho, giving a smooth (non-count-limited) joint estimate when the empirical cell (GF06-1) has too few historical same-game observations to be a reliable frequency.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Port bvnUpper(h, k, rho) plus normCdf/normPpf (both already dependency-free, Acklam's algorithm) as a single ~150-line pure JS module; use gaussianRho() (Pearson correlation of normal-scored uniform ranks) as the rho input, computed from the same historical pairs as GF06-1.
candidates.expected_value: Low-cost, high-reliability building block (no npm dependency, exact closed-form math) that removes 'small sample' as an excuse not to have any dependence model at all; real EV depends entirely on whether same-game rho is ever measured as significantly nonzero.
candidates.exit_test: Cross-check bvnUpper output against the empirical_joint (GF06-1) on the same historical data at several marginal grid points; if the two disagree by more than bootstrap noise, treat that gap as evidence the dependence is non-elliptical (tail-asymmetric) rather than trusting the Gaussian number blindly.

candidates.candidate: Adopt sdv-dev/Copulas' Archimedean (Clayton/Gumbel) fitting as an offline escalation path for asymmetric tail dependence
candidates.fixes_finding: Teaser-leg and same-game correlation is assumed independent (server/betting/nfl/strategy/teaser-leg-rates.js) with no copula/dependence model, despite legs sharing a game.
candidates.mechanism: Clayton and Gumbel copulas fit via Kendall's-tau-to-theta inversion capture lower-tail or upper-tail dependence a symmetric Gaussian copula cannot — relevant if same-game unders/covers co-move more strongly specifically in blowout or shootout tails than a Gaussian model would predict.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Offline Python script using copulas.bivariate.{Clayton,Gumbel} to fit theta on historical same-game leg pairs, writing fitted parameters to a static JSON file that teaser-leg-rates.js reads at load time; no runtime Python dependency added to the Node codebase.
candidates.expected_value: Speculative until GF06-1/GF06-2 establish that same-game dependence is real and non-Gaussian in shape; premature to build before that evidence exists.
candidates.exit_test: Only build this if GF06-1's empirical joint and GF06-2's Gaussian joint disagree systematically in a way consistent with tail asymmetry (not just sampling noise) across multiple marginal grid points.

candidates.candidate: Track vinecopulib/pyvinecopulib as the reference full-vine solution for 3+-leg same-game parlays, reference-only for now
candidates.fixes_finding: Teaser-leg and same-game correlation is assumed independent (server/betting/nfl/strategy/teaser-leg-rates.js) with no copula/dependence model, despite legs sharing a game.
candidates.mechanism: Automatic per-edge bivariate-family selection (Gaussian/t/Clayton/Gumbel/Frank/Joe/BB1/BB2/BB6/BB7/BB8 + rotations, chosen by AIC/BIC) assembled into a full R-vine, the academically correct way to price a joint of more than two dependent legs.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Not applicable today: Gridiron's teaser product (TEASER_POINTS=6, two-team teasers per teaser-leg-rates.js) only ever prices two legs; a full vine is over-engineering for a pair. Revisit only if Gridiron adds 3+-leg same-game parlay pricing.
candidates.expected_value: None today given Gridiron's current two-leg teaser scope; real if the product scope changes to 3+-leg SGPs, where a hand-rolled pairwise approach (GF06-1/2/3) stops being sufficient.
candidates.exit_test: Re-evaluate only when/if Gridiron's product roadmap adds a 3+-leg same-game parlay feature; until then this stays reference-only.

candidates.candidate: Adopt the nfl-sgp-model's train/test difference-bootstrap transport-validation gate as a general pre-registration pattern beyond teaser correlation
candidates.mechanism: Fit any historically-estimated parameter on an early season split, evaluate on a later split, and bootstrap the DIFFERENCE between the two halves' estimates (not just the test half's own CI) at a pre-registered grid of conditions; refuse to apply the parameter if the difference-CI excludes zero at more than a fixed fraction of grid points. The repo's own METHOD.md documents catching a false-positive failure mode from the naive version of this test (comparing a trained point estimate to a test-only interval, which ignores the training half's own sampling error).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Directly usable, beyond teaser correlation, on the nfl-ensemble.js blend weights, nfl-team-strength.js's preseason/in-season blend factor, and the 21-model historical search flagged tonight as lacking a trial registry — same train-early/test-late, bootstrap-the-difference, pre-registered-grid pattern each time.
candidates.expected_value: General-purpose discipline that would have caught (or at least flagged) several of tonight's findings earlier — the ensemble's shrinkage-toward-market blend and the team-strength hand-tuned blend are exactly the kind of historically-fit parameter this test is designed to validate honestly before trusting it.
candidates.exit_test: Pick one existing Gridiron historically-fit parameter (e.g. nfl-ensemble.js's 0.632 market weight), run the train<=2017/test>=2018 (or equivalent split) difference-bootstrap on it, and report whether it passes or fails at the same 20%-of-grid-points bar before applying this pattern anywhere else.

do_not_do: Do not add a Python or C++ runtime dependency (sdv-dev/Copulas, pyvinecopulib) directly into the Node/JS betting codebase — use offline-fit-to-JSON if these libraries are ever needed at all.
Do not copy code verbatim from mattymitch499-sketch/nfl-sgp-model — it has no LICENSE file (all rights reserved); reimplement the (uncopyrightable) math from its doc comments instead.

Do not apply any same-game correlation correction to teaser-leg-rates.js until a measurement clears a pre-registered significance bar — familyPairCorrelation()'s existing same-week rho CI [-0.095,+0.008] includes zero, and the correct response (already implemented) is to do nothing, not to force a correction in.
Do not build the full vinecopulib R-vine integration (GF06-4) before Gridiron's product actually needs 3+-leg same-game parlays — it is real over-engineering for today's two-leg teaser scope.

Do not treat the nfl-sgp-model repo's in-repo headline numbers (0.352 vs 0.250 joint, etc.) as an externally-audited benchmark — they are the repo's own unaudited output, not verified against a real book by this research pass.

result.label: GF05-backtesting-frameworks
result.summary: Cloned and read (source, not README) 5 backtesting frameworks — pmorissette/bt, mementum/backtrader, polakowo/vectorbt, martineastwood/penaltyblog, georgedouzas/sports-betting. Every one converges on the same shape: exactly one ledger/results object per backtest run, a structural (not conventional) no-lookahead split, and one canonical event-log schema that records rejected/no-edge attempts alongside filled ones. penaltyblog's Backtest+Account pair and implied.py's 7-method devig dispatcher, and georgedouzas/sports-betting's TimeSeriesSplit-gated backtest() plus its {provider}__{market}__{status}__{time} point-in-time odds grammar, are directly portable (MIT, small, active) and map onto named tonight's-defects: the 5 disagreeing CLV tables, the one-ad-hoc-devig gap, and the ad hoc team/game identity matching. backtrader (GPL-3.0, dormant 14mo) and vectorbt's numba core are borrow-idea/reference-only, not port targets. The overall fix is subtractive: replace 5-7 duplicate audit engines with one ledger, not build a 6th.
do_not_do: Do not take backtrader as a runtime/code dependency — GPL-3.0 and dormant 14 months; design-reference only.

Do not port vectorbt's numba-JIT simulation core (portfolio/nb.py, 7013 lines) — tightly coupled to its own dispatch/typing machinery, not worth a week+ extraction for Gridiron's much smaller scale (dozens of games/week vs thousands of assets/tick).

Do not build a 6th bespoke 'best of all five' audit engine — every framework read here converges on one canonical ledger object per run; the fix is deleting 4-6 of Gridiron's existing engines, not adding another.

candidates.candidate: Replace Gridiron's 5-7 duplicate audit/backtest engines with one penaltyblog-style Backtest+Account pair: a single date-indexed loop with a structural `lookback = df[df.date < date]` slice and one Account.history ledger table feeding one results() aggregator.
candidates.fixes_finding: Five independent, disagreeing CLV implementations exist over four different tables with different math and sign conventions.
candidates.mechanism: penaltyblog/backtest/backtest.py:78-130 iterates one calendar date at a time and slices lookback with a strict `<` comparison (line 115) so no logic function can ever see today's or a future row; penaltyblog/backtest/account.py's Account is the sole object allowed to place_bet() and append to self.history, and results() (backtest.py:132-162) is the only place ROI/win%/bankroll are computed. One ledger table cannot disagree with itself.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Write server/services/nfl-audit-ledger.js modeled on Account: one table `bet_ledger` (game_id, market, stake, odds, outcome, profit, date) populated by exactly one place_bet() function; delete the per-CLV-implementation tables and repoint every downstream consumer (dashboards, reports) at this one table's derived views.
candidates.expected_value: Eliminates the 5-way CLV sign/math disagreement outright by construction (one table, one function) rather than reconciling five after the fact; unblocks an honest trial registry (GF05-3) which needs one source of truth for what was tried.
candidates.exit_test: Run all 5 existing CLV implementations and the new ledger over the same 2025 season sample; if the new ledger's CLV matches at least one existing implementation's numbers to within rounding and the other four are provably wrong (sign or off-by-one bugs), retire the four; if the new ledger disagrees with all five, do not ship until traced to a specific bug.

candidates.candidate: Port penaltyblog's calculate_implied() devig dispatcher (7 methods: multiplicative, additive, power/Shin-family, shin, differential_margin_weighting, odds_ratio, logarithmic) into a single devig.py module and benchmark all 7 against Gridiron's actual closing-line outcomes.
candidates.fixes_finding: No real devig (de-vigorization) method comparison exists; probabilities are extracted with one ad hoc approach.
candidates.mechanism: penaltyblog/implied/implied.py (444 lines, read in full) dispatches all 7 methods behind one calculate_implied(odds, method=...) signature; power and shin methods are solved numerically via scipy.optimize.minimize rather than a closed-form approximation, and differential_margin_weighting/odds_ratio/logarithmic give three more independently-derived probability extractions to compare against.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add server/services/devig.js exposing the 7 methods (transliterated from the ~250 lines of real logic in implied.py, MIT-licensed); run it over the historical odds tape already ingested (per the diagnostic notes) and score each method's implied-probability calibration against realized outcomes before picking a default.
candidates.expected_value: Turns 'one ad hoc devig approach with unknown bias' into a measured choice among 7 named methods with calibration evidence; likely a small but real probability-accuracy gain feeding every downstream edge calculation.
candidates.exit_test: Compute Brier score / log-loss of each of the 7 devig methods' implied probabilities against realized game outcomes on held-out weeks; ship the current default only if it is not dominated by one of the other 6, otherwise switch.

candidates.candidate: Adopt georgedouzas/sports-betting's backtest() pattern: gate every walk-forward evaluation behind sklearn's TimeSeriesSplit (rejecting any other CV splitter), fit-then-bet per fold in one ~40-line function, and return one results schema keyed by (Training start, Training end, Testing start, Testing end).
candidates.fixes_finding: No trial registry exists with real preregistration + multiplicity correction (Holm/PBO/deflated-Sharpe) for the 21-model historical search that has already been run.
candidates.mechanism: src/sportsbet/evaluation/_model_selection.py:27-31 (_check_time_series_cv) structurally rejects any CV object that is not a TimeSeriesSplit, so a fold can never train on future data; backtest() (lines 84-170, read in full) parallelizes folds via joblib and returns one pd.DataFrame indexed by the four fold-boundary dates, giving a single canonical table of every trial's out-of-sample result to run a multiplicity correction over.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Wrap the 21 historical models' evaluation calls through one backtest(model, X, Y, O, cv=TimeSeriesSplit(n)) function; log every fold's result row into one `trial_results` table, then apply Holm or PBO correction over that table's full row count (all folds x all models), not just the ones that looked good.
candidates.expected_value: Makes an honest multiplicity correction possible for the first time by guaranteeing there is one row per actual trial run, structurally preventing after-the-fact cherry-picked comparisons.
candidates.exit_test: Re-run the 21-model historical search through the wrapped backtest() and confirm the resulting trial_results row count matches (models x folds) exactly; then apply Holm correction and check whether any previously-reported 'significant' edge survives at corrected alpha.

candidates.candidate: Adopt georgedouzas/sports-betting's odds column grammar `{provider}__{market}__{status}__{time}` (with STATUS_RANK ordering) as the schema for a unified odds/quote table spanning ESPN, nflverse, odds books, and the Polymarket tape, replacing ad hoc string matching in team-codes.js and nfl-contract-key.js.
candidates.fixes_finding: Game/team identity matching across sources (ESPN, nflverse, odds books, Polymarket) is done with ad hoc string matching in team-codes.js / nfl-contract-key.js, not real entity resolution; a 12.4-million-row Polymarket quote tape exists and is essentially unused for anything beyond spread-ladder construction.
candidates.mechanism: find_latest_odds_column() (src/sportsbet/evaluation/_base.py:44-69, read in full) resolves 'the latest odds quote as of a snapshot' deterministically from many candidate columns using a STATUS_RANK dict plus parse_event_time, rather than string-matching team names ad hoc each time; the same 4-token grammar generalizes to `{source}__{game_id}__{status}__{time}` for cross-source game identity resolution, not just odds.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Design one canonical long-format quote table with columns following this grammar (source, game_id or market, status, time) and a resolver function modeled on find_latest_odds_column(); use it to key the 12.4M-row Polymarket tape and existing odds-book data into one point-in-time-queryable table, replacing the string-matching layer in team-codes.js/nfl-contract-key.js.
candidates.expected_value: Directly unlocks the currently-unused Polymarket tape for anything beyond spread-ladder construction (e.g. as an independent CLV/edge cross-check) and removes a structural source of silent join failures across sources.
candidates.exit_test: Pick 50 known games and verify the resolver returns the correct game_id/quote for every one of the 4 sources without manual string-matching fallback; ship only if the false-match rate is measurably lower than the current team-codes.js approach on the same 50-game sample.

candidates.candidate: Borrow vectorbt's log-record pattern (every order attempt logged as filled/ignored/rejected with a reason code, not just accepted trades) to turn the fantasy weekly-learning loop's silent cold-start no-op into a visible, auditable status.
candidates.fixes_finding: The fantasy weekly-learning loop has never captured one forward snapshot in its life (cold-start: player_week_engine.heads is null week 1) — it needs a real cold-start/transfer strategy, not a silent no-op.
candidates.mechanism: vectorbt/portfolio/logs.py (confirmed via its own doctest, lines 24-40): every simulated order is written to a fixed-dtype log record with a `status` (Filled/Ignored/Rejected) and `status_info` reason code (e.g. NoCashLong), queryable via pf.logs.filled.count() / .rejected.count() off the same object — the framework logs what it tried and why it didn't happen, not only what succeeded.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add a `status` and `status_reason` column to the player_week_engine snapshot table; when heads is null (cold start), write a row with status='cold_start_skip' instead of writing nothing, so the gap is queryable and forces an explicit decision (backfill, transfer-learn from a prior season, or defer) rather than disappearing silently.
candidates.expected_value: Converts an invisible bug (a query that returns nothing looks identical to a query that correctly found nothing) into a visible, alertable condition at near-zero implementation cost.
candidates.exit_test: After the change, confirm week-1 of the next season produces an explicit cold_start_skip row in the snapshot table rather than a null/missing row, and that a simple COUNT query can distinguish 'skipped due to cold start' from 'ran and found nothing to log'.

candidates.candidate: Adopt the complementary_events-aware bet() constraint from georgedouzas/sports-betting (never place bets on more than one outcome within a mutually-exclusive group; pick only the highest-edge outcome per group) as a minimal, model-free first guard against Gridiron's uncorrelated teaser-leg/same-game assumption.
candidates.fixes_finding: Teaser-leg and same-game correlation is assumed independent (server/betting/nfl/strategy/teaser-leg-rates.js) with no copula/dependence model, despite legs sharing a game.
candidates.mechanism: BaseBettor.bet() (src/sportsbet/evaluation/_base.py:398-439, read in full) groups markets via derive_complementary_events() (e.g. home_win/draw/away_win must sum to 1) and for each group keeps only the single highest-estimated-return outcome, zeroing out the rest via a boolean mask — a structural guard against betting against yourself within one game, computed with no dependence model at all.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: In teaser-leg-rates.js, before combining legs from the same game into a parlay/teaser, apply the same complementary-events filter so mutually exclusive same-game legs are never both selected; this doesn't model correlation, it removes the worst-case failure mode (staking on both sides of one game) for free while a real copula model is scoped separately.
candidates.expected_value: Small, low-risk correctness fix that removes a specific class of self-defeating same-game combinations immediately, ahead of (not instead of) a real dependence model.
candidates.exit_test: Audit the last season's teaser/same-game-parlay selections for any case where two legs from the same complementary-outcome group (e.g. both a spread favorite and the same game's total-under that structurally conflict) were both selected; confirm the filter would have caught it and that it doesn't reject legitimate non-conflicting same-game combinations.

repos.what_it_does: Tree-of-Node backtesting engine (bt/core.py, 2247 lines) where Strategy and Security nodes lazily recompute value/weight/price only when a root 'stale' flag is set; a single Backtest class (bt/backtest.py:123) deep-copies its Strategy, takes a pluggable commission/cost model (flat callable or nonlinear CostModel/SqrtCostModel/AlmgrenChrissCostModel), and produces one Result object per run.
repos.adoption_path: Copy the 'one Backtest object, deep-copied strategy, one Result' structural pattern; the tree/Node hierarchy itself is overkill for Gridiron's flat game/market structure.

repos.what_it_does: Trade object (backtrader/trade.py:94) tracks a position's full lifecycle with pnl (gross) and pnlcomm (net of commission) as two always-separate fields, plus a TradeHistory audit trail (AutoOrderedDict) appended on every state transition; BackBroker (brokers/bbroker.py, 1237 lines) is the sole mutator of cash/margin/commission state, strategies never touch capital directly.
repos.adoption_path: GPL-3.0 and 14-month-dormant — do not take as a code/runtime dependency. Reference the gross/net-PnL-as-separate-named-fields and single-broker-as-sole-ledger-mutator design when building Gridiron's own ledger.

repos.license: Apache-2.0 with Commons Clause (non-commercial-resale restriction; internal use unaffected)
repos.what_it_does: Vectorized, numba-JIT'd portfolio simulator; every order attempt (filled, ignored, or rejected) is logged as one row in a fixed-dtype structured array (vectorbt/portfolio/logs.py) with a status and status_info reason code, queryable via pf.logs.filled/.ignored/.rejected.count(); built on a generic Records mapped-array abstraction reused across orders/trades/logs/drawdowns.
repos.adoption_path: Port the log-schema idea (one event table logging attempted, rejected, and filled bets with reason codes) directly; do not port the numba simulation core (portfolio/nb.py, 7013 lines) — too tightly coupled to vectorbt's own dispatch/typing machinery for the scale Gridiron operates at.

repos.what_it_does: Football-analytics package with a dedicated backtest module: Backtest(data, start_date, end_date) (penaltyblog/backtest/backtest.py, 163 lines) iterates one date at a time with a structural lookback = df[df.date < date] slice (line 115, strict less-than), an optional per-date trainer() refit hook, and a single Account object (account.py, 61 lines) as the only thing that can place_bet() and build the history/tracker ledger. Separately, implied/implied.py (444 lines) implements 7 independent devig methods behind one calculate_implied() dispatcher.
repos.adoption_path: Transliterate Backtest+Account (structural no-lookahead loop + one ledger) and calculate_implied() (7 named devig methods) directly into Gridiron's server/services/; both are small, dependency-light (pandas/numpy/scipy), and MIT-licensed.

repos.what_it_does: sklearn-native sports-betting evaluation package. BaseBettor (evaluation/_base.py, 550 lines) implements fit/predict_proba/bet() with a real odds-column grammar {provider}__{market}__{status}__{time} resolved via find_latest_odds_column() for deterministic point-in-time quote lookup, and a complementary_events guard preventing bets on more than one outcome within a mutually-exclusive group. backtest() (evaluation/_model_selection.py, 530 lines) is a ~40-line walk-forward harness that structurally requires sklearn's TimeSeriesSplit (rejects any other CV splitter), fits/bets per fold in parallel via joblib, and returns one results DataFrame keyed by fold boundary dates. BettorGridSearchCV reuses the same TimeSeriesSplit discipline for hyperparameter tuning.
repos.adoption_path: Direct pip dependency for the evaluation module is plausible, or transliterate _base.py + _model_selection.py (~1100 lines) into Gridiron's stack; the odds-column grammar generalizes to a cross-source game/quote identity scheme.

result.label: GF02-nfl-ratings-elo
result.summary: Cloned and read 5 real NFL rating/Elo/Bayesian systems (greerreNFL/nfelo, greerreNFL/nfelohfa, greerreNFL/nfelosrs, fivethirtyeight/nfl-elo-game, sublee/glicko2) to inform replacing nfl-team-strength.js's hand-tuned preseason blend. The standout find is greerreNFL/nfelosrs's BayesianRankings.py — a working, verified Gaussian-conjugate (precision-weighted) per-team, per-week Bayesian update over a WT-Ratings prior — exactly the "principled state-space/Bayesian update" the finding says is missing. nfelo's offseason_regression.py/prior_to_elo.py contribute the complementary piece: z-score normalization of each external prior against a trained per-season sigma before blending, which team-strength.js's raw feature differentials also lack. fivethirtyeight/nfl-elo-game (MIT) gives a portable, decades-validated simple-Elo baseline to backtest against. sublee/glicko2 (BSD-3-Clause) gives an off-the-shelf, correct per-team uncertainty estimate (phi/RD) team-strength.js currently has none of. nfelohfa additionally supplies a dynamic rolling-regression+EMA HFA model directly applicable to the separately-flagged flat-7-point HFA bug in nfl-drive-sim.js. None of the greerreNFL repos carry a LICENSE file (treat as all-rights-reserved, reimplement algorithms only); the 538 and glicko2 repos are MIT/BSD and portable directly.

repos.what_it_does: Production 538-style NFL Elo/market model. Verified in code: offseason_regression.py mean-reverts a team's Elo toward league median then blends in z-score-normalized external priors (DVOA, market win-total rating, preseason units rating) via prior_to_elo.py, which loads a per-season trained sigma from a JSON config and maps (value-mu)/sigma onto the Elo scale before a renormalized weighted average. elo_shift.py's calc_shift() implements a 'market resist' throttle: the in-season K-multiplier only increases when the model was more wrong than the market. Model/Nfelo.py's project_game() runs the full per-game pipeline: reversion -> dynamic per-game HFA -> QB adjustment -> playoff boost -> Elo-to-probability.
repos.adoption_path: Reimplement the two-part pattern (per-prior z-score normalization against a trained per-season sigma, then weighted blend with mean-reverted state) inside server/services/nfl-team-strength.js's teamStrength(season), replacing the current unweighted `?? leaguePrior` fallback.

repos.what_it_does: Per-game home-field-advantage model. BaseHFA.calc_hfa_sub() computes league HFA via a rolling regression over a trailing window with a kick-in gate, smoothed by an EMA. AdjustedHFA.py layers per-game adjustments (bye, timezone/travel, surface mismatch, divisional game) on top. Genuinely dynamic, not a flat constant.
repos.adoption_path: Structural pattern (rolling regression + EMA + per-game adjustments) to replace the flat 7-point post-OT HFA lump in server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js.

repos.what_it_does: WT Ratings converts sportsbook win-total futures into optimizer-fit preseason team strength. BayesianRankings.py implements a verified Gaussian-conjugate (precision-weighted) update per team per game: updated_mean = (prior_mean/prior_var + obs/obs_var) / (1/prior_var + 1/obs_var), updated_stdev = sqrt(1/(1/prior_var+1/obs_var)), run weekly with the prior stdev trained via scipy.stats.invgamma on historical margins/rankings. This is a real, working state-space Bayesian filter over team strength.
repos.adoption_path: Reimplement the Gaussian-conjugate weekly update in a new teamStrengthWeekly(season, week) inside nfl-team-strength.js, seeded from the existing preseason columns' cross-season variance, carrying a stdev output the file currently has none of.

repos.what_it_does: Canonical 538 NFL Elo, read in full (58-line forecast.py): HFA=65 Elo pts, K=20, season REVERT=1/3 with a hardcoded franchise-relocation exception table, and the well-known margin-of-victory multiplier that damps the update for an already-favored team winning by a lot (autocorrelation-adjusted elo_diff term in the multiplier denominator).
repos.adoption_path: Stand up server/services/nfl-baseline-elo.js as an independent, decades-validated baseline to backtest nfl-team-strength.js and nfl-ensemble.js against, scored with the existing backtest-significance.js harness.

repos.what_it_does: Faithful Glicko-2 implementation, read in full (172-line glicko2.py). Each team carries (mu, phi, sigma): rating, rating deviation, and volatility. rate() runs the full published 8-step algorithm including an Illinois-algorithm root-find for updated volatility. Verified against the published algorithm structure.
repos.adoption_path: Port to JS as nfl-glicko.js feeding the TEAM_STRENGTH_KEYS contract; use phi (rating deviation) as an off-the-shelf, correct per-team uncertainty estimate for the GBM's team-strength inputs.

candidates.candidate: Replace nfl-team-strength.js's raw feature differencing with z-score-normalized priors blended by trained per-season sigma (nfelo pattern)
candidates.fixes_finding: Team-strength ratings (nfl-team-strength.js) mix stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update.
candidates.mechanism: For each of the six TEAM_STRENGTH_KEYS columns, fit a per-season sigma (and a fixed mu) from the historical off_team_season/teamOffseasonSummary panel, mirroring nfelo's Priors/config/*.json + prior_to_elo.py. Z-score each raw column value, then combine z-scored columns via renormalized weights (summing to <=1, remainder defaulting to 0/league-neutral) exactly as offseason_regression.py combines external priors with mean-reverted Elo. This gives the blend an explicit, trained weighting scheme instead of unweighted raw differencing with an all-or-nothing leaguePrior() fallback.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-team-strength.js: teamStrength(season) and leaguePrior(season). Add a small trained-sigma table (new module, e.g. team-strength-priors.json) and a normalize-then-blend step before writing TEAM_STRENGTH_KEYS values; teamStrengthGbmFeatures() differencing logic is unaffected structurally.
candidates.expected_value: Turns an admittedly-arbitrary blend into a documented, backtestable normalization scheme; makes the 'shrink to league prior' behavior graded by evidence strength per column instead of on/off.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest teamStrengthGbmFeatures() output through the existing nfl-gbm.js challenger path pre/post change on held-out seasons via backtest-significance.js; ship only if MAE does not regress and the feature contract's CI in model-governance.js does not degrade.

candidates.candidate: Port the Gaussian-conjugate weekly Bayesian update from greerreNFL/nfelosrs's BayesianRankings.py into a new teamStrengthWeekly() in nfl-team-strength.js
candidates.fixes_finding: Team-strength ratings (nfl-team-strength.js) mix stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update.
candidates.mechanism: Seed each team's {mean, stdev} from the current preseason TEAM_STRENGTH_KEYS aggregate (using its historical cross-season variance as the prior stdev). After each game, update via the precision-weighted formula verified in BayesianRankings.py: updated_mean = (prior_mean/prior_var + obs/obs_var) / (1/prior_var + 1/obs_var); updated_stdev = sqrt(1/(1/prior_var + 1/obs_var)), where obs is the HFA/QB-adjusted actual margin and obs_var is a trained observation variance. This makes team-strength update in-season for the first time and gives it a genuine state-space form instead of a preseason-only static snapshot.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New export teamStrengthWeekly(season, week) in nfl-team-strength.js, called from wherever nfl-gbm.js currently re-reads teamStrength(season) per week; requires a new small distributions config analogous to nfelosrs's distributions.json, fit from Gridiron's own game-result history rather than copied from the repo.
candidates.expected_value: This is the single most direct fix for the named defect: it is a real, working, verified Bayesian filter, not a bespoke invention, and it is small (~40 lines of core math).
candidates.exit_test: Confirm posterior stdev shrinks monotonically as games accumulate within a season and resets appropriately at season boundaries; compare in-season predictive accuracy against the current preseason-only static feature on weeks 4+ of a held-out season.

candidates.candidate: Port sublee/glicko2's rate() update to JS as nfl-glicko.js and use its rating-deviation (phi) as the team-strength uncertainty output
candidates.fixes_finding: Team-strength ratings (nfl-team-strength.js) mix stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update.
candidates.mechanism: BSD-3-Clause licensed, verified in full: each team carries (mu, phi, sigma). phi (rating deviation) already IS a calibrated per-team uncertainty that shrinks with more games and widens with inactivity (bye weeks, off-season) via the built-in phi_star step -- exactly the state variable a hand-tuned point-estimate blend cannot produce.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/nfl-glicko.js (ported, MIT/BSD header retained) computing a Glicko-2 rating per team per week from game results; feed its mu as an alternative/ensemble input to TEAM_STRENGTH_KEYS and its phi as a genuine per-team confidence weight the GBM or ensemble can use to downweight noisy teams (few games, injuries).
candidates.expected_value: Cheapest correct source of per-team uncertainty in the whole pipeline; also partially serves the separately-flagged missing-calibrated-uncertainty finding without a bespoke calibration method.
candidates.exit_test: Verify ported rate() reproduces the reference implementation's output on a fixed synthetic series (unit test against sublee/glicko2's own glicko2tests.py cases) before wiring into any Gridiron feature.

candidates.candidate: Stand up fivethirtyeight/nfl-elo-game as an independent MIT-licensed baseline Elo to backtest team-strength/ensemble against
candidates.fixes_finding: Team-strength ratings (nfl-team-strength.js) mix stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update.
candidates.mechanism: A decades-validated, fully specified simple Elo (HFA=65, K=20, REVERT=1/3, log-margin multiplier with an autocorrelation-adjusted denominator that damps blowout over-reaction) gives a rigorous, well-understood reference point that the current ad hoc blend has never been checked against.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/nfl-baseline-elo.js, ported directly (MIT), fed the same game-result history already loaded for off_team_season; scored through backtest-significance.js alongside nfl-team-strength.js's contribution to the GBM.
candidates.expected_value: Cheap sanity check -- if the hand-tuned blend cannot beat a 58-line reference Elo on held-out seasons, that is itself a strong argument for replacing it with GF02-1/GF02-2.
candidates.exit_test: Run both models on the same held-out seasons; report MAE/Brier side by side. A replacement to team-strength.js should not ship unless it beats this baseline.

candidates.candidate: Adopt nfelohfa's rolling-regression+EMA dynamic HFA model to fix nfl-drive-sim.js's flat 7-point post-OT HFA lump
candidates.fixes_finding: home-field advantage is a flat 7-point post-OT lump distorting the key-number distribution
candidates.mechanism: BaseHFA.calc_hfa_sub() computes league HFA as a rolling regression over a trailing window (with a kick-in gate) smoothed by an EMA, tracking HFA's real decline over time instead of a fixed constant; AdjustedHFA.py adds per-game adjustments for bye weeks, timezone/travel, surface mismatch, and divisional matchups.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js: replace the flat 7-point HFA constant with a per-game HFA value computed by a ported rolling-regression+EMA function (reusing Gridiron's own game history, not the repo's fitted numbers) plus simple per-game adjustments Gridiron already has data for (bye weeks, divisional flag).
candidates.expected_value: Directly removes a named, specific bug (flat 7-pt lump distorting the key-number distribution) with a structurally proven alternative rather than an arbitrary smaller constant.
candidates.exit_test: Confirm the simulated margin distribution's mass at key numbers (3, 7) matches the empirical distribution of ATS/margin outcomes better than the flat-7 baseline, using the same evaluation the drive-sim's other 5 physics-bug fixes will be checked against.

do_not_do: Do not npm install, pip install, or execute any code from these cloned repos -- read-only extraction of the update-rule math only.

Do not copy code verbatim from greerreNFL/nfelo, greerreNFL/nfelohfa, or greerreNFL/nfelosrs -- none of the three carries a LICENSE file (treat as all-rights-reserved); reimplement the documented algorithm from scratch and cite repo/path/line as the source of the idea, not the text.
Do not touch fantasy-football-dashboard directly tonight -- it is read-only while a live server captures Week 1 games through Sunday; all candidates here are for a future edit session.

Do not feed any market-derived column back into a re-blended team-strength output -- nfl-team-strength.js's own header comment documents that implied_team_points/implied_points_delta was already tried and failed (0.995, CI 0.951-1.044); none of these candidates should reintroduce it.

Do not let the Bayesian/Glicko additions become a new source of look-ahead leakage -- any weekly update must only use data available before kickoff of the game being updated on, mirroring nfl-team-strength.js's existing no-look-ahead discipline.

result.label: GF03: devig/Kelly/EV GitHub libraries
result.summary: Cloned and read 4 real devig/Kelly repos. Baseline check first: nfl-devig.js already has Shin's method — but only for 2-outcome markets and with nothing to compare it against, and staking.js already has a documented Busseti/Ryu/Boyd simplification — but no closed-form check on its Monte Carlo drawdown estimate and no drawdown-aware Kelly multiplier. The real gaps: (1) neeljshah/shin-devig (MIT) is a small, zero-dep, line-by-line-verified library implementing 4 devig methods (multiplicative/additive/power/shin) with an N-outcome Shin solver — port it wholesale to give nfl-devig.js both a genuine method comparison and N-way market support (needed for Polymarket futures, currently 2-outcome-only per polymarket.js). (2) mberk/shin (MIT, 105 stars) is the community-standard Shin implementation with the same N-outcome fixed-point formula and published test vectors — use as the regression-test oracle for the port, don't port its Rust code. (3) cvxgrp/kelly_code (GPL-3.0) is Busseti/Ryu/Boyd's own paper repo, already cited in staking.js — confirmed the risk constraint's closed-form Chernoff bound Prob(W_min<alpha)<=alpha^lambda; GPL blocks porting code, but the formula (re-implemented independently) is a cheap analytic cross-check on slateRiskCheck's Monte Carlo drawdown_probability. (4) sergeisukhovmkt's Bayesian-Grossman-Zhou repo (MIT) bundles the well-established, peer-reviewed Grossman & Zhou (1993) linear drawdown-cushion Kelly rule (f=kappa*d/b) as one of its baselines — its own novel "Bayes GZ" contribution is a self-published, once-retracted-and-revised 2026 SSRN paper and should NOT be trusted, but the classical GZ93 baseline is real and directly fills staking.js's missing "drawdown-aware Kelly multiplier" (currently a flat 0.25 regardless of season bankroll drawdown).

repos.what_it_does: Zero-dependency pure-Python library implementing and comparing 4 devig methods (multiplicative, additive, power, shin) on N-outcome markets; verified every formula in src/shin_devig/methods.py by reading it line-by-line against Shin (1992) and Strumbelj (2014), and cross-checked its n=2 Shin==Additive identity against mberk/shin's independent test suite.
repos.adoption_path: Port multiplicative_devig/additive_devig/power_devig/shin_devig (generalized to N outcomes) into server/services/nfl-devig.js as sibling functions to the existing 2-outcome-only shinDevig; add a devigCompare() that runs all 4 and flags large disagreement (favorite-longshot-bias signal) the way the module docstring already frames it.

repos.what_it_does: Community-standard Shin's-method package (Rust core + Python bindings); n=2 closed-form solve, n>2 fixed-point iteration on the same closed-form relation, with published 3-way test vectors (odds [2.6,4.2*,4.3] etc.) matching other independent implementations.
repos.adoption_path: Do not port the Rust/PyO3 code. Use its published test vectors (3-way market -> [0.3730,0.4048,0.2222], z=0.01694) as the regression-test oracle for the N-outcome Shin port from neeljshah/shin-devig into nfl-devig.js's test suite (test/nfl-devig.test.js).

repos.what_it_does: Official companion notebooks for Busseti/Ryu/Boyd 'Risk-Constrained Kelly Gambling' (arXiv:1603.06183), already cited in staking.js's header comment; builds an old-API cvxpy convex program with a log_sum_exp risk constraint and empirically verifies the Chernoff bound Prob(W_min<alpha)<=alpha^lambda against 10,000 Monte Carlo trajectories.
repos.adoption_path: GPL-3.0 blocks direct porting. Re-implement (independently, from the public formula, not the GPL code) the closed-form bound alpha^lambda as a cheap analytic sanity-check inside staking.js's slateRiskCheck, cross-validating the existing 8000-trial Monte Carlo drawdown_probability estimate.

repos.what_it_does: Companion code for a self-published, unreviewed 2026 SSRN working paper. Its own novel 'Bayes GZ' formula is contested (an earlier version was retracted per its own README after an expert note found it didn't solve the stated HJB). But code/simulation.py correctly implements the well-established, peer-reviewed Grossman & Zhou (1993) linear drawdown-cushion Kelly rule f=kappa*(d/b) as one of its baselines.
repos.adoption_path: Borrow ONLY the classical Grossman-Zhou (1993) linear cushion rule (not the paper's own untested contribution) to make staking.js's stakeFor multiplier dynamic: shrink the 0.25 fractional-Kelly haircut as realized season bankroll approaches a chosen drawdown floor, instead of the current flat constant.

candidates.candidate: Port neeljshah/shin-devig's 4-method devig comparator (multiplicative/additive/power/shin) into nfl-devig.js, generalized to N outcomes
candidates.fixes_finding: No real devig method comparison exists; probabilities are extracted with one ad hoc approach (and the existing Shin solver in nfl-devig.js is hardcoded to 2-outcome markets only)
candidates.mechanism: Adds additive_devig and power_devig as independently-derived alternatives to Shin, plus generalizes the existing 2-outcome bisection into an N-outcome bisection on the same closed-form Shin relation (sum_i p_i(z)=1, monotonically decreasing in z so bisection is guaranteed to converge) -- verified by reading the source against Shin (1992) and cross-checked against mberk/shin's independent n>2 fixed-point formula, which derives the same relation a different way (fixed-point iteration vs bisection) and agrees on the published test vector.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/nfl-devig.js: add additiveDevig/powerDevig/shinDevigN alongside the existing proportionalDevig/shinDevig; wire nfl-market.js, nfl-props.js, nfl-clv.js, nfl-replay.js (current shinDevig/shinNoVig callers) to optionally report all 4 methods' spread as a favorite-longshot-bias diagnostic; extend to N outcomes so server/services/polymarket.js can devig genuine multi-way futures markets (division winner, Super Bowl winner) instead of being restricted to its current 2-outcome-only assumption.
candidates.expected_value: Turns a single unverified devig method into a checkable comparison (if power/additive/shin disagree by more than a few points on a given market, that's itself a signal worth surfacing) and unlocks N-way Polymarket futures devigging, which the 12.4M-row Polymarket tape currently can't use beyond spread-ladder construction.
candidates.exit_test: test/nfl-devig.test.js: for a 3-way market, all 4 methods sum to 1.0 within 1e-9; shin/power both raise the favorite's probability vs multiplicative baseline (favorite-longshot-bias direction); N-outcome shinDevig matches mberk/shin's published 3-way test vector ([0.3730,0.4048,0.2222] on odds [2.6,2.4,4.3]) to 1e-6.

candidates.candidate: Add a closed-form Chernoff drawdown bound (Prob(W_min<alpha) <= alpha^lambda) as a sanity check on staking.js's Monte Carlo drawdown_probability
candidates.fixes_finding: staking.js's slateRiskCheck computes drawdown_probability purely by Monte Carlo (8000 trials, no closed-form cross-check), and cvxgrp/kelly_code (the exact Busseti/Ryu/Boyd paper repo already cited in staking.js's own header) shows the paper's risk constraint has a cheap analytic companion bound that the codebase never implements
candidates.mechanism: The paper's log_sum_exp risk constraint is equivalent to a Chernoff/Markov bound: for a chosen risk-aversion lambda, Prob(min wealth < alpha) <= alpha^lambda. This is computable in closed form with no solver, and can be checked against the existing Monte Carlo estimate as an upper-bound sanity check.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/staking.js: in slateRiskCheck, alongside the existing Monte Carlo drawdownProbability, compute a closed-form upper bound using the fitted portfolio-level lambda implied by the correlation-adjusted stake sizing, and assert/flag if the Monte Carlo estimate exceeds it by more than sampling noise -- a correctness guard on the copula/correlation-matrix machinery, not a new staking decision.
candidates.expected_value: Catches silent bugs in the correlation matrix, cholesky decomposition, or copula draw (any of which could make the Monte Carlo drawdown estimate wrong) without adding a solver dependency or touching GPL code -- pure defensive verification on an already-cited paper's own math.
candidates.exit_test: test/slate-risk-staking.test.js: for several synthetic correlated slates, the Monte Carlo drawdown_probability never exceeds the closed-form alpha^lambda bound by more than 2x the trial-count-implied sampling error.

candidates.candidate: Make staking.js's fractional-Kelly multiplier drawdown-aware using the classical Grossman-Zhou (1993) linear cushion rule
candidates.fixes_finding: Betting model finding: 'execution edge + staking guardrail' is named as a real remaining gap -- staking.js's stakeFor uses a single static multiplier=0.25 regardless of how close realized season bankroll is to any drawdown floor
candidates.mechanism: Grossman & Zhou (1993, Mathematical Finance) show the growth-optimal leverage under a hard drawdown barrier is f=kappa*(d/b), where d is the log-distance from current wealth to the barrier and b=-ln(1-delta) for a barrier at delta fraction below the high-water mark -- leverage shrinks linearly and automatically as the bankroll approaches the floor, and returns to full (fractional) Kelly far from it. Verified as correctly implemented (as the 'oracle' baseline, distinct from the paper's own contested novel contribution) in sergeisukhovmkt's simulation.py.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: server/services/staking.js: in stakeFor, replace the static `multiplier=0.25` default with a computed multiplier = min(0.25, kappa_ratio * d/b) where d is derived from the season's running high-water mark on bankroll (already tracked wherever forward_ledger.js records settled results) and b=-ln(1-delta) for a Nick-chosen season drawdown tolerance delta (e.g. 20%); falls back to the current flat 0.25 when no drawdown history exists yet (cold start), so behavior is unchanged until there's a real high-water mark to measure distance from.
candidates.expected_value: Directly targets the named 'staking guardrail' gap with a 30-year-old, peer-reviewed, non-contested result rather than inventing a new rule -- shrinks stakes automatically during a bad stretch instead of waiting for a human to notice and manually cut sizing.
candidates.exit_test: New unit test in test/nfl-execution-staking-policy.test.js: multiplier equals ~0.25*full at the season high-water mark, strictly decreases as simulated bankroll drawdown deepens, and hits exactly 0 at the chosen drawdown barrier delta -- matching the closed-form d/b ratio to 1e-6 for several synthetic drawdown paths.

candidates.candidate: Use mberk/shin's published N-outcome test vectors as the permanent regression oracle for the ported N-outcome Shin solver
candidates.fixes_finding: No real devig method comparison exists (specifically: no independent verification that a ported/extended Shin implementation is numerically correct, since the current codebase only has its own single implementation to check itself against)
candidates.mechanism: mberk/shin (105 stars, MIT, actively maintained through 2025) is the most widely used Shin's-method package and ships published test vectors for a 3-way market (decimal odds [2.6, 2.4, 4.3] -> probabilities [0.3730, 0.4048, 0.2222], z=0.01694) derived via a fixed-point iteration that is mathematically equivalent to, but algorithmically different from, the bisection approach nfl-devig.js/neeljshah's port use -- so agreement between the two is a real independent-implementation cross-check, not just a self-consistency check.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: test/nfl-devig.test.js: add the mberk/shin 3-way vector as a hardcoded regression case for the new N-outcome shinDevig (from GF03-1), independent of whatever unit tests ship with the ported neeljshah/shin-devig code.
candidates.expected_value: Cheap, permanent protection against a future refactor silently breaking the N-outcome solver -- costs one test case, catches an entire class of numerical regression.
candidates.exit_test: The new test passes and stays in CI; deliberately breaking the N-outcome iteration (e.g. off-by-one in the (n-2) denominator) makes it fail.

do_not_do: Do not copy any code from cvxgrp/kelly_code (GPL-3.0) into the codebase -- re-implement the closed-form Chernoff bound independently from the public formula only.

Do not port sergeisukhovmkt's novel 'Bayes GZ' formula -- its own README documents that an earlier version of the paper's main result was retracted after an expert review found it did not solve the stated HJB; only the well-established Grossman-Zhou (1993) baseline it implements is trustworthy.

Do not treat neeljshah/shin-devig's community adoption as validation -- it is a single-commit, unstarred, brand-new repo; the reason to port it is that the code was read and independently verified line-by-line against the cited papers and against mberk/shin's test vectors, not because of stars or maturity.

Do not let the N-outcome devig extension change any existing 2-outcome caller's output -- nfl-market.js/nfl-clv.js/nfl-props.js/nfl-auto-picks.js/nfl-replay.js must keep getting byte-identical 2-outcome Shin results; the N-outcome path is additive, for genuinely N-way markets only (Polymarket futures), not a replacement.

result.label: GF09-nflverse-ecosystem-code
result.summary: Cloned and read nflverse/nflfastR (MIT, 541 stars, last commit 2026-08-13) and nflverse/nflreadr (MIT, 113 stars, last commit 2026-09-07). nflreadr is pure data-distribution code (no model logic) — it confirms Gridiron's nfl-pbp.js already consumes real xgboost-trained epa/wpa for historical plays via nflverse releases, so that path needs no fix. The actual EP/WP model-training code lives in nflfastR's data-raw/MODELS.R (xgboost multi:softprob EP, xgboost binary:logistic WP with monotone constraints) plus inference-time special-casing in R/helper_add_ep_wp.R (kneel hard-override, two-regime OT logic with a 2012 rule-era cutoff, separate PAT/2pt/kickoff branches, sign-flipped posteam_spread for away teams, HFA as a single learned binary feature never a flat additive constant). Gridiron has no equivalent state-aware WP scorer: nfl-live.js's liveWinProbability is a self-documented random-walk normal-CDF using only lead/clock/pregame-spread (explicitly no down/distance/possession/timeouts), and nfl-drive-sim.js's already-diagnosed physics bugs (inverted kneel rule, no OT, home-spread-for-away-team, flat 7-pt HFA lump, no timeout decrement) each have a direct, concretely-quotable correct reference in nflfastR's production code. All 5 candidates port that reference logic (not the trained binaries — irrelevant to Node.js) into the existing JS files.

repos.what_it_does: R package that scrapes/normalizes NFL play-by-play and computes real EP/WP/CP via pre-trained xgboost models (7-class multinomial EP, binary-logistic WP with monotone constraints, binary-logistic CP) plus a GAM field-goal model. Model-TRAINING code (feature lists, label construction, weighting) is in data-raw/MODELS.R; inference-time special-casing (kneels, OT regimes, PAT/2pt/kickoff branches, spread sign-flip) is in R/helper_add_ep_wp.R (2036 lines) and R/helper_add_nflscrapr_mutations.R (make_model_mutations, line 760).
repos.adoption_path: Port the exact feature lists (ep_model_select / wp_model_select at R/helper_add_ep_wp.R:151-218) and the inference-time special-casing (kneel override lines 397-408, OT branch lines 820-899, posteam_spread sign flip lines 250-254) into server/services/nfl-live.js and server/services/nfl-drive-sim.js as JS logic — not the trained xgboost binaries themselves, which are R/Python artifacts irrelevant to Node.

do_not_do: Do not try to load or call nflfastR's actual trained xgboost model files (.rda) from Node — they are R objects; port the feature engineering and special-case rules as JS, not the binaries.
Do not touch server/services/nfl-pbp.js's epa/wpa ingestion — it already carries real nflverse-computed values for historical plays via nflreadr's release pipeline; there is no defect there to fix.

Do not build a full xgboost training pipeline in JS for the live/forward WP path — a logistic regression on the same ~10 features (down, ydstogo, yardline_100, score_differential/Diff_Time_Ratio, half/game seconds remaining, timeouts, receive_2h_ko) trained on Gridiron's own historical nfl_play_by_play table gets most of the calibration benefit at a fraction of the engineering cost.

Do not merge the OT and regulation WP logic into one function — nflfastR keeps them as separate branches on purpose because the feature semantics (Drive_Diff, One_FG_Game, sudden-death vs 2012+-rules) are fundamentally different from down-to-down regulation play.
Do not treat nflreadr as a source of model code — it is a data-download wrapper only; there is nothing to port from it beyond confirming the ingestion path is already correct.

candidates.candidate: Fix the away-team win-probability sign bug by porting nflfastR's posteam_spread construction.
candidates.fixes_finding: away-team win-probability uses the home spread
candidates.mechanism: nflfastR (R/helper_add_ep_wp.R:250-254) computes posteam_spread = if_else(home==1, spread_line, -1*spread_line) BEFORE the spread ever reaches the WP model, so the model always sees the spread from the possessing team's own perspective. Gridiron's drive-sim/live-WP code evidently uses the raw home spread_line regardless of which team is on offense, so away-team win probability is silently computed off the wrong sign.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: In nfl-drive-sim.js (and anywhere nfl-live.js's liveWinProbability is called with a pregameSpread for the away team), add the same one-line transform: posteamSpread = isHome ? spreadLine : -spreadLine, and pass posteamSpread (never the raw home spread_line) into any win-probability calculation.
candidates.expected_value: Removes a directional bias that silently flips the favorite/underdog framing for every away-team-perspective win probability the app displays or bets against.
candidates.exit_test: For a known game (home favored by -6.5), verify liveWinProbability/simulateRemainder produce mirror-image probabilities when computed from the home side vs the away side at the same score/clock state (home_wp + away_wp == 1 exactly, not just approximately, at every tested state).

candidates.candidate: Replace the inverted kneel-down rule with nflfastR's hard probability override.
candidates.fixes_finding: the kneel rule is inverted and timeouts never decrement so any leading team burns an entire half
candidates.mechanism: nflfastR (R/helper_add_ep_wp.R:397-408) does not compute a kneel's outcome probabilities from the model at all for qb_kneel plays with yardline_100 > 50 — it hard-sets Touchdown/Opp_Touchdown/Field_Goal/Opp_Field_Goal/Safety/Opp_Safety = 0 and No_Score = 1, deterministically. A kneel from your own territory with the lead never has scoring risk baked in from either team.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: In nfl-drive-sim.js's kneel-handling branch, replace whatever conditional currently inverts win-probability/score-probability on a kneel with a direct override: on kneel plays (own side of field), force scoring-outcome probabilities to zero and clock-only outcome to 1, and separately fix timeout decrementing so the trailing team's forced timeouts actually reduce its own timeout count each kneel (this is a second, independent counter bug from the same finding).
candidates.expected_value: Stops the season-remainder simulator from letting a leading team run out an entire half via kneels without any clock/timeout cost, which was inflating simulated win rates for leading teams.
candidates.exit_test: Simulate a drive starting with team A leading, ball at their own 30, 3 timeouts for team B; confirm each team-A kneel drains exactly one play-clock cycle, team B's timeout count only decrements when team B actually calls one, and no kneel play is ever scored as a turnover/score risk for either side.

candidates.candidate: Port nflfastR's two-regime overtime win-probability logic (sudden-death vs 2012+ one-score-game rules) into the season-remainder simulator.
candidates.fixes_finding: the season-remainder simulator has no halftime or overtime at all
candidates.mechanism: nflfastR (R/helper_add_ep_wp.R:820-899) splits overtime rows into their own branch and computes two named quantities — Sudden_Death_WP (pre-2012 rules) and One_FG_WP (2012+ rules: receiving team keeps the ball unless it scores a TD on the opening OT drive, tracked via Drive_Diff and One_FG_Game flags) — selected by a game_year >= 2012 cutoff, then forces home_wp_post/away_wp_post to exactly 0 or 1 once OT resolves (lines ~1200-1213). None of this exists as a concept in Gridiron's simulator today.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add an explicit OT branch to nfl-drive-sim.js's season-remainder path: when regulation ends tied, simulate a separate OT drive sequence using current (2012+) one-score-game rules — track whether the first-drive team scored a TD, and if not, give the second team a possession before sudden death applies — rather than letting the existing regulation-play loop run past 3600 seconds with no rule change. Also add an explicit halftime break (clock reset to 1800s remaining, timeouts reset to 3 per team, receiving-team-of-2nd-half tracked via a receive_2h_ko-equivalent flag) since the finding notes halftime is missing too.
candidates.expected_value: Removes a structural hole in the simulator that currently either crashes, loops incorrectly, or silently misprices every game the simulator carries into overtime or across the halftime boundary — both of which happen in every real NFL season.
candidates.exit_test: Run 10,000 simulated games forced to a tied score at the 3600-second mark; confirm 100% resolve to a definite winner (no infinite loop, no tie output), and that simulated OT win rates for the receiving team land near the real 2012+-era empirical rate (~53-55%), not 50/50 sudden-death odds.

candidates.candidate: Replace the flat 7-point post-OT home-field lump with home-field advantage expressed only as a feature, matching how the real WP model treats it.
candidates.fixes_finding: home-field advantage is a flat 7-point post-OT lump distorting the key-number distribution
candidates.mechanism: Nowhere in nflfastR's actual production code (data-raw/MODELS.R, R/helper_add_ep_wp.R) is home-field advantage added as a flat point constant at any stage, OT included. It enters exactly once, as the single binary `home` feature inside the learned WP/EP models (R/helper_add_ep_wp.R:179-218, R/helper_add_nflscrapr_mutations.R:781), where its effect is learned jointly with score/clock/down state rather than bolted on afterward — there is no reference implementation anywhere in the real pipeline for a fixed additive HFA term, which confirms this is a Gridiron-only invention worth removing rather than tuning.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: In nfl-drive-sim.js, remove the flat +7 (or whatever the current constant is) applied post-OT / at game resolution, and instead let home-field advantage enter only through whatever scoring-rate or first-possession assumptions the simulator already uses per-play (i.e. make it a state feature the play-outcome sampler conditions on, not a lump-sum score adjustment at the end).
candidates.expected_value: Stops distorting the simulator's key-number distribution (3, 7, 10-point margins) with an arbitrary lump that has no basis in how the real nflverse models represent HFA, which was likely inflating push-rates around those exact numbers.
candidates.exit_test: Compare the simulator's simulated final-margin histogram (bucketed at 1-point granularity) against nflverse's actual final-margin distribution for 2021-2025 regular season games; confirm the post-fix distribution no longer shows an artificial spike/discontinuity at margin=7 that the pre-fix flat-lump version produced.

candidates.candidate: Give the live in-game win-probability estimator down/distance/field-position/timeout awareness, matching the real WP model's feature set.
candidates.fixes_finding: the kneel rule is inverted and timeouts never decrement so any leading team burns an entire half (extended: nfl-live.js's liveWinProbability has zero down/distance/possession/timeout awareness by its own docstring)
candidates.mechanism: nflfastR's real WP model (data-raw/MODELS.R:172-234, wp_model_select at R/helper_add_ep_wp.R:179-196) is trained on down, ydstogo, yardline_100, posteam/defteam_timeouts_remaining, score_differential (as Diff_Time_Ratio, clock-scaled), half/game_seconds_remaining, and receive_2h_ko — the exact state variables nfl-live.js's own docstring says its normal-CDF random-walk model explicitly lacks ("no possession, down-and-distance, or timeout awareness").
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Train a lightweight logistic regression (not full xgboost — Node has no mature xgboost binding) on Gridiron's own historical nfl_play_by_play table using the same ~10-feature set nflfastR uses (that table already has real outcomes plus nflverse's own epa/wpa for validation), and use it inside nfl-live.js / nfl-espn-pbp.js's simulateLiveGame for in-progress games instead of (or blended with) the current lead/clock/pregame-spread-only normal-CDF, especially in the final two minutes where the docstring admits the current model is worst.
candidates.expected_value: Materially improves live win-probability accuracy in exactly the game states (2-minute drill, 4th down, timeout situations) where the current model is self-documented as weakest and where in-game betting/fantasy decisions are most sensitive to accuracy.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest the new logistic-regression live-WP model against nflverse's own historical wpa-implied win probabilities on held-out games; confirm Brier score / calibration in the final 2 minutes of close games improves versus the current normal-CDF baseline, using the same calibration-bucket methodology nfl-espn-pbp.js already implements for auditing (liveWinProbabilityAudit).

result.label: GF01-drive-simulators
result.summary: Cloned/read 6 real GitHub NFL simulators and grounded each of nfl-drive-sim.js's 6 named physics bugs against an exact working line number, then found external repos with the correct pattern. Confirmed by direct code read (read-only against fantasy-football-dashboard): (1) turnover FP flip is missing specifically on interception/fumble (nfl-drive-sim.js:345 returns endYard unflipped) while the punt (:393) and turnover-on-downs (:402) branches in the SAME FILE already flip correctly with `100 - yard` — the bug is an inconsistency, not a universal miss. (2) clock units: half-scoped `clock` (0-1800, HALF=1800 at :48) is threaded into policy calls (kneel/timeout/two-minute-warning/4th-down-WP) that read like they want game-scoped seconds. (3) HFA is applied at :562 as `if (random() < homeFieldPoints/7) home += 7` AFTER the OT loop closes — a literal flat +7 lump on the final (possibly post-OT) score, confirmed exactly as described. Kneel/timeout: `kneelDecision` is fed `oppTimeouts` under the `timeouts` param name (:265), and the outer `timeouts` map is never decremented from anything `simulateDrive` returns. External evidence: rtelmore/NFLSimulatoR (MIT, 19★, real JOSS-adjacent R package) flips field position exactly once per drive-end in sample_drives.R:82; traskcon/Monte-carlo-NFL (3★, unlicensed) couples the FP-flip and possession-swap into one atomic method (monte_carlo.py:243-247), a pattern nishs9/nfl-simulation-engine (MIT, 0★ but tested) independently reproduces (GameEngine.py:89-118) while ALSO cleanly separating game_seconds_remaining vs quarter_seconds_remaining as two always-present, correctly-scoped fields (GameEngine.py:15-17, 41-42) with an explicit handle_halftime(). fivethirtyeight/nfl-elo-game (MIT, 348★, the real FiveThirtyEight Elo source) applies HFA=65 Elo points as a PREGAME probability shift gated by a neutral-site flag (forecast.py:39), never touching the score post-hoc — the architectural fix for the +7 lump. greerreNFL/nfelohfa (unlicensed but from the maintained nfelo project, pushed today) shows HFA estimated as a time-varying per-week regression+EMA value with explicit neutral-site zeroing (BaseHFA.py, AdjustedHFA.py:34-46) — the fix for the hardcoded 1.6 constant used identically at 3 call sites. nflverse/nfl4th (MIT, 22★, real nflfastR-adjacent package) treats posteam/defteam timeouts-remaining as required per-play win-probability model inputs (apply_win_prob.R:74-83), confirming timeouts must be live decrementing state, not a passively-read number. Honest negative finding: none of the 6 repos — including the two most credible ones — implements a correct OT drive simulator; this looks like a genuine gap in the OSS ecosystem, so the OT fix is "stop double-counting HFA into it" plus manual rule-audit, not "port someone else's OT loop."

repos.what_it_does: Real CRAN-adjacent R package (has paper.md, vignettes, CI) that resamples actual nflscrapR play-by-play into simulated drives/possessions given a game state (down, distance, yards-from-own-goal).
repos.adoption_path: Extract the flip-field-position-exactly-once-per-drive-end pattern from R/sample_drives.R:82 (`new_yfog <- 100 - new_yfog`, fired uniformly for every end_drive event) into a single JS helper called from ALL of nfl-drive-sim.js's drive-ending branches (interception, fumble, punt, turnover-on-downs, safety), replacing the current per-branch duplicated arithmetic where the interception/fumble branch at line 345 is missing the flip that the punt (393) and turnover-on-downs (402) branches already have.

repos.what_it_does: From-scratch Python Monte Carlo NFL game simulator built on nflverse player rate stats (completion %, INT rate, punt distance by punter); Streamlit app front end.
