result.label: GF07-entity-resolution-code
result.summary: Read team-codes.js and nfl-contract-key.js first: teamResolver()/eventKey() are deterministic and binary (exact match or null; ok:true or a typed failure) — there is no confidence gradation and no fuzzy-match path. Also found a second, un-canonicalized ad-hoc game-key at polymarket-lines.js:251-252 that builds its own `${away}@${home}` string join against espn_line_moves instead of going through eventKey()/teamResolver(), which is a second unaudited identity-matching site beyond the one named in tonight's finding. Cloned and read moj-analytical-services/splink (MIT, 2,398★, last commit 2026-09-10), dedupeio/dedupe (MIT, 4,512★, last real commit 2025-07-28), and J535D165/recordlinkage (BSD-3, 1,062★, last commit 2023-07-20, stale). Splink's Fellegi-Sunter log2(m/u) Bayes-factor summation (comparison_level.py:426-459) is the right idea to port as a hand-tuned (non-EM, no labeled pairs exist) confidence score layered on eventKey()'s existing deterministic key. Recordlinkage's SortedNeighbourhood/Block indexers (index.py) and its Date comparison's partial-credit pattern for common date errors (compare.py:335-427) are directly portable ideas for (a) blocking the 12.4M-row Polymarket tape against ~272 games without a cross join, and (b) giving graded credit to a game match that's off by exactly one calendar day from a UTC/ET boundary miss. Dedupe's active-learning ML loop is reference-only (needs labeled data and a human UI Gridiron doesn't have); its canonical.py cluster-merge pattern is a useful borrow-idea for replacing the flat TEAM_CODE_ALIASES dict with a proper per-source crosswalk table.

repos.what_it_does: Fellegi-Sunter (1969) probabilistic record linkage. comparison_level_library.py defines graded per-field comparison levels (exact, Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, Jaro, Jaccard, absolute-time-difference, geo-distance); comparison_level.py:426-459 computes match_weight=log2(m/u) per level and sums log2 Bayes factors across fields into one match probability; expectation_maximisation.py learns m/u via EM when unlabeled, accuracy.py scores against labels when available; blocking.py generates SQL blocking rules.
repos.adoption_path: Port the log2(m/u) Bayes-factor-sum scoring formula (not the EM training, SQL backends, or full linker) as a hand-tuned confidence layer on eventKey()/contractKey() in server/services/nfl-contract-key.js.

repos.what_it_does: Active-learning deduplication: predicates.py defines blocking predicates (TF-IDF, Levenshtein, canopy/search variants); training.py + labeler.py run a human-in-the-loop active-learning loop retraining a logistic-regression classifier (core.py) on labeled pairs; canonical.py collapses a matched cluster of duplicate records into one canonical merged record field-by-field.
repos.adoption_path: Do not adopt the ML/active-learning core (needs labeled pairs + human labeling UI Gridiron lacks). Borrow only canonical.py's cluster-merge pattern for building a per-source team crosswalk table.

repos.what_it_does: Classic Fellegi-Sunter toolkit on pandas: index.py provides Full/Block/SortedNeighbourhood/Random candidate-pair indexers (blocking before comparison); compare.py provides Exact/String(Jaro-Winkler,Levenshtein,qgram)/Numeric/Geographic/Date comparison classes each emitting a [0,1] similarity, with compare.py:335-427's Date class giving partial credit (default 0.5) for common date-entry errors like day/month swap; classifiers.py implements FellegiSunter-based NaiveBayes/ECM (unsupervised EM) and LogisticRegression/SVM (supervised) classifiers over the similarity-vector table.
repos.adoption_path: Do not depend on the package (stale since mid-2023). Reimplement two ideas: SortedNeighbourhood/Block-style date-window blocking for the 12.4M-row Polymarket tape against games, and the Date class's graded partial-credit pattern adapted to a one-calendar-day UTC/ET boundary near-miss inside eventKey().

candidates.candidate: Attach a Fellegi-Sunter-style match_confidence score (0-1) to eventKey()/contractKey() instead of the current binary ok:true/ok:false, using hand-tuned (non-EM) per-field log2(m/u) Bayes-factor weights for team-exact/fuzzy/miss and date-exact/shifted/miss.
candidates.fixes_finding: Game/team identity matching across sources (ESPN, nflverse, odds books, Polymarket) is done with ad hoc string matching in team-codes.js / nfl-contract-key.js, not real entity resolution.
candidates.mechanism: Port splink's comparison_level.py:426-459 log2(m/u) Bayes-factor-sum formula as a scoring layer computed alongside (not replacing) the existing deterministic nfl|{date}|{away}@{home} key; sum weights across home_team, away_team, date fields into one probability, threshold at score>=+15 (auto-accept, covers today's exact path), 0<=score<15 (log as fuzzy candidate with confidence attached), score<0 (ok:false as today).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Modify eventKey()/contractKey() in server/services/nfl-contract-key.js to compute and attach match_confidence/match_basis fields; keep the existing fail-closed contract for score<0.
candidates.expected_value: Turns silent unresolved_team failures and the raw-string join at polymarket-lines.js:251-252 into scored, auditable matches; unblocks using the 12.4M-row Polymarket tape for anything beyond spread-ladder construction.
candidates.exit_test: Hand-label ~50 known ESPN-vs-Polymarket game pairs (correct matches + known near-misses); replay through the scorer; verify 0 known-same games score below the accept threshold and 0 known-different games score above it.

candidates.candidate: Add sorted-neighborhood/date-window blocking ahead of any Polymarket-tape-to-game join, so the 12.4M-row tape is never cross-joined against every game.
candidates.fixes_finding: A 12.4-million-row Polymarket quote tape exists and is essentially unused for anything beyond spread-ladder construction (compounding the ad-hoc-matching defect above).
candidates.mechanism: Port recordlinkage's Index.Block/SortedNeighbourhood pattern (recordlinkage/index.py): sort candidate rows by ET-date and generate only a +/-1-day window of candidate games per Polymarket row before scoring, cutting candidate-pair generation from O(12.4M x n_games) to O(12.4M).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New blocking helper used ahead of the GF07-1 scorer, e.g. in polymarket-lines.js or wherever nfl-evidence-dataset.js builds its quarantine report.
candidates.expected_value: Makes it computationally tractable to actually use the Polymarket tape at scale; a hard prerequisite for any analysis that names the tape as underused.
candidates.exit_test: Benchmark candidate-set generation time and size on the full 12.4M-row tape before/after blocking; verify recall (true matches found) is unchanged versus a full cross join on a sampled subset.

candidates.candidate: Give partial credit in eventKey() for a game-date mismatch of exactly one calendar day (a UTC/ET boundary near-miss) instead of treating it as a hard non-match.
candidates.fixes_finding: Game/team identity matching across sources is ad hoc, specifically the date component of eventKey() in nfl-contract-key.js, which itself flags the '1:15am-UTC Monday-night problem' as a known risk but has no path to notice a one-day near-miss once it happens.
candidates.mechanism: Adapt recordlinkage's Date comparison class (compare.py:335-427), which gives partial credit for common date-entry errors, into a lower-weight Bayes-factor level (see GF07-1) fired when |date_a - date_b| == 1 calendar day and both team codes match exactly.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Extend eventKey()'s date handling in nfl-contract-key.js to compute a shifted-date candidate and feed it into the GF07-1 scorer as a +2-weight level.
candidates.expected_value: Closes a specific, already-flagged-in-comments class of near-miss game-key failure rather than leaving it as an acknowledged but unhandled risk.
candidates.exit_test: Unit test a kickoff at 12:15am ET Monday (11:15pm UTC Sunday) through two synthetic feeds with different tz handling; verify the module now attaches a fuzzy-date match instead of matching the wrong day or returning unresolved_team.

candidates.candidate: Replace the flat TEAM_CODE_ALIASES dict with a per-source team crosswalk table (one row per franchise, one column per source: ESPN, nflverse, Polymarket event-title tokens, book-feed spellings), and route polymarket-lines.js's raw-string game key through it.
candidates.fixes_finding: Game/team identity matching across sources is ad hoc — specifically, polymarket-lines.js:251-252 builds its own `${away_team}@${home_team}` string key straight from espn_line_moves rows instead of going through canonicalTeamCode()/eventKey(), a second unaudited identity-matching site beyond team-codes.js itself.
candidates.mechanism: Borrow dedupe's canonical.py pattern of collapsing a matched cluster's multiple source spellings into one canonical record, applied to teams: a TEAM_CROSSWALK table instead of a one-directional alias dict, with every join (including the Polymarket-to-ESPN one) routed through the same canonicalTeamCode()/teamResolver() call.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Refactor server/services/polymarket-lines.js lines ~251-252 to call eventKey()/teamResolver() instead of building the raw string join key; extend team-codes.js's alias structure into a crosswalk.
candidates.expected_value: Removes exactly one of the ad-hoc string-matching sites named in tonight's findings, at low risk since it is a refactor onto an already-tested canonical function.
candidates.exit_test: Re-run the polymarket-lines ESPN join over last week's captured data before/after the refactor; diff matched event_ids and expect an identical-or-superset match set with zero new unresolved games.

candidates.candidate: Build a small hand-labeled gold set of known game/team identity pairs (correct matches and known near-miss non-matches) and an accuracy harness that scores the confidence matcher against it in CI.
candidates.mechanism: Port splink's accuracy.py concept (precision/recall against labeled pairs) as a lightweight internal test fixture, independent of splink's SQL/EM machinery.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New test file, e.g. server/services/__tests__/nfl-contract-key.entity-resolution.test.js, exercising GF07-1's scorer against ~100 hand-labeled pairs.
candidates.expected_value: Gives objective, regression-testable proof that the confidence-scored matcher (GF07-1) actually beats the current binary resolver, rather than relying on spot checks.
candidates.exit_test: Test suite reports precision/recall on the gold set; merge gate requires 100% recall on known-same games and zero false-positive matches on known-different games.

do_not_do: Do not adopt dedupe's active-learning/ML classifier loop wholesale — it needs labeled training pairs and a human-labeling UI Gridiron doesn't have, for a 32-team problem that doesn't need ML.
Do not depend on recordlinkage as a live pip dependency — it has been stale since mid-2023; port the blocking and graded-date-comparison ideas, don't import the package.

Do not run splink's EM training against the 32-team dictionary — there is no ambiguity in a closed, well-known 32-entity set for EM to resolve; reserve any probabilistic/EM idea for the game-key fuzzy layer only, and start that hand-tuned, not EM-trained.
Do not touch fantasy-football-dashboard directly tonight — it is read-only while a live server captures Week 1 games; all candidates here are proposals for a future PR.

result.label: GF08-conformal-prediction-code
result.summary: Cloned and read (not README-skimmed) 4 conformal-prediction repos: scikit-learn-contrib/MAPIE (active, full CQR + non-exchangeable time-series methods, call as a library), henrikbostrom/crepes (active, minimal split-conformal + Mondrian binning, port), yromano/cqr (original CQR paper reference code, port the exact score formula), aangelopoulos/conformal-time-series (ACI/conformal-PID, port for the non-exchangeable week-over-week case). All four target the same verified defect: server/services/nfl-ensemble.js:203-251 predictiveDistribution() pools all-history residuals loosely conditioned on spread/total similarity and widens them with an ad hoc disagreement-based "inflation" multiplier — no held-out calibration split, no coverage backtest, and the code itself already flags calibration_state:'research_distribution_only', production_eligible:false. Also read hamrel-cxu/EnbPI (rough research-script code, MIT, 134★) and explicitly excluded it as reference-only/avoid-as-library. research/.venv already carries scikit-learn 1.7.2 + lightgbm as an isolated, no-app-runtime-dependency environment, which is where the calibration fitting and MAPIE cross-check belong — no live server code needs to be touched.

repos.what_it_does: Full CQR pipeline (mapie/regression/quantile_regression.py, 2343 lines): _QuantileConformalizer.conformalize() (line 744) computes conformity scores on a calibration split via QuantileRegressionScore.get_conformity_scores(); predict_interval() (line 1193) applies the calibrated width. Supports CV-aggregation strategies including pinball-loss-weighted fold averaging (_pinball_weighted_mean, line 796). Separately ships mapie/regression/time_series_regression.py (512 lines) for non-exchangeable/sequential EnbPI-style intervals, and mapie/metrics/regression.py for coverage/width scoring.
repos.adoption_path: pip install mapie into research/.venv (already an isolated env with scikit-learn 1.7.2/lightgbm/xgboost, explicitly 'No app-runtime dependency'); use SplitConformalRegressor/ConformalizedQuantileRegressor as an independent second implementation to validate the JS port's coverage/width before flagging production_eligible.

repos.what_it_does: src/crepes/base.py ConformalRegressor (line 556): fit() stores sorted abs calibration residuals (optionally normalized by a difficulty sigma, optionally split into Mondrian bins); predict_int() computes alpha_index = floor((1-confidence)*(n+1))-1 and returns y_hat +/- alphas[alpha_index] — the textbook split-conformal interval, with per-bin Mondrian variants for category-conditional width.
repos.adoption_path: Reimplement the ~30-40 line fit/predict_int algorithm directly in JS inside server/services/nfl-ensemble.js, replacing the residual-quantile + ad hoc 'inflation' block in predictiveDistribution() with real split-conformal math; use the existing |homeSpread| cohort filter as the Mondrian bin key.

repos.what_it_does: nonconformist/nc.py QuantileRegErrFunc (line 207): apply() computes CQR nonconformity score err = max(y_lower-y, y-y_upper); apply_inverse() sorts scores and takes index = clamp(ceil((1-significance)*(n+1))-1, 0, n-1) as the symmetric expansion applied to both quantile bounds — the exact construction from the original NeurIPS 2019 CQR paper.
repos.adoption_path: Port the ~15-line score/inverse formula (skip the neural-net/forest scaffolding around it) on top of LightGBM quantile models fit in research/tree_lab.py's existing 'Package C' infrastructure; export calibrated scalar(s) as a JSON file the Node service reads.

repos.what_it_does: core/methods.py aci()/aci_clipped() (line 35): maintains an online miscoverage target alphat, updated each step via grad = -alpha if covered else 1-alpha; alphat -= lr*grad — the Adaptive Conformal Inference / conformal-PID update rule for non-exchangeable, distribution-shifting sequences. trailing_window() (line 16) is the simpler sliding-window baseline it's compared against. Both operate on a precomputed conformity-score array, so they compose with the CQR/split-conformal scores from the other candidates.
repos.adoption_path: Port the ~20-line ACI update loop (skip statsmodels-based baselines) to run once per week after games settle: feed realized conformity scores in, update persisted alphat, use it (not the fixed nominal alpha) for next week's calibrated quantile — corrects for within-season team-strength drift that the current all-history residual pool ignores.

repos.what_it_does: PI_class_EnbPI.py compute_PIs_Ensemble_online() (line 118): bootstrap-ensemble LOO residuals + sliding-window empirical quantile for sequential data. Verified as rough research-script code (hardcoded keras.callbacks/Sequential branches inside the fit loop, commented-out profiling lines, stale __pycache__ in history) — not written for reuse as a library.
repos.adoption_path: Do not port or call; the underlying idea is subsumed by the cleaner aangelopoulos/conformal-time-series ACI code above. Use only as background reading on the online-residual-window idea.

candidates.candidate: Replace nfl-ensemble.js's ad hoc residual-inflation interval with a ported split-conformal regressor (crepes-style), Mondrian-binned by spread bucket
candidates.fixes_finding: No conformal or otherwise honestly-calibrated uncertainty interval exists anywhere in the pipeline — margins/totals are point forecasts with an assumed-normal SD (verified concretely as nfl-ensemble.js:203-251 predictiveDistribution()'s all-history residual pool + disagreement/30 inflation hack, self-flagged production_eligible:false).
candidates.mechanism: henrikbostrom/crepes src/crepes/base.py:556-609 ConformalRegressor.fit/predict_int: sort abs calibration residuals descending, take index=floor((1-confidence)*(n+1))-1 as the interval half-width, with a Mondrian-bin variant that repeats the same calculation per category so width can vary by bin while each bin keeps its own coverage guarantee. This is a distribution-free, finite-sample marginal-coverage guarantee under exchangeability — not an ad hoc multiplier.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: In nfl-ensemble.js, replace the marginResiduals/inflation block inside predictiveDistribution() with: (1) a genuinely held-out calibration slice of recent weeks (not just 'games before this week'), (2) bins keyed by |homeSpread| bucket instead of the current soft +/-2.5 filter with all-history fallback, (3) the crepes index formula for each bin's half-width. Ship as a JS function with no new runtime dependency.
candidates.expected_value: Turns 'research_distribution_only' into an interval with an actual, checkable coverage guarantee instead of a tunable fudge factor, enabling real risk-based staking decisions instead of an arbitrary inflation constant.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest empirical coverage on 500+ held-out games across multiple seasons: the 80% nominal interval must contain the true margin within roughly [76%,84%] (Clopper-Pearson tolerance); reject/redesign bins if coverage falls outside that band or is wildly uneven across spread buckets.

candidates.candidate: Port the exact CQR asymmetric nonconformity score onto LightGBM quantile regressors already buildable in research/tree_lab.py, for heteroscedastic (condition-dependent) interval width
candidates.fixes_finding: No conformal or otherwise honestly-calibrated uncertainty interval exists anywhere in the pipeline — margins/totals are point forecasts with an assumed-normal SD.
candidates.mechanism: yromano/cqr nonconformist/nc.py:207-229 QuantileRegErrFunc: score = max(y_lower-y, y-y_upper) on a calibration split; apply_inverse sorts scores and takes index=ceil((1-significance)*(n+1))-1 (clamped) as the symmetric expansion applied to both quantile bounds. Because y_lower/y_upper come from a quantile regressor conditioned on features, the resulting interval width varies by game (heteroscedastic) instead of being one global constant, while retaining the same finite-sample coverage guarantee as split-conformal.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Fit q10/q90 LightGBM quantile models offline in research/ (using the tree_lab.py Package C infra, which already targets 'quantile regression alike' per its own header comment) on the same feature set predictiveDistribution() consumes (spread, total, disagreement, etc); calibrate the CQR score on a held-out slice; export the calibration scalar(s) as a static JSON the Node service reads to widen/narrow its quantile predictions.
candidates.expected_value: Should tighten average interval width at matched coverage relative to the current fixed-shape residual approach — this is the documented advantage of CQR over plain split-conformal (narrower average width at equal coverage) because width now concentrates where the model's own quantile predictions say uncertainty actually is (e.g. wide-spread, high-disagreement games), not a single global constant.
candidates.exit_test: At matched ~80% empirical coverage, mean interval width under CQR must be no larger than the current predictiveDistribution() width; adopt only if width shrinks (or stays flat) without breaking the coverage check from GF08-C1's exit test.

candidates.candidate: Port ACI (adaptive conformal inference / conformal-PID) as a weekly online correction layer on top of C1/C2, to handle within-season non-exchangeability
candidates.fixes_finding: No conformal or otherwise honestly-calibrated uncertainty interval exists anywhere in the pipeline — margins/totals are point forecasts with an assumed-normal SD; this candidate specifically addresses that the current method draws from an all-history residual pool with no mechanism to notice or correct for a season running systematically hotter/colder/more-volatile than history.
candidates.mechanism: aangelopoulos/conformal-time-series core/methods.py:35-70 aci()/aci_clipped(): maintains an online miscoverage target alphat updated each step by grad = -alpha if covered else 1-alpha; alphat -= lr*grad, then draws the trailing-window empirical quantile at level 1-alphat instead of the fixed nominal alpha. This is the standard published fix (Gibbs & Candes 2021; Angelopoulos/Candes/Tibshirani 2023) for exactly the situation where the exchangeability assumption breaks down over time — which a shifting-team-strength NFL season is a textbook case of.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Run once per week after that week's games settle: feed the realized CQR/split-conformal scores from C1/C2 into a small persisted state object holding the current alphat, apply the ACI update, and use the resulting alphat for the next week's interval instead of a fixed alpha. Wire the weekly hook the same way forward-ledger.js already does weekly snapshotting.
candidates.expected_value: Keeps the interval's realized coverage tracked continuously through the season instead of only checked in an aggregate backtest — directly relevant given nfl-team-strength.js's rating blend is itself a hand-tuned, non-principled state-space substitute (a separate verified finding), meaning the residual distribution this interval draws on is generated by a process already known to drift without correction.
candidates.exit_test: Track rolling coverage over the last 50 realized games live through a season; alert/roll back to the static C1/C2 method if realized coverage drifts more than 10 percentage points from the target for 3+ consecutive weeks.

candidates.candidate: Stand up MAPIE in research/.venv as an independent cross-check on whatever hand-rolled JS conformal code ships, before flipping production_eligible
candidates.fixes_finding: No conformal or otherwise honestly-calibrated uncertainty interval exists anywhere in the pipeline — margins/totals are point forecasts with an assumed-normal SD; this candidate is the audit layer that keeps C1-C3's from-scratch implementations honest.
candidates.mechanism: scikit-learn-contrib/MAPIE mapie/regression/quantile_regression.py:744-790 _QuantileConformalizer.conformalize()/predict_interval(), and mapie/regression/time_series_regression.py's block-bootstrap non-exchangeable intervals, verified as an actively maintained (commits as recent as 2026-09-08), peer-adjacent (scikit-learn-contrib) reference implementation of both CQR and the non-exchangeable case behind one API, with mapie/metrics/regression.py providing ready-made coverage/width scoring.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: pip install mapie into research/.venv (already isolated, 'No app-runtime dependency' per its own requirements.txt comment); export the same feature/target CSV used to fit and calibrate the JS port; run MAPIE's SplitConformalRegressor/ConformalizedQuantileRegressor on it and diff coverage/width numbers against the hand-rolled JS output.
candidates.expected_value: Cheap insurance against a 7th silent numeric bug in hand-rolled probability/interval math — the drive simulator alone already had six verified physics bugs in this codebase's own hand-rolled numeric code, so an independent, actively-maintained library's numbers are a low-cost way to catch an analogous bug here before it reaches production_eligible:true.
candidates.exit_test: MAPIE's coverage matches the JS port within +/-2 percentage points and width within +/-5% on the same held-out data; any larger discrepancy is investigated and resolved before the JS port is marked production_eligible.

do_not_do: Do not port or call hamrel-cxu/EnbPI directly — it is rough, unmaintained (last commit 2023-11-25) research-script code (hardcoded Keras/Sequential branches inside the fit loop, leftover profiling print statements) not written for reuse; its idea is subsumed by the cleaner aangelopoulos/conformal-time-series ACI implementation.

Do not treat 'games before the target week' (cutoff-safety) as equivalent to a proper held-out calibration split — it is necessary but not sufficient for the exchangeability assumption any of these methods needs; a genuinely separate calibration slice from whatever data fit the point forecast is required.

Do not flip predictiveDistribution()'s production_eligible flag to true on the strength of any of these ports alone — run the actual coverage backtest (GF08-C1's exit test) and, ideally, the MAPIE cross-check (GF08-C4) first.

Do not conflate this fix with the team-strength rating blend defect (nfl-team-strength.js) — ACI (GF08-C3) mitigates the symptom (stale residual pool) at the interval layer but does not itself replace the non-principled state-space blend; that is a separate, larger fix.

result.label: GF04 Bayesian sports Stan/PyMC harvest
result.summary: Read 5 real Bayesian sports-modeling repos (verified by reading the actual Stan/Cython/PyMC source, not READMEs). Best find: LeoEgidi/footBayes (GPL-2, 59 stars, last commit 2026-09-09, tied to a 2026 JRSS-C paper) ships a working, currently-maintained dynamic bivariate-Poisson Stan model (Karlis-Ntzoufras likelihood + Owen/Koopman-Lit/commensurate-prior state-space evolution of attack/defense) AND a parallel dynamic hierarchical Negative-Binomial model in the same file family — i.e. real, working code for two of tonight's biggest gaps at once: the hand-tuned team-strength blend and the point-estimate-only player props. pymc-devs/pymc-examples supplies the canonical static Baio-Blangiardo hierarchical-Poisson reference plus a documented arviz diagnostics/JSON workflow (repo too large to full-clone, read via GitHub API instead). martineastwood/penaltyblog (MIT, 220 stars, updated yesterday) is a from-scratch pip-installable Cython/ensemble-MCMC hierarchical Bayesian model with Dixon-Coles correlation — no Stan toolchain needed, good cheap/always-on tier. lbenz730/soccer_ha_covid (unlicensed, published Benz & Lopez paper) independently corroborates the same bivariate-Poisson shared-intercept construction with a pre/post-COVID home-field split — reference-only, no license to port. pjastam/r-bayesian-football-odds was checked and is JAGS, not Stan/PyMC/NumPyro — explicitly excluded on toolkit grounds. Full posterior-to-JSON export recipes specified for all three code-bearing sources (draws_df/jsonlite for Stan+R, .values.tolist() for arviz, trace_dict for penaltyblog) so Node never needs a Stan/PyMC runtime, only JSON.parse.

repos.what_it_does: R package (CmdStan backend via instantiate/rstan) implementing ~18 football models. Verified in src/stan/biv_pois_dynamic.stan: Karlis-Ntzoufras bivariate Poisson likelihood (custom bipois_lpmf with correct normalizing constant + log-sum-exp), attack/defense abilities following a random-walk state-space evolution across time periods, with three real evolution-variance schemes (Owen 2011 shared sigma, Egidi et al. 2018 separate sigmas, Koopman & Lit 2015 variance inflation at summer breaks) plus a 2026-paper spike-and-slab commensurate-prior weighted-dynamic option. src/stan/neg_bin_dynamic.stan mirrors the same dynamic state-space structure with a hierarchical Negative Binomial likelihood instead — real overdispersion modeling for count props. generated quantities blocks do posterior-predictive replication and per-game log_lik for calibration/LOO.
repos.adoption_path: Run src/stan/biv_pois_dynamic.stan and src/stan/neg_bin_dynamic.stan via a CmdStanR/CmdStanPy sidecar fed from Gridiron's existing schedule+score tables; export posterior draws/summaries as JSON for server/services/nfl-team-strength.js (state-space update) and the props module (NB distributions) to consume.

repos.what_it_does: Repo is 1.15GB, over the 200MB clone-skip threshold, so read via GitHub contents API instead of git clone: fetched and read in full examples/case_studies/rugby_analytics.myst.md (489 lines). Verified real, current PyMC5 code implementing the canonical Baio & Blangiardo (2010) hierarchical Poisson model: sum-to-zero attack/defense parameters via pm.Deterministic, independent (not bivariate) Poisson likelihoods for home/away scores, static (non-dynamic) abilities, sampled with pm.sample and diagnosed with az.plot_energy/az.summary(kind='diagnostics')/az.hdi/az.plot_forest.
repos.adoption_path: Not a port target (footBayes is a strict superset) — copy the sum-to-zero parameterization and, more importantly, the arviz rhat/energy/hdi diagnostic checklist that Gridiron currently has nowhere in its pipeline.

repos.what_it_does: Verified in penaltyblog/models/hierarchical_bayesian_goal_model.py, penaltyblog/bayes/sampler_api.py, penaltyblog/bayes/likelihood.pyx: a from-scratch dependency-light Bayesian engine, NOT Stan/PyMC — a hand-rolled differential-evolution ensemble MCMC sampler (DiffEvolEnsembleSampler, multiprocessing, emcee-style) driving a Cython nogil log-posterior (_hierarchical_log_prob_c) with a real hierarchical prior (learned sigma_att/sigma_def) over a Dixon-Coles-weighted negative log-likelihood with a correlation parameter rho (dixon_coles_neg_ll_c) — correlation is the DC tau adjustment, not a joint bivariate distribution. fit() produces self.trace as a plain numpy array and self.trace_dict as {param_name: ndarray}.
repos.adoption_path: pip install penaltyblog; run HierarchicalBayesianGoalModel as a small weekly Python service/subprocess Gridiron's Node code shells out to — no CmdStan compile step, cheap always-on tier alongside the deeper footBayes fits.

repos.what_it_does: Repo tree is 4.5GB (mostly fbref_data scrape caches and figure PNGs), over the 200MB threshold — read specific files in full via GitHub contents API instead of cloning: stan/goals/bvp_goals_lambda3.stan (75 lines) and models/goals/bvp_goals_lambda3.R (95 lines). Verified working code behind a published paper (Benz & Lopez, home-advantage-during-COVID via bivariate Poisson regression; Lopez is the NFL's Head of Football Data & Analytics): Karlis-Ntzoufras bivariate Poisson with a shared lambda3=exp(fixed_cov) covariance intercept, empirical-Bayes priors splitting home-field advantage pre- vs. post-COVID, fit via rstan::stan(iter=20000, warmup=10000, adapt_delta=0.95), posterior pulled with rstan::extract().
repos.adoption_path: No license to port cleanly and the construction is already present, cleanly licensed, in footBayes. Use only as independent corroboration that the shared-intercept bivariate-Poisson trick is the standard approach — directly relevant as a real dependence model for Gridiron's currently-independent teaser/same-game leg correlation.

repos.what_it_does: Verified in NL_eredivisie_2014_2019.R (library(runjags), m3_string <- "model {" at line 48): this is JAGS, not Stan/PyMC/NumPyro. Fits a hierarchical Poisson model for Dutch Eredivisie goals via runjags::run.jags on 5 bundled seasons of CSV data.
repos.adoption_path: Explicitly out of toolkit scope for this task — kept only to document it was checked and correctly excluded; not a port/call candidate.

candidates.candidate: Port footBayes' neg_bin_dynamic.stan (dynamic hierarchical Negative Binomial) as a real distributional model for player props
candidates.fixes_finding: Player props are point-estimate projections, not distributions — no negative-binomial/hierarchical/calibrated model; the module is the project's one area of genuine measured skill (2+ TD Brier skill +27%) but under-measured against real prices.
candidates.mechanism: neg_bin_dynamic.stan (LeoEgidi/footBayes src/stan/neg_bin_dynamic.stan, read in full) fits a time-varying hierarchical NB per team/period with the same Owen/Koopman-Lit/commensurate variance machinery as the bivariate-Poisson sibling model, giving a real overdispersion parameter and full posterior predictive distribution instead of a point mean.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Run via CmdStanR/CmdStanPy sidecar on the existing player-week count outcomes (TDs, receptions), export posterior predictive draws/quantiles as JSON (see notes file export spec), feed into the props module in place of the current point-estimate projection so Brier/calibration can be measured against real prices honestly.
candidates.expected_value: Turns the project's one area of measured skill into a properly calibrated distribution instead of a point guess, which is a precondition for pricing props against real market vig rather than just picking a side.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest predictive-interval coverage (e.g. 80% CI should contain the realized count ~80% of the time) on held-out player-weeks; ship only if coverage is within 5pp of nominal and Brier skill on 2+ TD props does not regress from the current baseline.

candidates.candidate: Replace nfl-team-strength.js's hand-tuned preseason/in-season blend with footBayes' dynamic bivariate-Poisson state-space update
candidates.fixes_finding: Team-strength ratings (nfl-team-strength.js) mix stale preseason priors with in-season data via a hand-tuned blend, not a principled state-space/Bayesian update.
candidates.mechanism: biv_pois_dynamic.stan (read in full) implements att[t,team]/def[t,team] as a random walk with mu_att[t]=att[t-1], and three genuine variance-evolution options (Owen constant sigma, Koopman-Lit variance inflation at summer/bye breaks, and a 2026-paper spike-and-slab commensurate prior that lets each team's rating shrink toward 'no change' or 'free update' per period based on the data) — a real Bayesian filter, not a fixed hand-tuned weight.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Fit weekly via CmdStanR sidecar on completed games so far each season with the preseason prior as the t=1 prior; export att/def posterior (mean+sd+quantiles per team-period) as JSON per the notes-file spec; nfl-team-strength.js reads this JSON instead of computing its own blend coefficient.
candidates.expected_value: Replaces an arbitrary blend weight with a data-driven one whose uncertainty is honestly quantified, which should reduce the model's reliance on late-season overreaction or early-season preseason-prior stickiness that a fixed blend can't adapt.
candidates.exit_test: Walk-forward backtest: compare weekly team-strength-implied spread error (vs. actual margin) for the new state-space ratings against the current hand-tuned blend over at least one full past season; ship only if MAE improves or CLV on ratings-driven picks stops being negative.

candidates.candidate: Feed the footBayes/penaltyblog Bayesian rating posterior into nfl-ensemble.js as a genuinely independent signal
candidates.fixes_finding: The NFL ensemble's blend is forecast ≈ 0.68 + 0.632·market — a naive shrinkage toward the closing line, not real forecast combination. 20 components collapse to ~3 independent signals.
candidates.mechanism: Both footBayes (Stan, GPL-2) and penaltyblog's HierarchicalBayesianGoalModel (Cython/custom ensemble MCMC, MIT, verified in likelihood.pyx) are fit purely from historical scores/ratings, with no reference to the market line anywhere in the model — a structurally independent estimator, unlike the 17 components that already collapse into a market-shrinkage.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Add the Bayesian posterior mean margin/total (with its own posterior sd) as one ensemble component in nfl-ensemble.js, weighted by inverse posterior variance rather than a fixed shrinkage coefficient, so the ensemble has an actual second independent axis of information instead of 20 near-duplicate market-anchored features.
candidates.expected_value: Addresses the root cause of the -2.28 CLV / 78% adverse-move finding — a genuinely independent forecast is the only way an ensemble can beat forecast≈shrinkage(market), since averaging correlated components can't create new information.
candidates.exit_test: Re-estimate the ensemble weight vector after adding the Bayesian component; ship only if the new component's ensemble weight is non-trivial (not shrunk to ~0) and CLV on ensemble picks improves out-of-sample vs. the current -2.28 baseline.

candidates.candidate: Use the Karlis-Ntzoufras shared-intercept bivariate-Poisson term as a real dependence model for same-game/teaser correlation
candidates.fixes_finding: Teaser-leg and same-game correlation is assumed independent (server/betting/nfl/strategy/teaser-leg-rates.js) with no copula/dependence model, despite legs sharing a game.
candidates.mechanism: Verified identically in two independent implementations — footBayes' src/stan/biv_pois.stan/biv_pois_dynamic.stan and lbenz730/soccer_ha_covid's stan/goals/bvp_goals_lambda3.stan — a shared covariance intercept lambda3=exp(rho or fixed_cov) added to both team's Poisson rates (h_goals ~ poisson(lambda1+lambda3), a_goals ~ poisson(lambda2+lambda3)) gives home/away scores a real, estimated positive correlation instead of treating them (and legs derived from them, e.g. game total + spread) as independent.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Fit the bivariate-Poisson lambda3 term per game from the same posterior used for team strength; use the implied home/away score covariance to compute correlated joint probabilities for same-game teaser legs in teaser-leg-rates.js instead of the current product-of-independent-marginals assumption.
candidates.expected_value: Removes a specific, named independence assumption that is known to be wrong (legs from the same game are correlated by construction) and replaces it with an estimated, game-specific correlation rather than a guessed constant.
candidates.exit_test: Compare realized teaser-leg joint hit-rate against the model's predicted joint probability (calibration plot) for both the current independence assumption and the new bivariate-Poisson-implied correlation on held-out weeks; ship only if the new model's calibration error is smaller.

candidates.candidate: Export full posterior draws/quantiles (not an assumed-normal SD) for margin/total forecasts as the honest uncertainty source
candidates.fixes_finding: No conformal or otherwise honestly-calibrated uncertainty interval exists anywhere in the pipeline — margins/totals are point forecasts with an assumed-normal SD.
candidates.mechanism: footBayes' generated quantities blocks (verified in biv_pois_dynamic.stan) already compute per-game posterior-predictive y_rep/theta_home/theta_away draws; posterior::as_draws_df() + jsonlite::write_json() (or posterior::summarise_draws() for a smaller quantile-only payload) turns these into a JSON file with real empirical quantiles per game, no Gaussian assumption anywhere.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Replace the assumed-normal-SD step wherever margin/total point forecasts are converted to probabilities with a lookup into the exported empirical quantile grid (or a KDE fit to the exported draws) from the Stan posterior predictive.
candidates.expected_value: Directly closes a named, unambiguous gap (no calibrated uncertainty exists at all today) with output the model was already computing internally (generated quantities) but never exporting.
candidates.exit_test: PIT (probability integral transform) histogram of realized margins against the exported quantile forecasts should be approximately uniform; ship only if it is flatter than the current assumed-normal-SD PIT histogram on the same held-out games.

candidates.candidate: Establish one canonical posterior-export JSON schema (meta + params/draws) as the single source Node consumers read
candidates.mechanism: All three code-bearing sources found tonight (footBayes/R+posterior package, pymc-examples/arviz InferenceData, penaltyblog/plain numpy trace_dict) can each be reduced to the same two-file contract: a posterior_meta.json (dims, team/time labels, n_draws) plus either posterior_draws.json (full draws) or posterior_summary.json (mean/sd/quantiles) — verified as buildable from real, inspected APIs (posterior::as_draws_df + jsonlite::write_json for Stan; DataArray.values.tolist() for arviz; already-built trace_dict for penaltyblog).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Define this schema once, write a tiny shared Node-side loader (parse meta, reshape bracket-indexed param names like att[3,7] into arrays) that every Bayesian-model integration (props NB model, team-strength state-space, teaser correlation) writes to and reads from — a single contract instead of five independent ad hoc CLV-style implementations repeating the same mistake.
candidates.expected_value: Given tonight's separately-confirmed finding of five disagreeing CLV implementations over four tables, standardizing the export contract for every new Bayesian-model integration before it starts is cheap insurance against a sixth divergent implementation.
candidates.exit_test: Every new Bayesian-model JSON export (props NB, team-strength, teaser correlation) validates against one shared JSON-schema file and is read by one shared Node loader function, with zero per-integration reshaping code duplicated.

do_not_do: Do not run CmdStan/rstan/PyMC/penaltyblog's sampler inside the live Node process or anywhere near the live Week-1-capture server — these are offline/weekly-cron fits whose JSON output Node reads; the sampler itself never touches the production request path or the fantasy-football-dashboard repo, which stays read-only.

Do not port lbenz730/soccer_ha_covid's code directly — it has no license. Use footBayes (GPL-2, same Karlis-Ntzoufras construction) as the actual code source and cite Benz & Lopez only as corroborating published methodology.
Do not treat pjastam/r-bayesian-football-odds as an implementation target — it is JAGS, explicitly out of the Stan/PyMC/NumPyro scope given for this task; it was read and excluded, not adopted.

Do not full-clone pymc-devs/pymc-examples (1.15GB) or lbenz730/soccer_ha_covid (4.5GB) — both exceed the 200MB clone-skip threshold; relevant files were read individually via the GitHub contents API instead.
Do not make any paid API calls or install/execute any of the downloaded/fetched code — all repo code in this task was read-only, for extraction and specification purposes.

result.label: GF10-trial-registry-preregistration-code
result.summary: Cloned and read 4 repos (quantskills/skill-backtest-overfit, eslazarev/purged-cross-validation, Aliipou/backtest-audit, mnemox-ai/deflated-sharpe) covering DSR, PBO/CSCV, Holm/Bonferroni/BHY haircuts, and autocorrelation-corrected effective trial counts. Cross-checked against Gridiron's existing conventions (024_candidate_findings.js state machine, 027_decision_tape.js append-only/content-addressed pattern, and the five ad hoc *-lab/preregistered.json files) to design a concrete research_studies / research_trials / research_trial_corrections schema that promotes the existing per-lab JSON preregistration convention into a queryable, append-only, DB-enforced trial registry with real multiplicity correction for the 21-model historical search finding. Found, as a bonus, that DSR itself has two disagreeing formula variants across these small repos (variance-based vs. Gumbel closed-form) — the same governance gap already flagged for CLV, one level over — and designed the schema's dsr_method enum specifically to prevent that from recurring ungoverned.

sources.title: quantskills/skill-backtest-overfit — deflated_sharpe.py, pbo_cscv.py, haircut.py, overfit_report.py
sources.key_result: Correct, self-tested (PASS on known-answer noise/edge cases) implementations of DSR (Bailey & Lopez de Prado 2014), CSCV/PBO (Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado, Zhu 2017), and Harvey-Liu (2015) Bonferroni/Holm/BHY haircuts, orchestrated into one pass/fail verdict; GPL-3.0, no persistence layer, no purge/embargo inside its CSCV blocks.

sources.title: eslazarev/purged-cross-validation (purgedcv) — _pbo.py, _metrics.py, optuna_integration.py
sources.key_result: MIT-licensed, actively maintained (pushed 2026-09-04), tested package: PBO built on purge/embargo-aware CombinatorialPurgedCV (unlike quantskills' unpurged CSCV), plus effective_n_trials() — an autocorrelation-time correction (Geyer 1992 initial-positive-sequence) for the number of INDEPENDENT trials behind a correlated/sequential search, with a TrialSharpeRecorder callback that is a minimal working trial ledger.

sources.title: Aliipou/backtest-audit — auditor.py, backup.py
sources.key_result: Installable package (tests, CI, Docker) combining DSR+PBO+Monte-Carlo permutation+walk-forward+regime+robustness into an AuditReport with overall_risk_score() (PASS/WARN/FAIL -> 0.0/0.4/0.8, feeds position_size = base*(1-risk_score)); persistence is only timestamped JSON snapshots to a local backup dir keyed by strategy_id -- confirms file-based ad hoc registries (like Gridiron's own *-lab/ dirs) don't scale to cross-strategy multiplicity correction. No license file (all rights reserved); no Holm/Bonferroni present despite doing multiple-testing work.

sources.title: mnemox-ai/deflated-sharpe — gates.py
sources.key_result: Apache-2.0, dependency-light DSR + Benjamini-Hochberg FDR implementation that uses a DIFFERENT (Gumbel/extreme-value closed-form) approximation for E[max Sharpe] than quantskills/eslazarev's variance-based formula -- a real, literature-level instance of the same 'multiple disagreeing implementations, different math' failure mode already flagged for Gridiron's CLV, one level over, for DSR.

candidates.candidate: Create research_studies / research_trials / research_trial_corrections tables (full DDL in notes file) that promote the existing per-lab preregistered.json/report.json convention (server/data/{book-lag-lab,expert-selector-lab,market-lab,role-scenario-lab,tree-lab}/) into one queryable, append-only trial registry, with a DB-enforced scored_at >= declared_at CHECK on every trial.
candidates.fixes_finding: No trial registry exists with real preregistration + multiplicity correction (Holm/PBO/deflated-Sharpe) for the 21-model historical search that has already been run.
candidates.mechanism: Each of the 21 (or future) model/strategy trials becomes one preregistered research_trials row inside a research_studies group that defines the shared hypothesis/baselines/failure criteria/selection rule up front (mirroring *-lab/preregistered.json fields exactly); scoring can only fill scored_at after declared_at is already committed, enforced by a CHECK constraint plus an UPDATE-blocking trigger (following 027_decision_tape.js's append-only pattern) so a trial cannot be silently re-declared after its result is known.
