Exact file for the engine itself was not located in this read-only pass (only nfl-props-player-features.js and nfl-props.js were found under server/services for props; the player_week_engine module name should be grep-confirmed by whoever implements this before writing code).
candidates.expected_value: A validated cold-start prior would remove a known silent no-op in the fantasy loop, which per standing priority (fantasy over betting) is worth more than an equivalent betting-side improvement, but this candidate carries the most uncertainty of the four since the exact engine file/table was not verified in this pass.
candidates.exit_test: If grep for player_week_engine in the actual codebase does not turn up a heads/cold-start field matching tonight's finding, or if leave-one-season-out CV shows no held-out lift over a naive league-mean cold-start, do not implement.

do_not_do: Do not let PySR's or gplearn's own default model_selection / best-fitness output reach a production Gridiron surface directly — both are verified to select on training loss (with a complexity tax, not a generalization estimate); every promotion decision must go through the external walk-forward harness (GN08-C1).

Do not run GP/SR against the drive simulator's play-by-play sequence data to 'discover' physics rules — the drive simulator's 6 known bugs (turnover field-position swap, half/full game-clock mismatch, inverted kneel rule, non-decrementing timeouts, flat 7-point HFA lump, missing halftime/OT) are conventional logic bugs that need conventional fixes, not a symbolic-regression replacement of correct, known football rules.

Do not treat a single GP/SR run's result as a finding — a default run evaluates 10,000-100,000+ candidate expressions against tables of a few hundred to a few thousand rows; report only multi-rerun, held-out-tested results (mirrors tonight's standing finding on the missing trial registry/multiplicity correction for the 21-model historical search).

Do not use symbolic regression to search directly over the game/team identity-matching problem (team-codes.js / nfl-contract-key.js) — that is a record-linkage/entity-resolution problem, not a curve-fitting one; a genetic-programming search there would optimize a proxy metric with no ground truth to check against.

Do not vendor or fork gplearn or PySR source into the Gridiron repo — both are pip-installable, actively maintained (PySR pushed 2026-09-11, gplearn 2026-08-14); install as dependencies and pin versions instead.

result.label: GN10: aging-curve / survival-analysis code for dynasty-age-curve.js
result.summary: Read server/services/dynasty-age-curve.js in full: it applies a single point-estimate multiplier from a hand-typed, linearly-interpolated literature table (4for4 2025 prose anchors) with zero standard error, zero sample size, zero per-player variation — every RB aged 29 gets the identical 0.90x regardless of career workload. Cloned and read three real repos (all unlicensed, so ideas/APIs are reusable but code is not redistributable): kellytodhunter/KBO-Player-Analysis (1 star, 2026-07-22) implements a genuine delta-method aging curve with a per-age-bin standard error computed from real consecutive-season deltas, playing-time-weighted, backtested 2021-2024 against naive baselines; kennethho193/nfl-aging-curve (0 stars, 2026-03-20) fits a statsmodels random-intercept mixed-effects quadratic curve on RB rushing yards and derives a correct delta-method 95% CI on the fitted population curve by propagating the fixed-effect covariance matrix, but never turns the random-intercept variance into a per-player band; sashaostr/sklearn-lifelines (29 stars but stale since 2019, code unrunnable as-is) is a thin sklearn wrapper around lifelines' CoxPHFitter/AalenAdditiveFitter that demonstrates the constructor/API shape but not lifelines' real survival-curve confidence intervals, which live in lifelines itself (MIT, actively maintained, explicitly in-scope per this task). No single repo is a complete answer; the recommended design combines the KBO delta-method SE, the mixed-effects population CI, and a lifelines Cox survival model (time-to-decline framing, right-censored at "still above threshold") for genuinely player-conditioned uncertainty bands — attached via a new research/aging_curve_*.py script (parallel to existing research/*.py labs) that exports a JSON curve+CI table for dynasty-age-curve.js to load in place of AGE_CURVE_ANCHORS.

repos.what_it_does: Marcel-style KBO hitter/pitcher projection pipeline: empirical-Bayes regression-to-the-mean with method-of-moments-tuned m, a delta-method aging curve (per-age mean delta AND standard error from real consecutive-season pairs, playing-time weighted), cumulative age-adjustment curve anchored at 27, and a genuine 2021-2024 backtest vs. prior-year-only and league-average baselines (verified by reading code/03_regression_mean.py, code/04_age_curves.py, code/06_validation.py).
repos.adoption_path: Reimplement the delta-method (not copy, no license): join Gridiron's nflverse birth-date table with its season-level fantasy-points table in a new research/aging_curve_delta_method.py, compute per-position/per-age mean delta + SE from real consecutive-season pairs weighted by playing time, export JSON for dynasty-age-curve.js.

repos.what_it_does: Fits statsmodels mixedlm('rushing_yards ~ age_c + age_c2', groups=player_id) — random player intercept + fixed quadratic age curve, addressing survivorship bias by letting each player's own intercept absorb baseline quality. Derives peak age from the quadratic vertex and builds a correct 95% CI on the fitted population curve by propagating the fixed-effect covariance matrix (result.cov_params()) through the quadratic — verified by extracting and reading notebooks/02_modeling.ipynb's code cells directly (README oversells it as 'end-to-end').
repos.adoption_path: Reimplement the mixed-effects quadratic + delta-method CI against Gridiron's own fantasy-points schema; pip install statsmodels into research/.venv (currently only has scipy/sklearn, confirmed by listing site-packages). Report the random-intercept variance separately as a distinct 'player-to-player spread' number, since this repo computes it but never surfaces it as a band.

repos.what_it_does: Two ~35-line sklearn BaseEstimator wrappers around lifelines.CoxPHFitter and lifelines.AalenAdditiveFitter for Pipeline/GridSearchCV compatibility. predict() calls only predict_expectation() (a point estimate); the alpha/CI machinery is passed through to the constructor but never exercised — verified by reading the entire 75-line estimators_wrappers.py, the whole package. Stale since 2019, likely broken against current lifelines.
repos.adoption_path: Do not run this wrapper (avoid — stale/unverified). Use it only to confirm the lifelines CoxPHFitter/AalenAdditiveFitter constructor contract (duration_col, event_col, alpha), then call the real, actively-maintained lifelines library (MIT) directly for a time-to-decline survival model: event = fantasy PPG permanently drops below a peak-relative threshold, censored = still above threshold as of latest season, covariates = position/draft capital/injury games/target share. lifelines' native predict_survival_function() carries real confidence bands, which is what actually delivers a player-conditioned uncertainty band.

candidates.candidate: Replace AGE_CURVE_ANCHORS literature table with an empirical delta-method curve (mean + SE per age bin) computed from Gridiron's own nflverse birth-date + season fantasy-points data
candidates.mechanism: For every player, compute delta = fantasy_PPG(season N+1) - fantasy_PPG(season N), group by age-at-season-N and position, weight by harmonic mean of playing-time (games/snaps) in the two seasons, take the weighted mean and se = std/sqrt(n) per age bin (min_n floor, e.g. 8, below which the bin returns null rather than a fabricated number). Cumulatively sum deltas anchored at a chosen prime age to rebuild the multiplier curve, replacing the current hand-typed interpolated table with one fit directly on Gridiron's own player population (all positions, not just RB/WR/TE — this also fixes QB getting a flat 1.0 'because no published curve exists').
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New research/aging_curve_delta_method.py (parallel to existing research/*.py labs) reads nflverse_player_positions (birth_date) joined to the season fantasy-points table already used elsewhere in server/services/, outputs data/aging_curve_deltas.json (age -> {mean, se, n} per position/stat). server/services/dynasty-age-curve.js loads this JSON in place of AGE_CURVE_ANCHORS; ageDecayMultiplier keeps its interpolation shape but interpolates the empirical curve instead of literature points, and dynastyAgeAdjustment() adds low/mid/high fields (multiplier ± 1.96*se) plus the backing n so thin-sample ages visibly widen instead of pretending equal confidence at every age.
candidates.expected_value: Turns a single hard-coded number per player into a curve with an honest, sample-size-aware uncertainty band, extends coverage to QB and any position with a literature gap, and lets consumers (trade calculators, roster valuation) show a range instead of false precision — directly serves fantasy-over-betting priority since dynasty values are a fantasy surface.
candidates.exit_test: Backtest the delta-method curve against the current literature-anchor curve on held-out season-pairs (e.g. predict N+1 fantasy PPG from N using each curve's adjustment) and require the delta-method curve's MAE/RMSE to be no worse — if it's meaningfully worse, don't ship it as a silent replacement, keep the literature anchors as the fallback for thin-sample age bins only.

candidates.candidate: Add a mixed-effects (random player intercept) quadratic population curve with a covariance-propagated 95% CI, run as a cross-check against the delta-method curve
candidates.mechanism: Fit statsmodels MixedLM(fantasy_PPG ~ age_c + age_c2, groups=player_id) per position on the same season-level data as GN10-1. The random player intercept absorbs each player's baseline quality so the fixed-effect quadratic isolates the population aging trend without survivorship bias (a rookie's bad first year doesn't get read as 'aging'). Build the fitted curve's 95% CI by propagating result.cov_params() through the quadratic (Var(Intercept) + age_c^2*Var(age_c) + age_c^4*Var(age_c2)), exactly the delta-method-on-fitted-parameters technique read in kennethho193/nfl-aging-curve's notebook cell 4 — and additionally report the random-intercept variance itself as a separate 'player-to-player spread' number, which that repo computes but never surfaces.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: pip install statsmodels into research/.venv (confirmed absent — only scipy/sklearn present today). Add research/aging_curve_mixed_effects.py producing data/aging_curve_population_ci.json (age -> {fitted, ci_low, ci_high, between_player_sd} per position). Exposed in dynasty-age-curve.js as a second, cross-checking curve — when it disagrees materially with the delta-method curve from GN10-1 at some age, that disagreement itself is useful signal (thin data, non-quadratic shape) worth surfacing rather than silently picking one.
candidates.expected_value: Gives a second, methodologically distinct curve fit (parametric quadratic + real covariance propagation, vs. GN10-1's nonparametric bin-by-bin empirical fit) — agreement between the two raises confidence in the shape; disagreement flags exactly where the literature-anchor approach was most guessing (e.g. past age 33, thin samples). Also separates 'how sure are we about the average trajectory' from 'how much do players vary at a given age', two numbers the current single-multiplier design conflates into one.
candidates.exit_test: Compare GN10-2's CI width and mean curve against GN10-1's empirical SE curve at each age; if the two disagree by more than one SE at ages with n>=20 in both, treat that age range as unresolved (flag it in the served data, don't silently average the two) rather than shipping a single blended number.

candidates.candidate: Add a player-conditioned survival model (lifelines CoxPHFitter) for time-to-decline, giving per-player predicted decline curves instead of one curve applied uniformly by position/age
candidates.mechanism: Define event = a player's trailing-N-game fantasy PPG permanently drops below a peak-relative threshold (e.g. 70% of that player's own career-peak rolling PPG); duration = seasons from career start to event; censored = still above threshold as of the most recent season (real right-censoring — most active players haven't declined yet, and averaging them in as 'no decline' the way a naive mean would is the same survivorship-bias problem the delta method exists to fix). Fit lifelines.CoxPHFitter with covariates: position, draft capital/round, career target or touch share, prior injury-games count, age at debut. lifelines' predict_survival_function() returns, per player, a full survival curve with proper (Kaplan-Meier-anchored) confidence bands — a genuinely player-specific uncertainty band, not a per-position/age lookup applied identically to every player who happens to share that age.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: pip install lifelines (MIT license, actively maintained — NOT the stale sklearn-lifelines wrapper, which is reference-only for its constructor shape) into research/.venv. New research/aging_curve_survival.py fits the Cox model on Gridiron's multi-season fantasy history, exports each active player's predicted survival curve (age -> P(still above 70%-of-peak)) to a JSON keyed by gsis_id. dynasty-age-curve.js's dynastyAgeAdjustment() gains an optional player-specific path: when a Cox-fitted curve exists for that gsis_id, use its band instead of falling back to the position-level curve from GN10-1/GN10-2, and always report which source was used (mirroring the existing age_source pattern already in playerRealAge()).
candidates.expected_value: The only one of the three designs that answers 'how sure are we about THIS player's decline,' not just 'how sure are we about the position's typical decline' — directly useful for dynasty trade decisions on specific, borderline players (a 29-year-old RB with heavy or light career workload) where the current position-flat multiplier is least trustworthy.
candidates.exit_test: Concordance index (lifelines' built-in c-index) on held-out players must beat 0.5 (better than random ranking) by a real margin, and the Cox model's per-player survival curves must be validated against actual observed declines/non-declines in a holdout cohort before this path is trusted over the simpler position-level curves — if concordance is weak, ship GN10-1/GN10-2 only and leave this as a documented, not-yet-validated extension.

candidates.candidate: Report curve source, sample size, and disagreement across methods in every dynastyAgeAdjustment() response instead of a single silent number
candidates.mechanism: Once GN10-1/GN10-2/GN10-3 exist as independent estimates, dynastyAgeAdjustment() should never collapse them into one opaque multiplier the way it does today (raw_value * multiplier). Return the full set: empirical delta-method mid/low/high + n (GN10-1), mixed-effects population CI + between-player SD (GN10-2), and — when available — the player-specific Cox survival curve position (GN10-3), tagged with which curve(s) backed the number, mirroring the existing { age, age_source } transparency pattern already in the file (playerRealAge already does exactly this kind of 'never hide which source was used' design — extend it to the curve choice itself).
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Extend the return shape of dynastyAgeAdjustment() in server/services/dynasty-age-curve.js: add curve_source, sample_n, ci_low, ci_high fields alongside the existing raw_value/multiplier/adjusted_value/source fields, following the file's own stated design principle in its header comment ('a consumer can always see both the raw market price and the age-adjusted one side by side') — extend that same transparency to uncertainty, not just to the raw-vs-adjusted split it already does.
candidates.expected_value: Cheapest of the four candidates and consistent with the file's own existing design philosophy (never hide the raw number, never silently default) — makes the other three candidates' outputs actually usable by trade-value UI instead of requiring a second lookup, and costs almost nothing once GN10-1 exists since it's just adding fields to an existing return object.
candidates.exit_test: Existing dynasty-age-curve.test.js must still pass unmodified against the current fields (additive change only, read-only verified: check the test file asserts on adjusted_value/multiplier by exact match, not by object shape, before ruling out breakage) — since this repo is read-only for this task, verifying non-breakage of the test file is a note for whoever implements this, not something this research task performed.

do_not_do: Do not pip-install or execute the sklearn-lifelines wrapper (sashaostr/sklearn-lifelines) — it is 7 years stale, unverified against current lifelines, and its own predict() only calls predict_expectation() anyway, so it adds no capability over calling lifelines directly.

Do not copy code verbatim from any of the three repos into Gridiron — all three declare no license (GitHub API license:null), so only ideas/method design/API shapes may be reimplemented from scratch, never the code itself.

Do not silently replace the literature-anchor curve with the empirical delta-method curve without backtesting both against held-out season-pairs first — the empirical curve trades a small, clean literature table for real data noise, and at thin-sample ages (very young/old, or QB where no anchor exists today) it could be worse, not better, until validated.

Do not collapse multiple curve estimates (delta-method, mixed-effects, survival) into one blended number — report disagreement between methods as signal, matching the existing file's principle of never hiding the raw number behind a single adjusted one.

Do not touch server/services/dynasty-age-curve.js, its test file, or any other file in fantasy-football-dashboard — this task is research/design only; the repo is read-only and a live server is capturing Week 1 games.

result.label: GN07-live-win-probability-code
result.summary: Read nflfastR's actual xgboost WP training/runtime code (MODELS.R, ep_wp_calculators.R, helper_add_ep_wp.R) plus two smaller open implementations (AndrewRook/NFLWin, topfunky/r-nfl-win-probability). Live in-game WP in the reference implementations is a direct regression on 11 game-state features (down/distance/yardline/score-diff/time/timeouts/home/spread, with two engineered decay terms and explicit monotone constraints) evaluated once per play — not a simulation of remaining plays — which structurally rules out the class of bug tonight's audit found in Gridiron's nfl-drive-sim.js (wrong-direction WP from inverted kneel logic, non-decrementing timeouts, home-spread used for the away team). Gridiron's own nfl_play_by_play table already has 8 of the 11 needed features under different names; it is missing timeouts-remaining entirely, which is the first concrete build step. MVP path: ship a plain logistic-regression live-WP model in pure JS first (no new runtime dependency), then upgrade to a monotone-constrained gradient-boosted model trained offline and evaluated via a small JS tree-walker, with a ported KDE-based calibration check (MIT-licensed, from NFLWin) as the honesty gate.

sources.title: nflfastR EP/WP model training script (MODELS.R)
sources.key_result: Live WP is two binary-logistic xgboost gbtree models (65 trees no-spread / 534 trees with spread) on 11-12 features with an explicit monotone_constraints vector forcing WP to move the correct direction with score differential, time-decayed spread, down, distance, yardline, and both teams' timeouts; trained on guga31bb/metrics cal_data.rds, qtr<=4 only (no OT rows).

sources.title: nflfastR EP/WP runtime calculators (ep_wp_calculators.R)
sources.key_result: calculate_win_probability() derives home/posteam_spread/elapsed_share/spread_time/Diff_Time_Ratio from raw pbp columns then does one stats::predict() matrix pass through the pretrained model — no live simulation of remaining plays, unlike Gridiron's drive-sim architecture.

sources.title: nflfastR feature/column ordering and derived-variable helpers (helper_add_ep_wp.R)
sources.key_result: wp_model_select/wp_spread_model_select pin exact feature order (receive_2h_ko, spread_time, home, half_seconds_remaining, game_seconds_remaining, Diff_Time_Ratio, score_differential, down, ydstogo, yardline_100, posteam_timeouts_remaining, defteam_timeouts_remaining); prepare_wp_data() shows the exact spread_time = posteam_spread*exp(-4*elapsed_share) decay formula.

sources.title: AndrewRook/NFLWin model.py
sources.key_result: MIT-licensed sklearn Pipeline (logistic regression + isotonic CalibratedClassifierCV) for live WP, plus a from-scratch Gaussian-KDE reliability-diagram calibration validator (max_deviation, residual_area) with zero external service dependency — directly reusable for Gridiron's 'no honest calibration anywhere' gap.

sources.title: topfunky/r-nfl-win-probability win-probability.R
sources.key_result: A single plain glm(poswins ~ qtr+down+ydstogo+game_seconds_remaining+yardline_100+score_differential+timeouts+is_home_team, binomial) tracks nflfastR's own wp curve closely on real games and includes a 5%-bin reliability plot vs actual win rate by quarter — proof a first-cut logistic model on features Gridiron already has is a viable fast MVP.

candidates.candidate: Ship a real live in-game win-probability model (nfl-live-wp.js) trained on Gridiron's own nfl_play_by_play, staged from a plain logistic regression to a monotone-constrained gradient-boosted model
candidates.mechanism: Stage 1: reimplement topfunky's glm feature set (qtr, down, ydstogo, game_seconds_remaining, yardline_100, score_differential, timeouts, is_home) as a JS sigmoid(dot(coefs,features)) fit offline once on Gridiron's 251,591 pbp rows joined to game outcomes -- zero new runtime dependency. Stage 2: once timeouts/receive_2h_ko exist (GN07-c4), retrain nflfastR's exact 11/12-feature architecture (decayed spread_time and Diff_Time_Ratio terms, monotone_constraints on score_differential/down/ydstogo/yardline/timeouts) offline in Python/R, export via dump_model to JSON, evaluate at runtime with a ~40-line JS tree-walker (sum leaf outputs across trees, sigmoid) -- no xgboost native binary in Node.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New file server/services/nfl-live-wp.js reading directly from nfl_play_by_play + game_lines (for spread_line); new offline training script (outside the live app, run against a DB snapshot, never touching the live-capture process per the read-only/no-disturb rule) producing server/data/models/live-wp-v1.json; expose as a new read-only endpoint alongside (not replacing) nfl-drive-sim.js's existing win-probability outputs so the two can be compared before any cutover.
candidates.expected_value: Replaces an ad hoc, bug-carrying drive simulation with a direct, monotonic regression on game state -- structurally immune to the wrong-direction-WP bug class tonight's audit found (inverted kneel rule, non-decrementing timeouts, home-spread used for away team), because it never simulates plays at all.
candidates.exit_test: On held-out 2024-2025 games, bin predicted WP into deciles and compare to actual win rate (reliability diagram): max |predicted-actual| must beat the same statistic computed from nfl-drive-sim.js's current WP output on the same held-out set, and Brier score must improve.

candidates.candidate: Port NFLWin's KDE-based reliability-diagram calibration harness as a reusable Gridiron audit tool
candidates.mechanism: Gaussian-kernel KDE (bandwidth=0.01) over predicted probabilities, separately for the positive and total populations, gives a smooth empirical win-rate-at-each-predicted-probability curve plus a max-deviation and integrated-residual-area summary statistic -- a complete calibration check requiring no external library beyond a weighted sum of exponentials.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New server/services/wp-calibration-harness.js (or a new audit type registered in audit-registry.js), ported from AndrewRook/NFLWin model.py:285-396 (MIT license, small enough to port near-verbatim in JS); write a unit test that runs it against a public nflverse-pbp sample's own wp column (known well-calibrated) as a sanity fixture before trusting it on any Gridiron-produced model.
candidates.expected_value: Gridiron currently has zero honest calibration checks anywhere in the pipeline per tonight's audit; this gives a cheap, reusable one that generalizes past WP to CLV and player-prop distributions.
candidates.exit_test: Harness run against the nflverse-pbp sample's published wp column reproduces a near-diagonal reliability curve (max_deviation < 0.05) -- proves the harness itself isn't buggy before it's used to judge any in-house model.

candidates.candidate: Pull nflverse-pbp historical play-by-play (CC-BY-4.0, includes nflfastR's own wp/vegas_wp/spread_line columns) as an external training-data supplement and ingestion benchmark
candidates.mechanism: nflverse-pbp publishes yearly play_by_play_<season> files (static URLs, no auth, no paid API) back to 1999 with every raw feature the WP model needs plus nflfastR's own already-computed wp column to compare against.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: New one-time script scripts/import-nflverse-pbp-benchmark.js loading selected seasons into a new read-only table nfl_pbp_benchmark (never touching the live-capture DB or process); used purely offline for (a) more training rows for GN07-c1's model than Gridiron's own 251,591, and (b) a play-level accuracy check on Gridiron's own ingestion.
candidates.expected_value: More and better-labeled training data than Gridiron has alone, plus a free correctness check on Gridiron's own play-by-play capture (down/distance/score/yardline agreement rate against an independently-recorded source).
candidates.exit_test: On the overlapping set of real plays present in both nfl_play_by_play and the imported benchmark for the same game/season/week, core fields (down, distance, yardline, home_score, away_score) must agree in >99% of rows; disagreements get filed as their own ingestion-accuracy finding.

candidates.candidate: Add posteam/defteam timeouts-remaining and receive_2h_ko tracking to nfl_play_by_play ingestion
candidates.mechanism: nflfastR's monotone constraints treat timeouts-remaining as one of the two features WP must move monotonically in the team's own favor for; NFLWin and topfunky's simpler models require it too. Gridiron's nfl_play_by_play schema (nfl-a-to-m.js:306-333) has no timeout columns at all today.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Extend the nfl_play_by_play ingestion pipeline to derive posteam_timeouts_remaining/defteam_timeouts_remaining from timeout events already implied by the raw feed (the existing text column, or a small new event parser), plus a receive_2h_ko flag set once per game at kickoff; add as new nullable columns via ALTER TABLE (matching the existing pattern already used for shotgun/no_huddle/pass_depth/pass_direction at nfl-a-to-m.js:579).
candidates.expected_value: Unblocks the full-featured live-WP model (GN07-c1 stage 2) and is a prerequisite for any monotone-constrained model at all; as a side benefit, gives Gridiron ground-truth timeout tracking it can later use to validate/fix nfl-drive-sim.js's separately-audited non-decrementing-timeout bug.
candidates.exit_test: Spot-check the new timeout columns against nflverse-pbp's own posteam_timeouts_remaining/defteam_timeouts_remaining for the same real games (via GN07-c3's benchmark table) and require exact agreement outside of known edge cases (overtime, two-minute-warning stoppages).

candidates.candidate: Add a live win-probability chart to Gridiron's dashboard, modeled on topfunky's WP-vs-time plot design
candidates.mechanism: Quarter gridlines, a 50% reference line, the live-WP curve over game_seconds_remaining, and scoring-event rug marks -- a visualization idea (not code, no license on the source repo) reproduced from scratch once GN07-c1 supplies real numbers to plot.
candidates.how_in_gridiron: Small addition to the existing Gridiron HQ dashboard (Nick's local fantasy app, light-theme per his UI preferences) once nfl-live-wp.js exists; pure frontend charting work, no new backend surface beyond what GN07-c1 already exposes.
candidates.expected_value: Cheap, high-visibility payoff that makes the new model's output legible and lets Nick eyeball-QA it against known comeback games immediately, rather than trusting it blind.
candidates.exit_test: Manually replay a known historical comeback game through the chart and confirm the WP curve shows the expected inflection point at the actual turning play.

do_not_do: Do not copy nflfastR's R source (MODELS.R, ep_wp_calculators.R, helper_add_ep_wp.R) verbatim into Gridiron -- the repo is NOASSERTION-licensed (no explicit redistribution/derivative rights); reimplement the public formulas and monotone-constraint list independently in JS instead.

Do not add a native xgboost binary/binding as a new Node runtime dependency -- no maintained, trustworthy JS xgboost binding was found in the search; export trained trees to JSON offline and walk them with a small JS evaluator, or use a pure logistic model.

Do not apply the trained WP model to overtime plays without a fallback -- nflfastR's own spread model excludes OT from training (qtr<=4 filter); silently extrapolating into OT will be uncalibrated exactly where drama (and correlated live-betting risk) is highest.

Do not touch, migrate, or run anything against the live fantasy-football-dashboard database or process -- all research and any prototype training/scripts must run against a separate snapshot or read-only copy, per the standing rule that a live server is capturing Week 1 games through Sunday.
Do not treat greerreNFL/nfelo as a source for live in-game WP -- it is a pregame Elo/power-rating system with no play-level surface; it answers a different (already partially covered) question.

repos.what_it_does: R package computing NFL EP/WP/CP for play-by-play data; data-raw/MODELS.R is the literal xgboost training script for two live-WP models (no-spread 65-tree, spread-adjusted 534-tree, both monotone-constrained), R/ep_wp_calculators.R is the runtime one-pass predict() entry point used by every downstream nflverse tool.
repos.adoption_path: Reimplement the 11-feature list, the spread_time/Diff_Time_Ratio decay formulas, and the monotone_constraints vector from scratch in JS/Python trained on Gridiron+nflverse-pbp data; do not copy the R source files given the NOASSERTION license.

repos.what_it_does: sklearn-pipeline live-WP model (logistic regression + isotonic calibration) on a simpler feature set (no timeouts, no spread); its validate_model() implements a from-scratch Gaussian-KDE reliability-diagram calibration check with max-deviation and integrated-residual-area statistics.
repos.adoption_path: Port the KDE calibration validator (model.py:285-396) to a new server/services/wp-calibration-harness.js; MIT license permits direct porting, and it needs no scikit-learn since a Gaussian KDE is a weighted sum of exponentials.

repos.what_it_does: A single-file experiment: fits a plain glm(binomial) live-WP model on 8 basic features and plots it against nflfastR's own wp curve per game, plus a 5%-bin reliability-vs-quarter calibration plot.
repos.adoption_path: Use as a validated fallback design (fastest possible MVP) if the full monotone-xgboost path is too slow to stand up this week; reimplement the glm feature list and calibration-plot idea from scratch (no license to copy from).

repos.what_it_does: Pregame Elo-style power-rating system (538 Elo + QB/rest/weather adjustments, market blending); no play-level or in-game win-probability surface anywhere in the package.
repos.adoption_path: Not applicable to live in-game WP; already covered separately by tonight's finding that nfelo-vs-Pinnacle-opener favorites is Gridiron's one working +CLV signal.

repos.what_it_does: Build pipeline publishing yearly NFL play-by-play files (1999-present) including nflfastR's own computed wp, vegas_wp, and spread_line columns per play, refreshed weekly during season.
repos.adoption_path: Download selected season files (static URLs, no auth, no paid API) into a new read-only nfl_pbp_benchmark table for offline training-data augmentation and an ingestion-accuracy check against Gridiron's own nfl_play_by_play.

scores.reason: Grep-confirmed: nfl-neural-replay.js:24-27 has its own local implied/noVig feeding home_market_probability at line 130, exact duplicate of the F03-fix-1 defect pattern; swap is a 4-line import change with clearly bounded blast radius since the module is explicitly non-authoritative.

nfl-devig.js confirmed to export only proportionalNoVig/shinNoVig (line 114/109/119) so a power method is a real gap, but do not let it become a default until F03-new-1's backtest runs — build the function and tests now, gate default-swap behind evidence.

Directly answers whether power beats Shin on Gridiron's own NFL closes rather than borrowing an unverified-for-NFL literature result; correct sequencing before F03-fix-3 is trusted, but 'days' of effort against a single-method question is only worth it once F03-fix-3 exists to compare against.

Real gap (one-sided quotes fall back to raw implied) but 'weak' evidence on how much this actually moves accuracy, and it's downstream of F03-fix-3/new-1 settling which devig method the overround correction should even use — sequence after those land.

Cheap (hours, migration-only) insurance against the exact silent-baseline-change failure mode F03-fix-1 already surfaced by accident; low cost and directly protects future CLV comparisons, worth doing regardless of which devig method wins the F03-new-1 bake-off.

Confirmed: forward-ledger.js and shadow-ledger.js both independently compute CLV inline with different column sets (shadow-ledger.js:71 lacks closing_spread that forward-ledger.js:141 has) exactly as claimed; a full consolidation into one canonical module is 'days' of high-value but high-blast-radius work touching live grading paths (nfl_bet_log, forward_picks, shadow_decisions) — worth doing but needs the grading-invariant regression check run first, not shipped straight to production.

Grep-confirmed DEFAULT_CLOSING_BOOKS=null at nfl-execution-clv.js:59 feeding latestPerBook (lines 147-150) with no execution-book exclusion; this is a mechanical, hours-scale, high-confidence bias fix to a metric that (per governance) gates live decisions, exactly the kind of surgical fix that should ship now rather than wait for the larger F1 consolidation.

Directly confirmed by grep: shadow-ledger.js:71 SELECTs only spread,total (no closing_spread) and grades against it at lines 84-91, while forward-ledger.js:141/154 already does the correct closing_spread ?? spread fallback right next to it in the same codebase — this is a live, currently-active grading-correctness bug with an hours-scale, copy-the-adjacent-pattern fix; should ship immediately, independent of the larger CLV unification effort.

nfl-ensemble.js confirmed to exist with a market_residual blend path, but adding a decorrelation-aware objective is a multi-day research change to the core betting model when Nick's stated priority is fantasy-over-betting and betting only through governance gates — reasonable observability-only first step, but not urgent against that priority ordering.

Materially the same work as F03-new-1 (devig bake-off vs realized outcomes) described from a different angle; should be merged with F03-new-1 rather than run as a separate days-scale project, so on its own it's redundant effort rather than new value.

Real and well-motivated (protects the load-bearing 21-model/0-clear-materiality-gate number) but 'days' of statistical-methodology work competing with hours-scale live-bug fixes (F04-F2/F3) tonight; sequence after the cheap CLV correctness fixes ship, not before.

Grep-confirmed exactly as described: book-feeds.js:390 computes `at` post-Promise.all but line 417 passes it only as requestedAt (never receivedAt); migration 032 already exists so the columns are ready and unused for this live feed (the only one running since paid Odds API credits are gone) — a ~4-line, hours-scale fix with immediate real-world benefit tonight.

Plausible extension of the same defect into nfl-quote-tape.js's unwrap(), but this function currently has zero callers per the candidate's own exit criteria — a multi-day schema+migration change to harden a code path nothing uses yet should wait until quoteSurface/closingQuotes/bestExecutableQuote are actually wired to a caller.

Real but explicitly 'understates freshness (safe direction) rather than creating a look-ahead' per the candidate's own mechanism — a precision tightening, not a correctness bug, so it should wait behind F05-F1 which fixes an actual bias.

Cheap (hours) guardrail against the exact class of silent-defaulting bug F05-F1 exists because of; ingestQuoteSnapshot's receivedAt=null default confirmed structurally risky since nothing currently prevents a future call site from repeating the same mistake — good insurance to pair with the F05-F1 fix in the same PR.
Grep-verified turnover field-position bug with exact line numbers and an hours-scale fix that removes a systematic bias in every simulated possession change.
Concrete half-vs-full-game clock unit mismatch, hours to fix, and it currently miscalibrates roughly a quarter of all simulated game-time toward false urgency.
Inverted kneel logic plus timeouts that never decrement is credibly the single highest-value bug in the set since it structurally breaks every simulated endgame, worth the days-scale cost.

Fixes away-team WP reference frame (half of all possessions), a discrete 7-point HFA artifact at key betting numbers, and gives the season-remainder path real halftime/OT handling for live in-week resimulation.

A genuinely novel, non-self-referential audit that finally puts the underused 251,591-row play-by-play table to work and becomes a standing regression test catching future state-encoding bugs automatically.
A second independent audit method is useful but largely redundant with N1's purpose at similar days-scale cost, so validate N1's findings first before building a third cross-check.
Own EV note calls this only marginal on top of the F4(b) continuous-HFA fix, at weeks-scale cost, and it is a betting-model refinement when fantasy edge is the stated priority.
Explicitly weak evidence, days-scale cost for what is mainly a Monte-Carlo trial-count sanity check, and it is a third overlapping audit method alongside N1/N2 on the same epFor() surface.
Directly attacks the -2.28 CLV / 78%-adverse-move finding by replacing the mechanically-shrinking per-model regression average with one honest jointly-fit stacking optimization.

Replaces an uncorrected single-split t-test with the textbook Giacomini-White/DM standard plus Holm correction, fixing the same ad hoc-significance root cause behind five disagreeing CLV implementations.
Cheapest fix in the set: the equal-weight and inverse-MSE code paths already exist, this only wires up the comparison that has never been run against the naive-shrinkage default.

A strong idea that converges the ensemble fix and the missing-calibrated-uncertainty gap at once, but weeks of cost and a dependency on F02-fix-1's LOO machinery argue for prototyping before committing.
Valuable regime-decay monitoring but depends on F02-fix-2's GW implementation landing first and is weeks-scale, so it is a natural next step rather than a tonight priority.
Cheap-ish (days) dimensionality reduction that would make F02-fix-1's stacking QP more stable, but moderate evidence and dependency ordering argue for validating after fix-1 exists.

Grep-verified: the totals governance gate still reimplements a naive proportional devig instead of importing the already-built shinNoVig, an hours-scale fix that removes a live silent double standard between two staking gates.

Grep-verified in nfl-drive-sim.js:345-346 (and reused unflipped at :536/:825) — every simulated turnover hands the new offense the old team's field position, a systematic bias in every possession change; hours to fix with a trivial unit-test exit criterion.

Confirmed HALF=1800 clock but urgency formulas divide by 3600 (nfl-sim-policy.js:214,415), mis-calibrating roughly the first quarter of every half toward false late-game desperation; a one-line denominator fix with a clean assertion test.

The kneel/timeout defect (inverted kneelable threshold, single-call clock burn, discarded timeoutPolicy result) means timeouts never decrement, so leading teams get a free clock-kill every game — this is the highest-leverage fix in the batch since it corrupts every end-of-half/end-of-game win-probability decision downstream, not an edge case.

Bundles three verified defects (away-team WP uses home-frame spread, a discrete 7-pt HFA lump distorting key numbers, and a season-remainder loop with no halftime/OT) that together corrupt roughly half of all possession-level decisions and any live in-week resimulation of the games this server is currently capturing — worth the days of work but should ship as three separately-tested sub-fixes given the surface area.

nflWAR's multinomial-logit EP method is a single peer-reviewed paper (not replicated), but fitting it on Gridiron's own 251k-row play-by-play gives the drive simulator its first non-self-referential regression test, cheaply reused after every future nfl-drive-sim.js change — run once now as the pre-fix baseline, then again after F1-F4 land.
A useful second, functional-form-free cross-check (NFLSimulatoR-style resampling) but materially redundant with N1's real-data audit; do only if N1 surfaces a disagreement N1 alone can't resolve.

Per-team decaying HFA is a real but marginal refinement on top of F4(b)'s already-continuous HFA nudge, needs multiple seasons of home-margin history to fit reliably, and weeks of cost for a second-order betting-model improvement is hard to justify given fantasy-first priority.

The candidate's own evidence rating is weak and its stated best use is only as a convergence check on epFor()'s Monte-Carlo trial count — cheaper to just raise the trials count directly than to build a separate closed-form Markov solver for this.

Directly attacks the diagnosed root cause (averaging 31 single-covariate regressions instead of jointly fitting) of the confirmed 0.68+0.632·market shrinkage and -2.28 CLV finding, using textbook constrained-least-squares stacking (Yao et al.) — ship only if it beats the current blend on the same GW test (F02-fix-2), which is the correct honest gate.

Replaces an uncorrected, single-split, unconditional t-test (nfl-ensemble.js:1185-1188) with the peer-reviewed Giacomini-White conditional predictive-ability test plus Holm correction across 31 simultaneously-tested models — this is the shared root fix behind the five disagreeing CLV implementations and should gate every other ensemble change, including F02-fix-1.

The equal-weight and inverse-MSE weighting code paths already exist in nfl-ensemble.js (lines 1167-1168) but are never compared or promoted — wiring this up is hours of work with a well-replicated literature result (Claeskens et al. 2016, Smith & Wallis 2009) predicting equal-weight likely wins against 31 collinear inputs; essentially free to check before trusting any more complex blend.

Yao/Vehtari/Simpson/Gelman's log-score Bayesian stacking is the principled way to get an honestly-combined predictive SD (feeding both the ensemble and the props module), but it's weeks of work that should follow F02-fix-1/2 landing, not precede them.

A standing conditional-decay monitor is the right long-term risk-management layer once F02-fix-2's GW test exists, but as a new weekly job with no separate literature backing beyond GW itself, it's weeks of build for a monitoring capability that should wait until the underlying gate (F02-fix-2) is live.

Clustering the 31 correlated models before the F02-fix-1 stacking QP is cheap conditioning insurance and answers 'how many real signals exist' honestly, but should be validated as a preprocessing step within F02-fix-1's own exit test rather than built as a standalone deliverable.

Grep-confirmed: nfl-cover-calibration.js imports the real shinNoVig from nfl-devig.js while nfl-total-calibration.js:37 reimplements a naive proportional-split noVig locally — the spread and totals governance gates are silently using two different definitions of 'the market' for the same devig problem; an hours-scale import swap with a version bump fixes a live inconsistency in an active betting gate.

Grep-verified one-line import swap makes the neural-head audit consistent with every other model-vs-market comparison, but the module explicitly never gates live staking so the ceiling on impact is low.

Adds the literature's stronger devig candidate (power) as a non-default sibling method at low risk, completing the comparison nfl-devig.js's own docstring implies but doesn't yet run, without touching production behavior.

The only proposal that settles power-vs-Shin with Gridiron's own historical NFL closes and scores instead of borrowed literature authority, and it doubles as the pipeline's first real calibration validation, a capability flagged absent everywhere.
Speculative single-sided-vig correction on weak evidence with no data yet showing the gap is material; sequence it after F03-new-1's backtest infrastructure exists to reuse.
Cheap, migration-only provenance tagging that closes exactly the silent-baseline-drift risk this research session stumbled into by accident tonight.

Directly resolves the flagged five-disagreeing-CLV-implementations defect via a consolidation pattern (nfl-devig.js) already proven to work in this exact codebase, reducing duplication rather than adding it.
Confirmed live bug (DEFAULT_CLOSING_BOOKS=null lets the execution book leak into its own reference close) mechanically biases CLV toward zero exactly when it matters; hours-cost, high-confidence fix.

Confirmed live bug: shadow-ledger.js's SELECT omits closing_spread and grades against the mutable game_lines.spread column that forward-ledger.js's own comment already flags as unsafe — cheap, concrete, high-confidence fix.

Targets the single most consequential flagged defect (the ensemble's shrinkage-to-market blend) with real decorrelation theory, but the cited result is soccer-only and unproven for NFL spreads, so it belongs as an observability metric that must clear its own backtest before touching any live blend weight.

Substantially duplicates F03-new-1's own devig backtest and additionally proposes an 'additive' method that F03's research already shows is mathematically identical to Shin on every two-outcome Gridiron market — redundant machinery, not a second capability.

Directly protects the one number Nick already treats as load-bearing (the 21-model, zero-materiality-gate result) from being silently re-litigated by an overfit 22nd model; a genuinely absent capability.

Confirmed, grep-verified defect actively discarding the only currently-running live quote feed's evidence eligibility right now (permanently stamped legacy_request_time_only); a ~4-line fix with no schema change needed.

Real latent gap in unwrap()'s per-row clock, but those three query functions currently have zero callers anywhere in the repo, so it's worth doing before anything wires up point-in-time execution analysis rather than tonight.
Only understates freshness for fast providers (the safe direction), not a correctness bug, so it's lower priority than the other three F05 fixes.
Cheap regression guardrail against the exact silent-default-to-legacy-clock failure mode that produced F05-F1's live bug, at hours of cost.

Verified in code: turnover paths set endYard in the pre-turnover offense's frame and both possession-change sites (nfl-drive-sim.js:536,825) consume d.endYard directly as the new offense's yard with no flip; cheap, mechanical, high-leverage fix touching every simulated possession change.

Verified exactly: urgency=clamp(1-secondsLeft/3600) at nfl-sim-policy.js:214,415 while secondsLeft is capped at HALF=1800 everywhere it's produced, so every half opens with urgency=0.5 instead of 0; a one-line denominator fix with broad, easily-testable impact.

Verified: kneelable=40+timeouts*40 increases with opponent timeouts (backwards — more opponent timeouts should shrink the safe-kneel window since timeouts stop the kneel-down clock runoff), and the computed `to` timeoutPolicy result at nfl-drive-sim.js:475 is never applied back to the timeouts object, which is hard-reset to 3/3 every half; this is the single most structurally important bug in the set (kills all clock-management realism) but the 3-part fix is genuinely multi-day work with real risk of new edge cases (2-minute warning interaction, OT), hence cost=days not hours.

Sub-claims (a) and (c) are plausible and consistent with confirmed sibling bugs (I did not independently trace every liveWinProbability call site's sign convention or fully diff simulateGame vs the season-remainder loop), and (b)'s discrete 7-pt HFA coin-flip is a real, checkable pattern of exactly this codebase's style; ship (a)+(c) as a fix but verify the reference-frame direction with the stated mirror-symmetry unit test before merging since a sign error fixed wrong would silently flip every away-team decision the other way.

The 251,591-row play-by-play table's existence is corroborated by the standing research brief and its 'never used for sequence/classifier work' framing is consistent with F1-F3 confirming the simulator is purely self-generated/self-consistent; a real value-add as a regression harness, but nflWAR-grade multinomial logistic replication with proper CV is genuine multi-day effort before it pays for itself — worth a scoped spike first to confirm the play-by-play table has the needed columns (down/distance/yardline/half-seconds) before committing full effort.

Sound methodologically as an independent cross-check, but resampling-based simulators need dense (down,distance,yardline) coverage per bucket to avoid the paper's own sparse-cell fallback dominating the result, and Gridiron's real play-by-play volume/coverage at fine-grained buckets is unverified; lower priority than N1 since it duplicates much of N1's value with weaker guarantees and no confirmed data-density check.

A per-team Elo-style HFA layered on top of F4(b)'s not-yet-shipped continuous HFA fix is a legitimate but marginal refinement; explicitly flagged by its own author as depending on unverified third-party HFA benchmarks and overlapping with a separately-owned team-strength workstream — not worth building before the underlying continuous-HFA fix (F4b) even exists.

Author's own evidence rating is weak and the mechanism concedes it mainly just checks epFor()'s Monte Carlo trial count (200) rather than testing anything F1-F4 actually broke; a closed-form Markov chain over a hand-coarsened state space is real effort for a narrow, low-confidence payoff when N1 already gives a stronger real-data ground truth.

Directly targets the verified forecast=0.68+0.632*market shrinkage finding with a textbook Yao-et-al stacking-of-means fix reusing the existing weekly train/score split machinery in nfl-ensemble.js; genuinely valuable but a QP-based joint refit is real days-scale work, and per its own exit criterion should only ship if it beats the current blend on out-of-sample CLV/RMSE — build the refit and gate on that comparison rather than assuming it wins.

Replaces an admittedly ad hoc, uncorrected single-split t-stat gate (nfl-ensemble.js:1185-1188) with a standard Giacomini-White/DM-with-Holm-correction test; well-specified, reuses existing test scaffolding (nfl-ensemble-authority.test.js), and fixes a real multiple-testing problem (~1.5 false positives expected among 31 models at alpha=0.05) independent of whether F02-fix-1 ships.

Cheapest item in the set: weighting='equal' and 'inverse_mse' code paths already exist in nfl-ensemble.js (lines 1167-1168) per the candidate's own citation and are simply never compared against the production 'exponential' default in nfl-forecast-identity.js — wiring up the comparison and a promotion gate is hours of work with a well-established literature prior (equal-weight combinations are notoriously hard to beat) that could immediately de-risk the ensemble.
